findings.session_b_note:
The verse evidence names explicit exclusions:

**Moral incompatibility:** 2Cor 6:14 uses four rhetorical pairs — righteousness/lawlessness, light/darkness, Christ/Belial, believer/unbeliever — to name what genuine fellowship excludes. The exclusion is not merely behavioural but ontological: these realities cannot share common ground.

**Idolatrous joining:** Group 7565-001 (Hos 4:17) presents joining to idols as the wrong direction of the joining capacity — fellowship resists misdirected joining by the moral logic embedded in the fear-of-God companionship standard (Psa 119:63).

**Occult practice:** Groups 7565-002 (Psa 58:5) and 7569-001 (Psa 58:5) place the chavar and chever terms in occult charming contexts — the programme has classified these as inner spiritual misdirection. Fellowship as genuine shared life resists spiritual power-seeking through occult means.

**Faithlessness in covenant:** Mal 2:14 — fellowship resists the disposition of faithlessness toward the covenant companion.

findings.session_b_note: Goodness explicitly excludes: (1) Self-direction as the governing principle — Isa 65:2 names "following their own devices" as the way that is not good. Goodness resists the self as its own standard. (2) Wilful resistance to the revealed good — Jer 6:16 names refusal of "the good way" as the inner posture goodness cannot coexist with. (3) Moral self-justification that redefines the good — Jer 44:17 / Mal 2:17. (4) Departure from faith/trust relationship with God — Rom 11:22 names departure from chrēstotēs as the condition in which it is withheld. These exclusions are not merely behaviours but inner orientations. Goodness is structurally incompatible with self-sovereignty, wilful resistance, moral inversion, and relational departure from God. (OBS-067-OBS-021, OBS-067-OBS-028)

findings.session_b_note: 1Cor 13:4-7 provides the programme's most explicit catalogue of what love excludes: envy, boasting, arrogance, rudeness, self-seeking, irritability, resentfulness, rejoicing in wrongdoing (OBS-103-127). The list names love's resistances across moral, relational, and emotional registers. At the structural level, love resists division of ultimate allegiance (Jam 4:4 — cannot love God and world simultaneously, OBS-103-058), resists self-assertion as the primary orientation (love-of-self as the first item in the last-days catalogue, OBS-103-137), and resists the withholding of self (Joh 15:13 — love's maximum is the giving of the soul/life, OBS-103-125). Love also explicitly resists concealment of inner truth from the beloved: Lev 19:17 contrasts hate-as-silence with love-as-frank-correction (OBS-103-114).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-001: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanch…
findings.finding_value: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved), condition of its object (eleeinos — the pitiable state that calls compassion forth), and externalised act (almsgiving, mercy-act). No other characteristic in the programme review set operates across all four kinds simultaneously. The four root families (RACHAM, CHASAD, SPLANCHN, OIKTIROM) identify four constituent dimensions of the single characteristic, each naming a distinct register — somatic-maternal, covenantal-relational, visceral-immediate, and deliberative-pitying respectively. The structural opposites are two distinct kinds: willed judicial hardness (the hardened heart that refuses compassion) and unwilled prosperity-blindness (Eze 16:49 — the one who does not see the need because they are satiated). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed by the consistent outward-facing structure: compassion cannot exist without a suffering other. The definitional tier's most critical gap — the receiver's inner-being experience — is entirely absent from the data, affecting T1.5, T1.6, and T1.7 throughout. This gap is the single most significant analytical absence in the registry.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-010: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of coven…
findings.finding_value: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) evidenced in T4 is the relational expression of T1's boundary-definition: compassion ends where the condition (pitiable need) is absent, not where covenantal membership ends. T1's four modes of operation (T1.4) — intra-covenantal, cross-boundary, anticipatory, Christological — map onto T4's chesed/splanchnizō distinction (within-bond sustaining vs across-distance extending) and the scope analysis (covenantal and transcovenantal registers). Definition and relational scope are structurally co-determining.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-012: T1's primary dimension (Relational Disposition) and T6's co-occurrence landscape are mutually confirming. The love co-occurrence dominance (196 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T1's relation…
findings.finding_value: T1's primary dimension (Relational Disposition) and T6's co-occurrence landscape are mutually confirming. The love co-occurrence dominance (196 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T1's relational-disposition classification: love and compassion co-occur at this extraordinary rate because they share the relational-disposition register. T1's finding that compassion is constitutively outward-facing explains why the co-occurrence landscape shows the C17 cluster (love, mercy, kindness) as the primary co-occurrence family. T6's unresolved compassion/mercy distinction (SD-009) is the most critical consequence of T1's definitional incompleteness — the boundary between compassion and mercy as adjacent Relational Disposition characteristics is the definitional question T1 cannot answer without T6 data.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-001: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition of being in favour — charis as inhabited state), enabling capacity (the specific power given for specific tasks — 2Cor 12:9), and character quality (gracious speech, gracious conduct — chen in 889-003). No single English equivalent captures all four. The four modes of operation (sovereign bestowal, covenantal-relational sustaining, capacity-conferring, character-forming) correspond to the four kinds without collapsing them. Two structural opposites are identified: pride (the self-elevation that refuses the favour of the greater, active and willed) and ingratitude/gracelessness (acharistos — the failure to register and respond to grace received, which T3 confirms as image-impairment). The immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response before positive states settle) is a T1.5 finding confirming that grace does not bypass creaturely recognition but requires and produces it as a transitional state. The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed throughout: grace is constitutively directional — it flows from the greater to the lesser and requires the receptor's inner-being engagement to complete its operation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-010: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-su…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-sustaining mode corresponds to the relational scope (T4.5 — grace operating within and across covenantal boundaries). The capacity-conferring mode corresponds to the human-to-God direction in its supplication register (T4.2 — SD026: grace giving even the capacity to appeal). The character-forming mode corresponds to the human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious conduct and speech as the horizontal expression of received grace-character). The vocabulary's structural insight (T4 synthesis: giving-side and receiving-side built from the same root, chen/tachanum) explains T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner engagement to complete its operation — the vocabulary encodes the two-sidedness because grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-012: T1's dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) and T6's co-occurrence pattern are mutually confirming. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is the co-occurrence ex…
findings.finding_value: T1's dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) and T6's co-occurrence pattern are mutually confirming. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner posture of appeal: seeking is the relational posture before grace arrives, and the vocabulary encodes this (tachanum — built into the same root as chen). T6's structural uniqueness finding (grace is not produced by any other characteristic) is T1's definitional consequence: because grace is constitutively the uncaused inclination of the greater toward the lesser, it cannot be produced by anything in the lesser's constitutional system. T1's definition predicts T6's structural uniqueness.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Partiality, injustice, and inconsistency. "He does no injustice" (Zep 3:5); "there is no a.val in him" (Deu 32:4). It resists the accommodation of the guilty without ground — which is why the cross is necessary: "that he might be just and the justifier" (Rom 3:26).

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Distortion and counterfeit (M26-A2-003), the toleration of wickedness, the absence of orientation toward God (A2-004), and the forfeiting of the state through turning to injustice (A2-002). It resists the claim that righteousness can be transferred from one person to another independent of their own inner state (Eze 18:20).

The resistance to self-generated righteousness is more than exclusion — it extends to active contamination. The verse evidence establishes that the attempt to produce righteousness without the God-relation does not merely fail to produce the real thing; it produces something that looks like righteousness but is actively defiled. Isa 64:6 — "all our righteous deeds are like a polluted garment" — names human righteous acts as contaminated in the absence of the God-relation; the garment is worn and visible as something, but what it actually is is unclean. Deu 9:4–6 — "not because of your righteousness... the Lord explicitly denies that Israel's righteousness is the operative cause" — identifies the self-attributed righteousness as real enough to be disclaimed, but as having no independent causal power before God. Luk 18:9 names the inner consequence of self-generated righteousness: the person who "trusts in themselves that they were righteous" develops contempt for others — the counterfeit state produces a specific and destructive inner orientation. Mat 23:28 closes the picture: the outward appearance of righteousness masks "hypocrisy and lawlessness" within. These five passages together reveal that self-generated righteousness is not a partial achievement but a self-deceiving distortion that produces specific negative inner consequences: contamination (Isa 64:6), ineffectiveness before God (Deu 9:4–6), contempt (Luk 18:9), and inner lawlessness (Mat 23:28). Human righteousness excludes and actively resists the self-generated form.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Crookedness, deviousness, smooth-talking falsehood (Isa 30:10: the refusal to hear what is right and the demand for smooth things, VSG 1214-001). It resists the accommodation of false appearances.

**[C — Justification]** Self-justification — "you who would be justified by the law; you have fallen away from grace" (Gal 5:4). It resists the claim that human moral performance can achieve the standing that only God can confer.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Personal, autonomous vengeance (Rom 12:19: "never avenge yourselves"). It resists the impulse to take retribution into one's own hands outside the limits of delegated commission.

**[E — Condemnation]** Hypocritical judgment — "you condemn yourself, because you, the judge, practice the very same things" (Rom 2:1, VSG 4846-002). It resists the pretence of moral superiority in the one who passes verdict while sharing the same fault.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Prejudiced, partial, or faithless assessment. Adiakritos (impartial, VSG in sub-group) names the quality of assessment that is "without partiality and without hypocrisy" (Jam 3:17). The reckoning faculty resists conclusions not grounded in truth and faith.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** By definition, G is excluded from A2 and resists A1. Wickedness excludes standing before God (Psa 1:5), excludes the community of the righteous, and resists the standard of divine righteousness.

**[CLUSTER]** The cluster collectively excludes: self-generated righteousness (resisted by C), autonomous retribution (resisted by D), hypocritical judgment (resisted by E), corrupt assessment (resisted by F), and the whole domain of wickedness and injustice (named by G).

findings.finding_value: Constitutional in its primary form, with functional expressions. The divine grace-character (2330-001 — chan.nun) and the established sphere of grace (888-002 — Rom 5:2; 1Cor 15:10) are constitutional — stable and identity-forming. The acts of blessing (1299-001), grace-giving (5470-001), and forgiving (5470-002) are functional expressions of the constitutional disposition. The completed-standing form (5471-001 — charitoō) is constitutional: a permanent alteration of relational status.

findings.finding_value: M01-A explicitly excludes: (1) pride and self-reliance (Pro 3:7: fear-of-God is "set against self-reliant pride"); (2) exploitation of the vulnerable (Lev 25:43: fear of God "prohibits ruthless domination"); (3) misplaced reverence toward false gods (2Ki 17 corpus; Judg 6:10); (4) moral blindness (Psa 36:1: absence of fear allows transgression to speak freely). It also excludes the panic-fear that would disable action (Deu 20:3: "soldier commanded not to let fear grip them before battle" — reverential fear of God displaces the panic-fear of human enemies).

M01-B in its commanded-release form (B-VCG-06) explicitly resists the paralysis and flight that un-countered acute fear would produce. The "do not fear" corpus (Isa 43:1 anchor through the full corpus) shows the characteristic being contested and resisted.
M01-D's commanded-against form (D-VCG-04, Jer 1:17 anchor) explicitly excludes prophetic and pastoral capitulation — dismay "must not grip" the prophet because it produces paralysis before opponents.
M01-F, in its covenantal-curse form (Deu 28:66-67 anchor), excludes rest and settled trust — it is the experience of having no secure inner resting point.
M01-G explicitly excludes faithful stewardship (Mat 25:25: timidity produces burying rather than investing) and honest witness (Rev 21:8: cowardice in the context of apostasy under pressure).

Across M01, the characteristic in its ordered forms excludes: self-reliance, exploitation, moral blindness, and misplaced reverence. In its disordered or acute forms, fear excludes: rest, trust, courageous action, and faithful witness. The ordered fear (M01-A) and the disordered fear (M01-B excessive; M01-F, G) exclude different things — this asymmetry is a structural finding.

Wrath excludes mercy: Eze 8:18 (M02-B-VCG-06) states that God acts in rage without pity or hearing — the inner wrath shuts off compassion and responsiveness. Divine wrath in its full expression excludes the relational softness of mercy.
Jam 1:20 (M02-A-VCG-04) states that human wrath "does not produce God's righteousness" — it explicitly excludes the righteous outcome it imagines it is serving.
Eph 4:26 (M02-C-VCG-02) and Eph 4:31 (M02-A-VCG-04) show anger in its entrenched form excluding the Spirit's presence and the relational health of the community.
Strife explicitly excludes the community of the Spirit: Gal 5:20 (M02-F-VCG-01) lists it as a work of the flesh; 1Ti 2:8 (M02-A-VCG-04) names anger as incompatible with holy prayer.

The characteristic, in its disordered form, excludes mercy, effective righteous action, the Spirit's community, genuine prayer, and restored relationship. In its ordered form (righteous anger), it excludes indifference to moral violation.

Grief resists and excludes: comfort (Rachel refusing comfort, Jer 31:15 — M03-A-VCG-01; Jerusalem's lovers offering no comfort, Lam 1:2 — M03-A-VCG-01); rest (sighing has replaced bread, Job 3:24 — M03-E-VCG-03; grief preventing rest, Jer 45:3 — M03-E-VCG-03); rejoicing (sorrow coexisting with joy but not yielding to it in C-VCG-01; godly grief displacing levity in M03-B-VCG-04; mourning commanded as the appropriate inner state displacing laughter, Jam 4:9); and eating/normal bodily function (Hannah's grief so consuming she cannot eat, 1Sa 1:7-8 — M03-A-VCG-01; sighing replacing bread, Job 3:24). Grief also resists the superficiality that refuses to mourn when mourning is appropriate — the Corinthians' arrogance where mourning was fitting is named as a deficiency (1Cor 5:2 — M03-B-VCG-04).

**[Folded from wa_session_b_findings.id=73; finding_id=DIM-13-001; registry=bitterness]**
Bitterness in Reg 13 operates in two structural registers: (a) affective quality — bitter grief, anguish, affliction (something that happens to the inner person), and (b) dispositional-character state — root of bitterness, bitter jealousy as heart-state, bitter rebellion (something the inner person becomes). Session B should examine whether biblical bitterness is primarily an experience or a condition, and whether the two registers are sequential or independent.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Exultation excludes: (1) **self-directed triumph** — nowhere in M04-A-VCG-01 does exultation produce pride directed at the self; the consistently named object is God, his salvation, his name; (2) **enemy-triumph over the righteous** — Psa 13:4 expresses the psalmist's prayer that his enemy should not rejoice over his defeat; (3) **rejoicing at another's fall** — Pro 24:17 explicitly prohibits the heart's gladness over an enemy's stumbling; (4) **hollow joy on false grounds** — Hos 9:1 prohibits Israel's rejoicing because it is built on unfaithfulness; (5) **premature joy in the face of judgment** — Eze 21:10 ("shall we rejoice?") exposes the impossibility of exultation under the sword.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Joy explicitly excludes or resists: (1) **Rejoicing at evil** — 1Cor 13:6 ("love does not rejoice at wrongdoing"); Pro 24:17 ("do not rejoice when your enemy falls"); Job 31:29 (Job denying he rejoiced at enemy's ruin); (2) **Hollow festivity without covenant ground** — Isa 22:13 ("let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die" — reckless joy-without-substance condemned); Ecc 2:1–2 (pleasure tested and found vain); (3) **Illegitimate joy** — Hos 9:1 ("rejoice not, O Israel, for you have played the whore"); (4) **Premature joy** — Isa 14:29 (Philistia warned not to rejoice at the broken rod); (5) **Self-focused delight** — Luk 10:20 (Jesus redirecting joy from power over spirits to the deeper ground of names written in heaven); (6) **Shallow surface-level joy** — Mat 13:20; Mar 4:16; Luk 8:13 (rocky-ground hearer receives word with joy but lacks root). Joy resists being rooted in wrong objects, shallow grounds, or morally corrupted directions.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Suffering-Joy explicitly excludes: (1) **Performed or hollow cheerfulness** — M04-F makes clear that ba.lag is not easy or automatic; Job 9:27's attempted cheerfulness immediately collapses — the characteristic is not a performance of happiness; (2) **Joy based on wrong grounds** — Joh 5:35 ("you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light") — the crowds' transient agalliao in John's light was real but shallowly grounded and did not endure; Suffering-Joy resists joy that lacks the depth to hold through difficulty; (3) **Denial of suffering** — 1Pe 1:6 ("though now for a little while, if necessary, you have been grieved") explicitly acknowledges the grief alongside the rejoicing; Suffering-Joy does not pretend suffering away; (4) **World-aligned rejoicing** — Rev 11:10 (earth-dwellers rejoicing over the prophets' deaths) — this is joy rooted in opposition to the gospel, not in participation in it.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gladness explicitly excludes: (1) **False evaluation** — Num 14:3 (preferring Egypt as better is fear-distorted evaluation, not true gladness); Jer 44:17 (misattributing former wellbeing to idol-worship); Isa 41:7 (the craftsman's self-congratulatory "it is good" over an idol) — Gladness resists evaluation that is not grounded in reality; (2) **Self-righteous entitlement** — Deu 9:6 ("not because of your righteousness") directly corrects the inner assumption that the good land was merited; (3) **Premature or shallow evaluation** — Hezekiah's self-serving reception of Isaiah's word as "good" (Isa 39:8) because it means peace in his own lifetime — Gladness resists the cognitive shortcut of evaluating as good only what benefits the self; (4) **Despair-assessment** — Jon 4:3, 8 (Jonah's "better to die") is the extreme distortion of the circumstantial-gladness faculty. Gladness resists any inner assessment that is not grounded in genuine moral and covenantal reality.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Delight explicitly excludes: (1) **External ritual without inner transformation** — Psa 40:6; 51:16; Isa 1:11; Heb 10:6, 8 — God's delight is not engaged by sacrifice and offering without the accompanying inner reality; "to obey is better than sacrifice" (1Sa 15:22; M04-M-VCG-02); Hos 6:6 — God's desire is steadfast love, not sacrifice; (2) **Self-seeking pleasure on holy time** — Isa 58:13 — "not going your own ways, or seeking your own pleasure" on the Sabbath; (3) **Delight in wrong objects** — Psa 5:4 — "you are not a God who delights in wickedness"; Isa 65:12; 66:4 — the people "chose what I did not delight in"; 1Cor 10:5 — God was not pleased with most of Israel in the wilderness; Heb 10:38 — God's soul has no pleasure in the one who shrinks back; (4) **Impulsive desire without knowledge** — Pro 19:2 — "desire without knowledge is not good"; (5) **Misdirected worship-delight** — M04-P-VCG-01 (ni.cho.ach aroma to idols — Eze 6:13; 16:19; 20:28).

**[CHAR-5]** E — Pleasure explicitly excludes: (1) **Worship without covenant faithfulness** — Lev 26:31 (God will not smell pleasing aromas from the unfaithful) — the ni.cho.ach pleasure-relationship is bounded by covenant obedience; (2) **Corrupt luxury** — Isa 47:1 (Babylon's delicateness about to be stripped — pampered ease built on evil must end); Pro 19:10 (luxury unfitting for fools); (3) **Illicit sensual pleasure** — Pro 7:18 (the seductress's a.las as carnal indulgence); (4) **Excess of pleasant things** — Pro 25:27 ("not good to eat much honey") — even genuine pleasantness becomes not-pleasant in excess; (5) **Self-serving pleasant words without moral reality** — Isa 58:2 (adjacent — delight to seek God but without justice) — Pleasure in worship without moral correspondence is explicitly rejected.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Wonder explicitly excludes: (1) **Overreach** — Psa 131:1 ("I do not occupy myself with things too great and too marvellous for me") — Wonder, rightly oriented, also restrains; not everything that is marvellous should be grasped at; (2) **Complacency** — the VCG-01 proclamation-commands ("tell of all his wondrous works"; "sing to him, sing praises; tell of") resist the complacency of forgetting; Wonder resists the drift toward treating God's extraordinary acts as ordinary; (3) **Dark wonder at evil** — the Rev 17:6–7 sequence where John wonders at the harlot and is immediately questioned ("why do you marvel?") — genuine Wonder resists marvelling at evil or at the adversary's apparent power without understanding; (4) **Wonder-failure under accumulation** — Isa 29:14 ("the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the discernment of their discerning men shall be hidden") — when human wisdom accumulates to the point of no longer recognising the extraordinary, Wonder resists this closure.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The exclusion and resistance patterns across the seven reveal a common cluster-level discipline: **all seven resist directed inner-state toward wrong objects**. The specific resistances: Exultation excludes exultation at evil (Pro 24:17) and hollow festivity (Hos 9:1); Joy excludes rejoicing at wrongdoing (1Cor 13:6) and joy without root (Mat 13:20); Gladness excludes false evaluation (Num 14:3; Isa 41:7) and premature or self-serving assessment (Isa 39:8); Delight excludes external ritual without inner transformation (Psa 40:6), self-directed pleasure (Isa 58:13), and delight in wrong objects (Psa 5:4); Pleasure excludes covenant-unfaithful worship-pleasure (Lev 26:31), corrupt luxury (Isa 47:1), and deceptive pleasantness (Pro 9:17); Wonder excludes overreach (Psa 131:1), complacency (the proclamatory imperatives resist forgetting), and dark wonder at evil (Rev 17:7); Suffering-Joy excludes performed hollow cheerfulness (M04-F), shallow grounding (Joh 5:35), and denial of suffering (1Pe 1:6). The cluster as a whole thus presents a consistently morally-structured positive-affect: not any positive inner state is good, but positive inner states directed at genuinely good objects in genuinely right ways.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Shame in its acute form excludes the upright face, bold speech, confident self-presentation, and the capacity to approach. The covering of the face (Jer 14:3; Eze 7:18), the inability to lift the face toward God (Ezr 9:6), the shutting of the mouth (Eze 16:63 — "never open your mouth again because of your shame"), the backward turning (Psa 35:4; 129:5) — all evidence what shame excludes. In the M07-B seared-conscience register, the absence of shame is what the wicked person has achieved — they have excluded shame from their inner repertoire, which is not a positive attainment but a moral collapse. Shame also resists the fraudulent: blameless conduct produces opponents' shame precisely because it refuses to give them grounds for accusation (Tit 2:8; 1Pe 3:16).

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 excludes the continued self-elevation of pride. The VCG-03 evidence (Isa 2 series; 5:15; 13:11) shows God's enforced abasement targeting every form of proud self-positioning — haughty looks, pompous display, confident ability (Isa 25:11). Military defeat (VCG-02) excludes confident national power. Social demotion (VCG-01) excludes the assumption that social position is permanent.

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 excludes the recognition of the other's worth. In VCG-01, what is excluded is the inner movement of regard (entrepō) — the judge who lacks inner deference toward God and persons has excluded the worth-recognition act from his inner repertoire.

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 excludes conduct that can bear open scrutiny (2Cor 4:2 — "shameful, underhanded ways" are the opposite of openness). CHAR-4 excludes proper appetitive ordering (VCG-02 — "dishonorable passions" are the corruption of natural relations). CHAR-4 excludes genuine moral seriousness: "it is shameful even to speak of the things that they do in secret" (Eph 5:12) — shameful conduct excludes the possibility of open acknowledgment.

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 excludes the genuine worth-recognition that should accompany the person. The commands against despising (Rom 14:3 — "do not despise the one who abstains"; 1Cor 16:11 — "let no one despise him"; 1Th 5:20 — "do not despise prophecies") reveal what CHAR-5 excludes: the recognition that what is being dismissed has genuine worth that the contemptuous attitude cancels.

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 explicitly excludes the deliberate moral failure that produces guilt. The "integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands" (Gen 20:5) excludes intentional sin of the heart and willful wrongdoing of the hands. The "I wash my hands in innocence" (Psa 26:6) excludes participation in the conduct of the wicked — Psa 26:4-5 (contextually) shows that innocence is maintained by refusing association with deceitful, hypocritical, and evil persons.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The six characteristics collectively exclude a consistent set of inner-being states: (1) Upright confident self-presentation before God and community — Chars 1, 2, 3 all exclude the capacity to stand forward (the covered face, the stripped crown, the refused acknowledgment of worth). (2) Bold speech — Char 1 excludes it through silence; Char 2 through speechlessness (Mat 22:12); Char 3 through worth-denial's suppression. (3) Moral openness — Char 4 names what must remain hidden because it cannot bear scrutiny. (4) The worth-recognition that proper human community requires — Chars 3 and 5. (5) Approach to God without guilt's barrier — Char 6 in its absence-mode. At the cluster level: M07's characteristics name the barriers to the free, confident, morally grounded engagement with God and community that the image-bearer was designed for.

**[CHAR-1]** E — CHAR-1 explicitly excludes five realities that the verse evidence names directly. First, gratitude: Deu 8:14 (vc=34223, M08-A1-VCG-01) — "your heart will be lifted up and you forget the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt" — the lifted heart displaces the memory of divine provision; Hos 13:6 (vc=34232, M08-A1-VCG-01): "their heart was lifted up; therefore they forgot me." Second, hearing and repentance: Jer 13:15 (vc=34053, M08-A4-VCG-04) — "be not proud, for the Lord has spoken" — pride blocks attentiveness to God's word; Hos 7:10 (vc=34001, M08-A3-VCG-03): "the pride of Israel testifies to his face; yet they do not return to the Lord." Third, seeking God: Psa 10:4 (vc=34074, M08-A2-VCG-02) — "the wicked does not seek him; all his thoughts are, 'there is no God.'" Fourth, wisdom: Eze 28:17 (vc=34047, M08-A1-VCG-02) — "your heart was proud... you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendour." Fifth, the fear of the Lord: Pro 8:13 (vc=33958, M08-A4-VCG-04) — "Pride and arrogance and the way of evil and perverted speech I hate" — wisdom's voice names CHAR-1 as categorically incompatible with fearing God.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 explicitly excludes and resists four things named in the evidence: (a) Obedience to revealed divine commands: Deu 1:43 (vc=34123, M08-B-VCG-01) — Israel's presumption means they did not obey God's explicit prohibition; Neh 9:16 (vc=34120) — "did not obey your commandments"; (b) Submission to appointed authority: Deu 17:12 (vc=34110, M08-B-VCG-02) — "the man who acts presumptuously by not obeying the priest who stands to minister there before the Lord your God"; (c) Reverence/fear of God: Psa 86:14 (vc=34097, M08-B-VCG-02) — "they do not set God before them"; 2Pe 2:10 (vc=42739, M08-B-VCG-03) — "they do not tremble before the glorious ones"; (d) Wisdom: Pro 11:2 (vc=34109, M08-B-VCG-02) — arrogance excludes the wisdom that accompanies the humble.

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 (VCG-01 form) excludes and resists: (a) Honest self-assessment: 2Cor 10:12 (context of vc=33888, M08-C-VCG-02): comparing oneself with others and measuring oneself by oneself — Paul identifies this as the epistemic failure underlying self-commendation; (b) Acknowledgment of received goods: 1Cor 4:7 (vc=33871, M08-C-VCG-01): "why do you boast as if you did not receive it?" — self-directed boasting denies the received quality of one's capacities; (c) Integrity between inner and outer: 2Cor 5:12 (vc=33872, M08-C-VCG-02): Paul contrasts boasting in outward appearance with what is in the heart — CHAR-3's surface-boasting resists inward honesty; (d) Patience: Pro 27:1 (vc=33359, M08-C-VCG-01): boasting about tomorrow resists the patient non-claim over an uncertain future.

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 excludes: (a) Accurate self-knowledge: Rom 12:3 (vc=60866, M08-D-VCG-02) — thinking within God-assigned measure is what CHAR-4 exceeds; (b) Understanding/comprehension: 1Ti 6:4 (vc=33925, M08-D-VCG-02) — conceit paired with "understanding nothing" (mēden epistamenos) — CHAR-4 produces comprehensive epistemic failure; (c) Love's other-orientation: 1Cor 8:1 (vc=33935, M08-D-VCG-01) — "knowledge puffs up, but love builds up" — CHAR-4 is the cognitive turning-inward that resists love's outward building; 1Cor 13:4 (vc=33936): "love is not arrogant [fusioō]"; (d) Mourning/appropriate grief: 1Cor 5:2 (vc=33940, M08-D-VCG-01): puffed-up community that should be mourning — CHAR-4 resists the appropriate affective response to genuine failure.

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 explicitly excludes: (a) Trust in God as the genuine source of power and wealth: 1Ti 6:17 (vc=60878, M08-E-VCG-02) — "set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches" rather than God; Lev 26:19 (vc=33982, M08-E-VCG-01): "the pride of your power" is broken by God — implying it resisted acknowledging God as the source; (b) Service to the vulnerable: Eze 16:49 (vc=33979, M08-E-VCG-01) — Sodom's power-pride paired with failure to aid the poor and needy; (c) Humility before God's power: the repeated "God will bring down proud might" pattern (Eze 30:6; 30:18; 32:12) implies CHAR-5 resists the recognition that God's power supersedes structural human power.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Across the five, what M08 as a cluster explicitly excludes is coherent: every characteristic resists the acknowledgment that what the person is or has comes from God. CHAR-1 resists the posture of creaturely lowliness before God. CHAR-2 resists obedience to God's established authority. CHAR-3's VCG-01 form resists the acknowledgment that received goods were received (1Cor 4:7, M08-C-VCG-01). CHAR-4 resists the accurate self-assessment within God-given measure (Rom 12:3, M08-D-VCG-02). CHAR-5 resists trust in God as the source of structural goods (1Ti 6:17, M08-E-VCG-02). The cluster resists gratitude and dependence — the creaturely posture that acknowledges God as the source of all the creature is and has. This is the cluster-level synthesis of the five characteristic-specific resistances.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The corpus reveals several explicit exclusions. (a) *Eye-service and people-pleasing:* Eph6:5 and Col3:22 both explicitly contrast sincere-heart submission with "eye-service" and "people-pleasing" — the characteristic excludes compliance driven by social observation or approval. (b) *Yielding to false authority:* Gal2:5 — Paul's non-submission to false teachers is the principled exercise of the same capacity. The characteristic excludes submission to illegitimate or gospel-distorting authority. (c) *Mere ignorance-compliance:* 2Th1:8 frames disobedience as paired with "not knowing God" — genuine submission is not identical with mere ignorance-compliance or cultural conformity; it involves inner knowledge and orientation. (d) *Inner refusal:* 2Th3:14 frames the one who does not obey as having an "inner refusal" that the communal response must address.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic excludes *self-sufficiency and pride* as inner orientations: the crushed spirit (Psa34:18) is by definition one that no longer stands in proud self-sufficiency. It excludes *self-justification* — genuine contrition requires honest confrontation with moral failure rather than denial or defence. It excludes *detachment from one's own moral condition* — the broken heart (Psa34:18) is one that genuinely registers the weight of what has occurred rather than remaining analytically distant from it. The characteristic is incompatible with the self-protective deflection of genuine moral reality.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Metriopatheō explicitly excludes *excessive severity* (the harsh judgment that exceeds what is appropriate toward the ignorant and wayward — Heb5:2) and *cold detachment* (the priestly withdrawal that does not engage with the erring's condition). The grounding in "shared weakness" (Heb5:2) also excludes *prideful superiority* — the gentle dealing is incompatible with the stance of the one who has not acknowledged their own weakness. Okneō's negation (Act9:38 — "without delay") explicitly excludes *hesitation and reluctance* — the inward dragging of the will that delays genuine responsiveness. The characteristic excludes self-protective inwardness in both its engagement-quality (severity/detachment) and its responsiveness-quality (hesitation/delay).

**[CHAR-5]** E — The three-verse corpus evidences the following exclusions. (a) *Self-promotion and performance:* the inner-grounded quality of semnotēs excludes the need to perform, assert, or display — 1Ti3:4's dignity producing household order from the inside rather than through imposed force implies the characteristic is incompatible with leadership-by-self-assertion. (b) *Frivolousness and lack of moral seriousness:* Tit2:7 — dignity alongside integrity authenticating teaching — implies the characteristic excludes levity or moral flippancy in contexts requiring seriousness. (c) *Unstable self-presentation:* 1Ti2:2's dignity enabling a "peaceful and quiet life" implies the characteristic excludes the anxious, unstable self-presentation that requires constant external validation.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Exo35:5 — "whoever is of a willing heart" — explicitly structures the offering around the inner condition rather than external compulsion: the characteristic excludes giving that originates in external pressure, social obligation, or duty-compliance rather than inner free movement. 1Ch28:21 — "every willing man who has skill" — the willingness is paired with skill but distinguished from compulsion: the characteristic excludes skilled service done under force or fear. Psa51:12's request for upholding implies the characteristic excludes the self-generated will that has collapsed — it is not mere willpower but the freely-springing inner readiness that can only be divinely sustained after failure.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The corpus reveals several explicit exclusions. (a) *Self-exaltation:* Mat23:12 — the self-exalting and the self-humbling are direct opposites; the humble do not assert their standing. (b) *Conceit and selfish ambition:* Phili2:3 — humility is defined as the direct counter to conceit (kenodoxia) and selfish ambition (eritheia). (c) *Performed or externally-driven self-lowering:* Col2:18 and Col2:23 expose humility that is outward performance masking inner pride — the characteristic explicitly excludes pseudo-humility that is self-focused. (d) *Haughtiness and social hierarchy:* Rom12:16 — associating with the lowly is contrasted with being "haughty" and being "wise in your own sight." (e) *The refusal to hear God's word:* 2Ch36:12 — Zedekiah's refusal to humble himself before the prophet is his failure to receive divine address; humility includes openness to being spoken to and corrected by God.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's exclusions form a coherent pattern. All six characteristics exclude the same underlying orientation: the self turned inward against God and others. The exclusions differ in their specific form. CHAR-1 explicitly excludes self-exaltation, conceit, and performed pseudo-humility (Col2:18/23). CHAR-2 excludes eye-service and yielding to false authority (Gal2:5 — submission withheld from false teachers). CHAR-3 excludes self-sufficiency, self-justification, and detachment from one's own moral condition. CHAR-4 excludes excessive severity (the opposite of metriopatheō) and self-protective hesitation (okneō). CHAR-5 excludes self-promotion, frivolousness, and unstable self-presentation. CHAR-6 excludes compelled compliance and self-generated willpower as a substitute for genuine willing-heartedness. Cluster-level: the exclusions confirm that M09 is not primarily against strength, authority, or achievement — it is specifically against the self-asserting and self-protective *inner orientations* that make a person closed to God and closed to others. The cluster is internally consistent in what it excludes.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — Wilful sinning explicitly excludes several inner conditions. (1) *Divine restraint / protection*: Gen 20:6 — God's external intervention is what prevented sinning; sinning is what happens when that protection is not operative or is refused. (2) *Intercession*: 1Sa 12:23 — Samuel identifies ceasing to pray for Israel as itself a sin; sinning and faithful intercession stand in opposition. (3) *Covenant faithfulness*: Jos 7:11 — "Israel has sinned; they have transgressed my covenant" — sinning is the act of covenant-breaking. (4) *God's word dwelling in the heart*: Psa 119:11 — the stored word guards against sinning. (5) *Self-restraint of speech*: Psa 39:1 — guarding the mouth resists sinning with the tongue. The characteristic resists and excludes every inner condition that aligns the will with God: covenant faithfulness, stored word, intercession, restraint, and divine protection.

**[CHAR-10]** E — (1) *Enticement (deleazō)*: excludes the person's resistance of their own desire as the mechanism's entry point (Jam 1:14); excludes the "unsteady souls'" capacity to maintain stability (2Pe 2:18 — targets those "barely escaping"). (2) *Collective hypocrisy (sunupokrinomai)*: excludes honest self-presentation before others (Gal 2:13 — the acted performance replaces authentic identity); excludes Barnabas's capacity for independent moral judgement (he was "led astray" by the collective hypocrisy). (3) *Apostasy (apostasia)*: excludes continued covenantal faithfulness (Act 21:21 — "forsake Moses" = abandon circumcision and ancestral customs).

**[CHAR-11]** E — The condition explicitly excludes: (1) *Justification by works*: Rom 3:20 — "by works of the law no human being will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes knowledge of sin" — the condition is too total for law-works to remedy; (2) *Self-rescue*: Eph 2:1 — "dead in trespasses and sins" — the dead person cannot self-revive; (3) *Righteousness*: Rom 6:20 — "when you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness" — slavery to sin is a total condition that excludes even the possibility of righteousness from within; (4) *Sanctification and eternal life*: Rom 6:22 — freedom from sin is the precondition for the fruit of sanctification and eternal life; under sin, these are unavailable.

**[CHAR-12]** E — The enslaving power explicitly excludes: (1) *Freedom of will toward God*: Joh 8:34 — the slave to sin cannot freely choose toward God; the will's God-directed freedom is what the enslavement eliminates; (2) *The practice of righteousness*: Rom 6:1/2 — "continue in sin... live in it" — living in sin excludes living in righteousness by the same logic (one cannot simultaneously live in two opposed domains); (3) *The born-of-God non-sinning pattern*: 1Jo 3:9 — "he cannot keep on sinning, because he has been born of God" — the enslaving power excludes this constitutional sinlessness-pattern; those still under sin's mastery cannot produce the born-of-God pattern.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The divine record explicitly excludes: (1) *Concealment from God*: Num 32:23 — "your sin will find you out" — the record resists the person's attempt to hide it; Job 10:14 — "if I sin, you watch me and do not acquit me" — the record precludes acquittal through divine surveillance; (2) *Transfer of liability to another*: Deu 24:16 — "each one shall be put to death for his own sin" — the record resists being assigned to someone else; (3) *Self-exculpation through prosperity*: Hos 12:8 — "in all my labors they cannot find in me iniquity or sin" — Ephraim's wealth-based self-exculpation is explicitly unfounded; the record persists regardless of material standing.

**[CHAR-14]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes: (1) *Self-generated forgiveness*: the priestly mediation (Lev 10:17 — priest bears the congregation's iniquity) and Christ's blood (Mat 26:28) both establish that forgiveness requires an external mediatorial mechanism; self-forgiveness is excluded as an option; (2) *Forgiveness without seeking*: Act 2:38 — "repent and be baptized... for the forgiveness" — the grammatical structure makes repentance the condition of forgiveness-reception; passive receipt without seeking is not evidenced; (3) *Forgiveness for the eternal sin*: Mar 3:29 — the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit resists all seeking; the characteristic cannot operate in that direction.

**[CHAR-15]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes: (1) *Belief in God's wonders*: Psa 78:32 — "they still sinned; despite his wonders, they did not believe" — the persistent sinning is rooted in unbelief; belief in God's demonstrated power is what the sinning-pattern resists; (2) *Response to God's provision*: Psa 78:17 — "sinned still more against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert" — the rebellion is against God's own desert provision; the sinning-pattern resists gratitude and appropriate response; (3) *Learning from the ancestral warning*: Isa 43:27 — the first father's sinning named as Israel's starting-point implies the warning that the pattern carries and which each generation resists receiving.

**[CHAR-16]** E — The sinner-identity explicitly excludes: (1) *Standing in judgment*: Psa 1:5 — "sinners will not stand in the judgment" — the sinner-identity is incompatible with standing under divine scrutiny; (2) *Membership in the righteous congregation*: Psa 1:5 — "nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous"; (3) *Divine responsiveness*: Joh 9:31 — "God does not listen to sinners" — the sinner-identity cuts off divine hearing; (4) *Association with Christ's holiness*: Heb 7:26 — Christ "separated from sinners" — the sinner-identity is structurally incompatible with the high priestly holiness.

**[CHAR-17]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes: (1) *Standing before God*: Ezr 9:15 — "none can stand before you because of this" — guilt-state excludes the capacity to stand in God's presence; (2) *Self-concealment*: Jer 2:22 — "the stain of your guilt is still before me" — guilt cannot be hidden from God by any human self-cleansing effort; (3) *Self-exculpation*: Gen 44:16 — "how can we clear ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants" — the divine discovery of guilt forecloses self-justification; (4) *Acquittal without address*: Lev 5:19 — guilt is incurred before the Lord — it cannot simply evaporate; it requires addressing through the prescribed remedy.

**[CHAR-18]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes: (1) *Divine acceptance*: Lev 7:18 — offering eaten on the third day is "tainted" and the person "shall bear his iniquity" — iniquity nullifies the acceptance that the offering would have granted; (2) *Covenant standing*: Isa 59:2 — "your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God" — iniquity excludes unimpeded God-relationship; (3) *Answered prayer*: Isa 59:2 — "your sins have hidden his face from you so that he does not hear" — iniquity excludes divine responsiveness; (4) *Standing before God*: Psa 130:3 — "if you, O Lord, should mark iniquities, O Lord, who could stand?" — iniquity, if fully accounted, excludes every person from standing before God.

**[CHAR-19]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes: (1) *Covenant membership*: Eze 20:38 — "I will purge out the rebels from among you... they shall not enter the land of Israel" — transgression excludes from the restored community; Eze 37:23 — no longer defiling themselves with transgressions is the condition for becoming "my people"; (2) *Divine pardon in certain cases*: Exo 23:21 — "he will not pardon your transgression"; Jos 24:19 — "he will not forgive your transgressions"; (3) *Wisdom and understanding*: Hos 14:9 — transgressors stumble in the Lord's right ways — the capacity to walk in wisdom is excluded by transgression; (4) *Divine prosper*: Pro 28:13 — "whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper."

**[CHAR-2]** E — Unintentional sinning explicitly excludes *deliberate defiance*: the bishgagah qualifier (Lev 4:2; Num 15:27/28) specifically marks the act as not arising from a will consciously set against God's command. The Lev 5:1 verse (willful silence of a witness who "knows the matter yet does not speak") sits at the boundary — it involves a person who *knows* but withholds testimony, which approaches deliberate omission. The Pass A meaning marks it as "willful silence" — conscience is engaged because knowledge is present. This borderline verse reveals that CHAR-2 excludes acts where the person's knowledge of the moral reality was operative at the moment of the act. The characteristic resists: deliberateness, defiance, and conscience-active commission.

**[CHAR-20]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes: (1) *God's continued presence*: Jos 22:31 — "today we know that the Lord is in our midst, because you have not committed this breach of faith" — the absence of faithlessness is the condition of divine presence; Eze 39:23 — "I hid my face from them" — faithlessness drives God's face away; (2) *Divine blessing and stability*: Pro 13:15 — "the way of the treacherous is their ruin"; Pro 11:3 — "the crookedness of the treacherous destroys them"; (3) *Standing in the covenant community*: Eze 20:38 (CHAR-19 adjacent) — rebels purged from among Israel; 2Ch 30:7 — those who were faithless made "a desolation"; (4) *Reliable relational presence*: Pro 25:19 — "trusting in a treacherous man in time of trouble is like a bad tooth or a foot that slips."

**[CHAR-21]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes: (1) *Wisdom and knowledge*: Pro 2:12 — wisdom delivers from "men of perverted speech" — perversity and wisdom are mutually exclusive; 1Ti 6:5 — "depraved in mind and deprived of the truth" — perversity of mind excludes truth; (2) *Inheritance of the kingdom*: 1Cor 15:50 — "the perishable cannot inherit the imperishable" — the corruptible state is constitutively incompatible with God's kingdom; (3) *Divine favour*: Deu 32:20 — God hides his face from a perverse generation; (4) *Proper function of judgment*: Exo 23:8 — bribery-perversion blinds and subverts what judgment is designed to produce.

**[CHAR-22]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes: (1) *Inheritance of God's kingdom*: 1Cor 6:9 — "the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God" — the unjust character disqualifies from the kingdom; (2) *Reliable trustworthiness*: Luk 16:11 — "if you have not been faithful in the unrighteous wealth, who will entrust to you the true riches?" — injustice forfeits the trust that enables greater stewardship; (3) *Standing before the righteous*: Pro 29:27 — "an unjust man is an abomination to the righteous" — injustice makes the person morally repugnant to those who value right conduct; (4) *Functioning as a judge*: 1Cor 6:1 — "does he dare go to law before the unrighteous?" — the unjust are unsuitable arbiters.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Confession explicitly excludes and resists three things. (1) *Denial*: confession names the act as sin, which excludes the alternative of denying it occurred or denying it was wrong. The hollow-confession verse (Deu 1:41) shows denial's proximate alternative — not denying the sin verbally but denying it in action by proceeding autonomously. (2) *Self-justification*: the corpus's genuine confessions are notable for their absence of excuse — 1Ch 21:17 ("It is I who have sinned and done great evil. But these sheep, what have they done?") is self-accusatory without self-justification; Luk 15:21 ("I am no longer worthy to be called your son") accepts the full moral consequence without appealing to mitigating circumstances. (3) *Displacement*: Num 12:11 (Aaron — "we have done foolishly and have sinned") and Num 21:7 both own the community's sin rather than displacing it onto others.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience suppression excludes and resists: (1) *Accurate moral self-knowledge*: Jer 16:10 — the people's failure to recognise their sin excludes the self-knowledge that would name it correctly. (2) *The fear of God*: Ecc 8:12 — "those who fear God" is explicitly contrasted with the sinner who lacks this inner orientation — the fear of God as an operative inner state is excluded by conscience suppression. (3) *Confession*: Jer 2:35 — the active "I have not sinned" is the verbal exclusion of what confession would say; the denial explicitly resists the confessional naming. (4) *Shame and awakening*: 1Cor 15:34 — "I say this to your shame" — Paul's appeal to shame presupposes that the shame-response is what the stupor resists; the continued sinning excludes the shame-and-awakening that right moral awareness would produce.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes and resists: (1) *Obedience to God's law*: 2Ki 10:31 — "not careful to walk in the law of the Lord, the God of Israel" — law-walking is what refusal to repent excludes. (2) *Complete heart-commitment*: 2Ki 10:31 — "with all his heart" — wholehearted inner alignment is what the divided/non-turned will resists. (3) *Response to warning*: Neh 9:29 — "you warned them in order to turn them back... yet they acted presumptuously and did not obey" — responsive turning to prophetic warning is what the stubborn will resists. (4) *The sacrifice*: Heb 10:26 — deliberate sinning after knowing truth closes off sacrifice — refusal to repent excludes the use of the divine remedy.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Habitual defection explicitly excludes: (1) *Abiding in Christ*: 1Jo 3:6 — the mutually exclusive relationship: "no one who abides in him keeps on sinning; no one who keeps on sinning has either seen him or known him" — abiding and habitual sinning are structural contraries. (2) *Pleasing God*: Ecc 7:26 — "he who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is taken" — the sinner's orientation is defined by not pleasing God. (3) *Moral legacy*: Pro 13:22 — the sinner's wealth cannot be transmitted; habitual defection excludes the capacity to build a lasting good inheritance. (4) *Escape from moral entrapment*: Ecc 7:26 — the sinner "is taken" by the snare — habitual defection is the condition of being caught rather than escaping.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Contagious sin explicitly excludes: (1) *The community following the Lord*: 2Ki 17:21 — "Jeroboam drove Israel from following the Lord" — following the Lord is what contagious sin excludes from the community's orientation. (2) *The uninterrupted God-human authority chain*: 1Ki 16:2 — God elevated the leader to form his people; contagious sin breaks the intended chain (God → leader → people toward God) and replaces it with leader → people away from God. (3) *The community's moral independence from the leader's sin*: Exo 23:33 — the divine command to prevent foreign nations from dwelling in the land is precisely to prevent the loss of moral independence; contagious sin excludes the community's capacity to maintain their own God-orientation in the face of the leader's transmitted sin.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Political revolt explicitly excludes: (1) *Governing submission*: 2Ki 8:20 — "revolted from the rule of" — the ruling authority's governance is what revolt refuses; (2) *Covenantal political loyalty*: 1Ki 12:19 — "rebellion against the house of David" — the Davidic covenantal authority structure is what Israel's revolt resists; (3) *The divine order that political authority structures express*: 2Ch 21:10 — the revolt is linked to the ruler's forsaking of God — revolt against political authority mirrors and is linked to the inner revolt against God's authority.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sinful speech explicitly excludes: (1) *Truthful speech about God and persons*: Rev 2:9 — "the slander of those who say that they are Jews and are not" — sinful speech excludes honest identity; (2) *Proper acknowledgment of God's exclusive authority*: Mar 2:7 — "who can forgive sins but God alone?" — sinful speech claims divine prerogatives rather than acknowledging them; (3) *Creaturely constraint in speech*: Jude 9 — Michael withholds the blasphemous judgment — sinful speech resists the creaturely humility that acknowledges speech's limits before God; (4) *Heart-generated righteous speech*: Mat 15:19 — slander comes from the corrupted heart; pure heart-generated speech is what sinful speech corrupts and displaces.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence shows wickedness-as-settled-person-identity explicitly excluding and resisting: (1) God — the God-exclusion mechanism is definitional (Psa 10:4; 9:17; 10:13 "renounce God from within their heart"; Mal 3:18 non-service; Pro 15:29 "the Lord is far from the wicked"); (2) moral correction — Pro 9:7 ("whoever corrects a scoffer gets himself abuse") and Isa 26:10 ("if favor is shown to the wicked, he does not learn righteousness") show resistance to correction as structural; (3) justice — the wicked pervert justice (Isa 5:23; Pro 17:23; Hab 1:4) and the Ezekiel corpus shows wickedness explicitly resisting the turn toward what is just (Eze 33:9: "he does not turn from his way"); (4) the righteous — active hostility toward the righteous is a structural feature (Psa 37:12-14; 11:2; 34:21 — VCG-03).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The evidence shows constitutional inner evil explicitly excluding and resisting: (1) truth — Rom 1:18 (vc=14336 — VCG-05): unrighteousness "suppresses the truth" — active resistance to truth is definitional for adikia; (2) faith — 2Th 3:2 (vc=14450 — VCG-06): "wicked and evil men" are those for whom "not all have faith" — faithlessness is the ground of constitutional moral depravity; Heb 3:12 (vc=14423 — VCG-06) fuses evil heart with unbelieving heart; (3) the implanted word — Jam 1:21 (vc=14368 — VCG-05): rampant wickedness must be "stripped away before the implanted word can take root"; (4) genuine approach to God — Heb 10:22 (vc=14426 — VCG-06): the evil conscience makes approach to God impossible; (5) love — 1Cor 13:6 (vc=14341 — VCG-06): love refuses to rejoice in unrighteousness — evil's presence resists the orientation love requires.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The abominable inner conditions explicitly exclude and resist: (1) divine intimacy — Pro 3:32 (vc=1686 — VCG-02): the devious person is an abomination and therefore excluded from divine confidence — the characteristic forecloses the relational proximity with God; (2) divine acceptance of worship — Pro 15:8 (vc=1678 — VCG-03), Pro 21:27 (vc=1693 — VCG-03), Isa 1:13 (vc=1695 — VCG-03): the inner corruption renders religious approach unacceptable; (3) sacred space — Rev 21:27 (vc=22 — VCG-05): nothing abominable enters the holy city; Eze 44:13 (vc=66003 — VCG-04): those who committed abominations are barred from sacred service; (4) moral turning — Pro 13:19 (vc=1687 — VCG-05): fools find turning from evil to be abominable — the characteristic in fools resists its own correction; (5) shame as inner corrective — Jer 6:15 (vc=1680 — VCG-04): the silenced conscience resists shame as the natural inner response to abomination.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes and resists: (1) the divine presence — Eze 8:6 (vc=65976 — VCG-05): abominations "drive me far from my sanctuary" — the characteristic is incompatible with divine presence; (2) covenant separation from the nations — Ezr 9:1 (vc=65949 — VCG-03): "have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands with their abominations" — the characteristic is expressed through the refusal of covenant separation; (3) divine instruction — Eze 20:8 (vc=65911 — VCG-05): "not willing to listen to me. None of them cast away the detestable things" — the characteristic resists hearing and obeying; (4) the will to turn — Jer 44:4 (vc=65966 — VCG-04): persistent prophetic warnings ignored; (5) cleansing — Eze 37:23 (vc=65913 — VCG-05) shows that divine cleansing is required precisely because the characteristic resists self-generated departure.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes and resists: (1) divine hearing — Psa 66:18 (vc=38182 — VCG-04): "If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened" — cherished iniquity closes the divine ear; (2) calling on God — Psa 14:4 (vc=38229 — VCG-03): evildoers "do not call upon the Lord" — the characteristic resists the person's movement toward God; Psa 53:4 (vc=38238 — VCG-03): same — "do not call upon God"; (3) justice — Isa 59:4 (vc=38192 — VCG-02): "No one enters suit justly; no one goes to law honestly" — iniquity as inner scheming subverts the justice system; (4) wisdom — Psa 36:3 (vc=38234 — VCG-04): "he has ceased to act wisely and do good" — iniquity displaces wisdom; (5) moral instruction — Job 36:10 (vc=38215 — VCG-04): God opens ears to return from iniquity — the characteristic resists the instruction that would produce departure.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The characteristic explicitly excludes and resists: (1) repentance — Rev 16:9 (vc=14352 — VCG-01): "they did not repent and give him glory"; Rev 16:11 (vc=14350 — VCG-01): "they did not repent of their deeds" — under direct divine judgment, the hardened blasphemer refuses the repentance that would arrest the characteristic; (2) glory-giving — Rev 16:9 (VCG-01): glory is withheld; (3) truthful testimony — 1Pe 2:12 (vc=14377 — VCG-03): false accusation resists accurate naming of the person's actual character; (4) rational understanding — Jude 10 (vc=14355 — VCG-01): "blaspheme all that they do not understand" — blasphemy fills the void left by the refusal or inability to understand; (5) submission to authority — Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): "reject authority and blaspheme the glorious ones" — authority-rejection is the precondition of the blasphemous speech.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a composite exclusion profile across the six characteristics. All six characteristics exclude God's presence, communion, or response in some form: Char 1 (Psa 5:4 — the wicked cannot dwell in God's presence), Char 2 (Luk 11:39 — the cup-outside cleaned while inside full of wickedness resists genuine communion), Char 3 (Pro 3:32 — exclusion from divine confidence), Char 4 (Eze 5:11 — divine presence withdrawal), Char 5 (Psa 66:18 — cherished iniquity closes the divine ear), Char 6 (Psa 14:4 — evildoers do not call on the Lord; Rev 16:9 — refuse repentance and glory-giving). The cluster's most universal exclusion is of genuine divine-human relationship: every form of inner evil covered by M10b disrupts the divine-human relational access in some way. Char 6's additional exclusion of repentance (Rev 16:9/11 — "they did not repent") is distinctive — it shows the characteristic as self-sealing, actively resisting its own reversal.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The ritual defilement-state explicitly excludes the person from: (1) sacred eating — flesh touching an unclean thing is burned and may not be eaten (Lev 7:19 M10c-A-VCG-08); eating holy things while unclean is the grounds for being "cut off" (Lev 7:21 M10c-A-VCG-08; Lev 22:4 M10c-B-VCG-03); (2) communal worship participation — the Passover (Num 9:6-7 M10c-A-VCG-07); the Lord's offering; (3) residence within the community — those with discharge or skin disease are sent out of the camp (Num 5:2 M10c-A-VCG-07; Lev 13:46 M10c-B-VCG-03: "he shall live alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp"); (4) sacred tithe-giving — Deu 26:14 (M10c-B-VCG-01) the worshiper must declare freedom from unclean state at tithe time; (5) proximity to the divine tabernacle — unchecked defilement risks defiling the tabernacle (Lev 15:31; Num 19:13 M10c-A-VCG-07/08).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The moral-inner defilement-state explicitly excludes: (1) divine inheritance and kingdom membership — Eph 5:5 (VCG-04): "everyone who is... impure... has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God"; (2) divine welcome — 2Cor 6:17 (VCG-03): "touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you" — touching what is unclean is the barrier to divine welcome; (3) access to the eschatological Way of Holiness — Isa 35:8 (VCG-05): "the unclean shall not pass over it"; (4) the naming and communal identity of saints — Eph 5:3 (VCG-04): impurity "must not even be named among you, as is proper among saints"; (5) right motivation before God — 1Th 2:3 (VCG-02): the apostolic appeal does not spring "from impurity"; (6) worthiness for eschatological fellowship with Christ — Rev 3:4 (VCG-05): those not soiled are "worthy" to walk with Christ.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The corporate/covenantal defilement-state explicitly excludes: (1) divine presence in the defiled space — Num 35:34 (VCG-04): "you shall not defile the land in which you live, in the midst of which I dwell" — defilement and divine habitation are incompatible; (2) divine inquiry and engagement — Eze 20:31 (VCG-02): "shall I be inquired of by you, O house of Israel? As I live, declares the Lord God, I will not be inquired of by you" — persistent idolatrous self-defilement closes divine accessibility; (3) land possession and rest — Mic 2:10 (VCG-04): "this is no place to rest, because of uncleanness that destroys with a grievous destruction" — defilement disqualifies the land for habitation; (4) covenantal integrity and blessing — Num 5:27/28 (VCG-01): the defiled woman receives the curse; the undefiled receives blessing and children.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The characteristic explicitly suppresses: (1) speech and hearing — Mar 9:25 (VCG-01): Jesus addresses the spirit as "mute and deaf" — both faculties suppressed; (2) communal access — Mar 5:2 (VCG-01): "utterly cut off from clean, communal life"; (3) self-directed bodily agency — Luk 8:29 (VCG-01): "driven by the demon into the desert"; (4) the presence and authority of divine power — the spirits resist expulsion (Act 8:7 — crying out; Mar 5:8 — command must be issued); (5) restoration to familial/social belonging — Luk 9:42 — "gave him back to his father" implies the spirit had severed the familial bond.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four characteristics collectively name a comprehensive set of exclusions that together map the full scope of what defilement forecloses. Characteristic 1 excludes: sacred eating (Lev 7:19/21), communal worship participation (Num 9:6-7), residence within the camp (Num 5:2, Lev 13:46), sacred tithe-giving (Deu 26:14), proximity to the divine tabernacle (Lev 15:31). Characteristic 2 excludes: divine inheritance and kingdom membership (Eph 5:5), divine welcome (2Cor 6:17), access to the eschatological Way of Holiness (Isa 35:8), the communal identity of saints (Eph 5:3). Characteristic 3 excludes: divine habitation in the defiled space (Num 35:34), divine inquiry and engagement (Eze 20:31), land-possession and rest (Mic 2:10), covenantal blessing (Num 5:27-28). Characteristic 4 excludes: speech and hearing (Mar 9:25), communal access (Mar 5:2), self-directed bodily agency (Luk 8:29), restoration to familial belonging (Luk 9:42). The cluster's combined exclusion inventory reveals a hierarchical structure of divine access: (1) the divine dwelling and tabernacle (Chars 1, 3), (2) divine inquiry and welcome (Chars 2, 3), (3) communal-sacral participation (Chars 1, 2, 3, 4), (4) eschatological kingdom access (Char 2), and (5) personal bodily and relational integrity (Chars 1, 4). Defilement across the cluster forecloses access to God and to the community that images God's holiness.

questions.question_text: Where does the characteristic end and another thing begin — what is it not?

findings.session_b_note:
The data provides partial evidence on this boundary question. Several distinctions are implicit but not all are assembled as explicit boundary statements:

**Forgiveness is not reconciliation:** Mat 5:24 (shared anchor with R130 reconciliation) places forgiveness and reconciliation in sequence — the leaving-act (forgiveness vocabulary) *enables* reconciliation. They are distinct: forgiveness is the unilateral release of the claim; reconciliation is the bilateral restoration of the relationship. The data confirms the distinction through shared anchors but does not state it explicitly as a boundary definition.

**Forgiveness is not tolerance or indifference:** The registry description states that forgiveness is "not pretending the wrong did not happen." It presupposes moral seriousness about the wrong done. Tolerance (overlooking without moral engagement) and indifference are not addressed explicitly in the data but are implied as distinct by the emphasis on the legitimate claim being genuinely released.

**Forgiveness is not merited release:** The intercessory corpus (group 5379-002) consistently grounds the appeal in God's character, not the petitioner's merit (OBS-064-016). Forgiveness explicitly excludes merit as its basis — this distinguishes it from acquittal on grounds of innocence.

*Gap noted:* The boundary between forgiveness and mercy (R111, 16 shared verses) is not explicitly drawn in the data. DIM-064-SD016 flags this as a Session D question. The boundary between forgiveness and grace (R068) is similarly deferred (DIM-064-SD017). These are live boundary questions not yet resolved.

**Forgiveness is not merited release:** The intercessory corpus (group 5379-002) consistently grounds the appeal in God's character, not the petitioner's merit (OBS-064-016). Forgiveness explicitly excludes merit as its basis — this distinguishes it from acquittal on grounds of innocence.

*Gap noted:* The boundary between forgiveness and mercy (R111, 16 shared verses) is not explicitly drawn in the data. DIM-064-SD016 flags this as a Session D question. The boundary between forgiveness and grace (R068) is similarly deferred (DIM-064-SD017). These are live boundary questions not yet resolved.

findings.session_b_note:
The data provides boundary observations but the formal distinction work between compassion and its nearest adjacent characteristics is explicitly deferred to Session D across multiple SD pointers.

**What the data establishes:**

Compassion is not mercy (eleos/eleeō), though they are closely related. SD-009 raises the question directly: Rom 9:15 pairs oikteirō (compassion) and eleeō (mercy) as parallel verbs — are they distinguishable or purely rhetorical parallelism? The question is deferred; the boundary is not resolved in the current data.

Compassion is not grace (chen/channum), though they share the same root (CHIN/CHEN). SD-006 raises: is graciousness (channum, the character quality) distinct from grace (chen, the relational gift)? The inner-being boundary between them is unresolved.

Compassion is not steadfast love (chesed/agapē), though the chesed vocabulary is extensively present in the OWNER terms. The chesed in Reg 23 carries the negative-pole (shame) and the covenantal-character senses; the primary chesed content belongs to R103 (love) and R104 (kindness/loyalty).

Compassion is not pity in the modern sense — the vocabulary resists sentimentality. The chus (pity) term appears predominantly in judicial contexts where it is withheld; the ra.cham vocabulary grounds it in bodily-constitutional movement, not in sentiment.

**What is missing (P):** The precise inner-being boundary between compassion and mercy, and between compassion and grace, is not established in the current data. These are the most critical boundary questions and both are explicitly Session D targets (SD-006, SD-009). No new gap is required — the existing pointers capture the need.

findings.session_b_note:
The data provides partial answers to the boundary questions:

**Contrition is not shame**: The registry description distinguishes them explicitly — shame is oriented toward social observers and the fact of being caught; contrition is oriented toward the actual harm done and toward God. The verse evidence uses no shame vocabulary (busah/bosheth) in the contrition groups.

**Contrition is not repentance**: Contrition is the inner precondition for repentance; repentance (turning) is the directional act that follows from the contrite state. The relationship is sequential: contrition precedes and grounds repentance (Q040 answer). The boundary: contrition is a condition; repentance is an act.

**Contrition is not sorrow/mourning**: Related (Isa 53:5 shared with R151 sorrow) but distinguishable. Sorrow is the affective experience of grief; contrition is the moral-relational inner posture before God that may include sorrow but is not identical to it.

findings.session_b_note:
The data provides partial evidence for fellowship's boundaries, but the boundary with closely adjacent characteristics is not fully drawn.

**Fellowship is not covenant:** Covenant (R34) names the bond structure; fellowship (R62) names the participatory inner reality within that bond. They are distinct: covenant establishes the terms; fellowship is the lived experience of sharing within those terms. DIM-62-SD001 notes explicitly that fellowship may be "functionally analogous to covenant as a structural container." The boundary is deferred to Session D.

**Fellowship is not unity:** Unity (R167) appears in the co-occurrence table at 4 shared verses. Unity is the state of oneness; fellowship is the active participation that generates or constitutes that oneness. The relationship is close but the direction of the phenomena differs.

**Fellowship is not love:** Love (R103) co-occurs at 3 shared verses. Love is the motivating inner-being quality; fellowship is the structural relation it generates or is expressed through. Love can exist without fellowship being actualised; fellowship without love risks becoming formal or hollow.

**Gap:** These boundary observations are inferred from the co-occurrence data and SD pointers, not from verse-level analysis of the boundaries. SD pointers 062-SD007 and SP-062-007 (covenant) flag this for Session D. A fuller boundary analysis is Session D work.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-001: Love's definition resolves to a structured family of inner-being orientations sharing one mechanism — directed attachment toward an object — whose moral character is entirely determined by the object …
findings.finding_value: Love's definition resolves to a structured family of inner-being orientations sharing one mechanism — directed attachment toward an object — whose moral character is entirely determined by the object chosen. Within this shared mechanism, the vocabulary distinguishes three structural registers: love as disposition (the stable inner orientation — chesed, agapē as character), love as act (the commanded and exercised expression — agapaō, enemy-love), and love as condition (the identity-constituting state of being-loved — agapētos). These are not three separate loves but three aspects of love's single operation: the person has a deep stable orientation (disposition), exercises it in specific acts (act), and exists within the love-relationship as constituted by it (condition). The vocabulary arc runs from the ontologically highest (God is love — 1Jo 4:8) through the morally normative (chesed, commanded agapē) to the affective-natural (phileō, dod) to the morally inverted (love of darkness, love of self). No other characteristic in the programme commands a comparable vocabulary range. The definition's boundary with adjacent characteristics (compassion, mercy, kindness) is partially drawn: love is the broader orientation; compassion is love's suffering-triggered mode; mercy and kindness are love's formal relational expressions. The boundaries require Session D precision.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-001: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanch…
findings.finding_value: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved), condition of its object (eleeinos — the pitiable state that calls compassion forth), and externalised act (almsgiving, mercy-act). No other characteristic in the programme review set operates across all four kinds simultaneously. The four root families (RACHAM, CHASAD, SPLANCHN, OIKTIROM) identify four constituent dimensions of the single characteristic, each naming a distinct register — somatic-maternal, covenantal-relational, visceral-immediate, and deliberative-pitying respectively. The structural opposites are two distinct kinds: willed judicial hardness (the hardened heart that refuses compassion) and unwilled prosperity-blindness (Eze 16:49 — the one who does not see the need because they are satiated). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed by the consistent outward-facing structure: compassion cannot exist without a suffering other. The definitional tier's most critical gap — the receiver's inner-being experience — is entirely absent from the data, affecting T1.5, T1.6, and T1.7 throughout. This gap is the single most significant analytical absence in the registry.

findings.finding_value: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) evidenced in T4 is the relational expression of T1's boundary-definition: compassion ends where the condition (pitiable need) is absent, not where covenantal membership ends. T1's four modes of operation (T1.4) — intra-covenantal, cross-boundary, anticipatory, Christological — map onto T4's chesed/splanchnizō distinction (within-bond sustaining vs across-distance extending) and the scope analysis (covenantal and transcovenantal registers). Definition and relational scope are structurally co-determining.
