findings.finding_value: T1's definitional structure explains T6's co-occurrence pattern with precision. Guilt-073 (51 shared verses) is the definitional counterpart (T1 — forgiveness releases guilt; they are structurally inseparable). Mercy-111 (15 shared) is the generating disposition (T1 — God's mercy is what produces the forgiving act). Repentance-135 (12 shared) is the access-posture (T1 — human side receiving condition). Love-103 (8 shared) is the named downstream state (T1 — Luk 7:47). Faith-059 (9 shared) is the receiving instrument (T1). Every major co-occurrence registry corresponds to a logical role in T1's definitional structure. T6's co-occurrence data is therefore a reading of the complete forgiveness transaction from the outside — each co-registry names one element of the transaction that T1 defines from the inside.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-001: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanch…
findings.finding_value: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved), condition of its object (eleeinos — the pitiable state that calls compassion forth), and externalised act (almsgiving, mercy-act). No other characteristic in the programme review set operates across all four kinds simultaneously. The four root families (RACHAM, CHASAD, SPLANCHN, OIKTIROM) identify four constituent dimensions of the single characteristic, each naming a distinct register — somatic-maternal, covenantal-relational, visceral-immediate, and deliberative-pitying respectively. The structural opposites are two distinct kinds: willed judicial hardness (the hardened heart that refuses compassion) and unwilled prosperity-blindness (Eze 16:49 — the one who does not see the need because they are satiated). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed by the consistent outward-facing structure: compassion cannot exist without a suffering other. The definitional tier's most critical gap — the receiver's inner-being experience — is entirely absent from the data, affecting T1.5, T1.6, and T1.7 throughout. This gap is the single most significant analytical absence in the registry.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-008: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional com…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional compassionate character) operates at the soul level (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character). The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-009: T1's four kinds explain T3's most distinctive finding: that affect and moral action are structurally unified rather than sequential. In T1 terms, compassion-as-inner-event (splanchnizō) and compassion…
findings.finding_value: T1's four kinds explain T3's most distinctive finding: that affect and moral action are structurally unified rather than sequential. In T1 terms, compassion-as-inner-event (splanchnizō) and compassion-as-externalised-act are not two separate kinds but a continuous movement — the felt-movement is the beginning of the act. T3 confirms this: affect is the mechanism of movement, not its precursor. T1's finding that compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action (the unique position as motivational ground of conscientiousness) maps onto T3.10's finding of the same: the definitional claim (T1) that compassion is constitutively outward-facing explains T3's finding that it is the driving faculty between moral knowledge and moral action.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-010: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of coven…
findings.finding_value: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) evidenced in T4 is the relational expression of T1's boundary-definition: compassion ends where the condition (pitiable need) is absent, not where covenantal membership ends. T1's four modes of operation (T1.4) — intra-covenantal, cross-boundary, anticipatory, Christological — map onto T4's chesed/splanchnizō distinction (within-bond sustaining vs across-distance extending) and the scope analysis (covenantal and transcovenantal registers). Definition and relational scope are structurally co-determining.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-001: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition of being in favour — charis as inhabited state), enabling capacity (the specific power given for specific tasks — 2Cor 12:9), and character quality (gracious speech, gracious conduct — chen in 889-003). No single English equivalent captures all four. The four modes of operation (sovereign bestowal, covenantal-relational sustaining, capacity-conferring, character-forming) correspond to the four kinds without collapsing them. Two structural opposites are identified: pride (the self-elevation that refuses the favour of the greater, active and willed) and ingratitude/gracelessness (acharistos — the failure to register and respond to grace received, which T3 confirms as image-impairment). The immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response before positive states settle) is a T1.5 finding confirming that grace does not bypass creaturely recognition but requires and produces it as a transitional state. The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed throughout: grace is constitutively directional — it flows from the greater to the lesser and requires the receptor's inner-being engagement to complete its operation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-008: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's ow…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (disposition, standing, capacity, character quality) maps onto T2's constitutional levels. The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's own disposition; not a human constitutional level). The standing kind operates at the soul level (T2.2 — Rom 5:2 "this grace in which we stand"). The capacity kind operates at the spirit-soul interface — the specific enabling for specific tasks (2Cor 12:9) is received at the deepest level and expressed through specific faculties. The character-quality kind operates at the soul-to-body level (T2.7 — gracious conduct and speech expressing the received inner character outward). T1's constitutional movement finding (SD021 four-faces sequence) is the longitudinal form of T2's spatial map: T2 identifies the constitutional levels; T1 identifies the movement between them.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-010: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-su…
findings.finding_value: T1's four modes of operation map onto T4's four relational directions. The sovereign-bestowal mode corresponds to the God-to-human direction (T4.1 — primary and dominant). The covenantal-relational-sustaining mode corresponds to the relational scope (T4.5 — grace operating within and across covenantal boundaries). The capacity-conferring mode corresponds to the human-to-God direction in its supplication register (T4.2 — SD026: grace giving even the capacity to appeal). The character-forming mode corresponds to the human-giving direction (T4.3 — gracious conduct and speech as the horizontal expression of received grace-character). The vocabulary's structural insight (T4 synthesis: giving-side and receiving-side built from the same root, chen/tachanum) explains T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner engagement to complete its operation — the vocabulary encodes the two-sidedness because grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit.

findings.session_b_note: Four distinct modes of operation are visible in the data (building on Q&A-016): (1) Structural-binding mode: covenant operates as the self-binding act by which the person commits themselves to a relational bond — entry into covenant through oath, cutting ritual, or formal agreement (Neh 10:29 — OBS-034-035). This is the initiating mode. (2) Moral-sustaining mode: covenant operates as the ongoing moral character quality of keeping one's word and maintaining loyalty (3308-002 — OBS-034-053). This is the sustaining mode. (3) Constitutional-transforming mode: under the new covenant, covenant operates as the mechanism of inner constitutional change — God writes law on the heart (OBS-034-040), Spirit replaces letter (OBS-034-061). This is the receiving-and-being-changed mode. (4) Identitary-locating mode: covenant establishes and sustains the person's inner-being identity — belonging to the covenantal community (OBS-034-035, OBS-034-060). Inclusion or exclusion from covenant shapes the person's fundamental inner condition (hope vs. desolation — OBS-034-060, OBS-034-074). These four modes are not sequential stages but concurrent registers in which covenant operates simultaneously.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-001: T1 as a whole reveals that covenant is constitutively architectural — it is not a characteristic that exists on its own terms but one that structures the conditions within which other inner-being char…
findings.finding_value: T1 as a whole reveals that covenant is constitutively architectural — it is not a characteristic that exists on its own terms but one that structures the conditions within which other inner-being characteristics operate. Its working description (Q&A-018) names it as "the solemn, binding relational bond... the structured architecture of faithful relationship." Its primary dimension is Relational Disposition (Q&A-034), but its four modes of operation (disposition, act, quality, condition — Q&A-016) and its composite structure (five constituent elements — Q&A-017) reveal that covenant is genuinely multi-modal. No other characteristic in the programme is described as simultaneously a disposition, an act, a quality, and a condition — this four-modal nature is unique to covenant and is what makes it architecturally prior to other C17 characteristics. T1 establishes that covenant is not one inner-being characteristic among equals but the structural framework within which the relational-grace vocabulary of C17 operates.

findings.session_b_note: Three modes: (a) Dispositional orientation — chasid is characterised by this as settled personal quality [XREG: H2623, OBS-099-094]. Prior to specific acts; the inner ground from which acts arise. (b) Deliberate act of will — Ruth's graduated kindness, David's covenant-loyalty, Judah's surety-pledge — each a chosen act [OBS-099-086, OBS-099-071, OBS-099-063]. (c) Spirit's interior work — Gal 5:22 — chrēstotēs as fruit of the Spirit; formation mode in which kindness is produced organically [XREG: G5544, OBS-099-092]. Three modes are not mutually exclusive: Spirit forms the disposition; disposition generates deliberate acts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-001: T1 reveals that kindness is a structurally composite, other-oriented disposition — not a simple quality. Its essential character is loyal goodwill (chesed = faithfulness + kindness in a single concept…
findings.finding_value: T1 reveals that kindness is a structurally composite, other-oriented disposition — not a simple quality. Its essential character is loyal goodwill (chesed = faithfulness + kindness in a single concept), constituted internally by faithfulness, justice, compassion, and forgiveness. It operates in three distinct modes — dispositional orientation, deliberate volitional act, and Spirit-produced formation — and these are not alternatives but layers of a single integrated phenomenon. The immediate and sustained effects are distinct in kind: the immediate response to received kindness is receptive and affective (praise, relief, petition); the sustained effect is formative and dispositional (the person becomes the chasid — one whose character is shaped by chesed over time). The structural opposite is the self-enclosed inward orientation; the counterfeit (chrēstologia) is not merely an absence but an active imposture. T1's most significant intra-tier finding: kindness is primarily dispositional, but the disposition is itself composite — removing any one of its constituent elements (faithfulness, compassion, justice) changes what remains into something that is no longer fully kindness.

findings.session_b_note: The data shows a rich cognate field. Hebrew near-synonyms functioning alongside shalom: (1) Nuach/menuchah (rest, resting-place) — the cessation-dimension of peace; (2) Nachat (H5183A — quietness) — the inner stillness dimension, co-occurs with shaqat in Isa 30:15 at the analytical summit; (3) Shaqat (H8252 — quiet/quieted) — the active quieting, most prominent in its paired form "quietness and trust" (Isa 30:15); (4) Sha'anan (H7600 — at ease) — the ease dimension, positively (Isa 32:18) and negatively (Amo 6:1); (5) Demamah (H1827 — profound silence) — the threshold silence before divine speech. Greek near-synonyms: eirēnē (G1515) is not a synonym but the translation equivalent; hēsuchia/hēsuchios (G2271/G2272) — quietness, the NT equivalent of the Hebrew silence vocabulary (1Pe 3:4 — gentle and quiet spirit); anesis (G0425) — relief/rest from pressure. The cognate field reveals that peace has an inner-face (the silence/stillness vocabulary) and an outer-face (the welfare/wholeness vocabulary), and shalom is the integrative term that spans both.

findings.session_b_note: The data reveals five distinct operational modes (OBS-060-025, OBS-060-051). (1) Performative giving: the act of giving constitutes a covenantal reality — "I will give this land" enacts the covenant (OBS-060-016, OBS-060-036). (2) Responsive giving: giving triggered by the recipient's inner condition — God gives in direct answer to suffering/need (OBS-060-037). (3) Endowing giving: giving that deposits inner-being capacity — Spirit, wisdom, understanding given directly to the inner life (OBS-060-040, OBS-060-041). (4) Judicial giving: giving as moral consequence — giving-over as the expression of inner moral response to faithlessness (OBS-060-042, OBS-060-043). (5) Transformative giving: giving that reverses inner-being states — replacing depletion with fullness, mourning with gladness (OBS-060-048, OBS-060-049, OBS-060-050). In the human direction, a sixth mode is also present: (6) Relinquishing giving: releasing what was received, recognising divine sovereignty over all given goods (OBS-060-044).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-001: T1 as a whole reveals that faithfulness in this registry is structurally composite and directional. The name ("faithfulness") promises a character quality; the OWNER term (na.tan) delivers an action. …
findings.finding_value: T1 as a whole reveals that faithfulness in this registry is structurally composite and directional. The name ("faithfulness") promises a character quality; the OWNER term (na.tan) delivers an action. These are not contradictory — they are complementary aspects of the same inner-being reality: the dispositional quality only becomes faithfulness when it enacts itself (Q&A-016, Q&A-018). The triadic architecture (inner-being source → act → object given) is the definitional shape of this characteristic: it cannot be reduced to disposition alone or act alone (Q&A-017). The five operational modes (Q&A-022) show that this single definitional structure produces radically different expressions depending on what is given and from what inner state — the characteristic is definitionally unified but expressionally plural. The primary dimension (Moral Character) grounds this — it is the character quality that makes the giving faithful rather than merely generous. The definition's most distinctive feature is its disposition-in-action structure: faithfulness is a verb that must be enacted to be real, not a noun that can be possessed without expression.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-002: The disposition-in-action definition (T1) requires the full inner faculty set to be operational (T3). The triadic architecture (source → act → object) maps directly onto faculty engagement: the source…
findings.finding_value: The disposition-in-action definition (T1) requires the full inner faculty set to be operational (T3). The triadic architecture (source → act → object) maps directly onto faculty engagement: the source requires affect (compassion/anger motivating), volition (choosing to give), and moral evaluation (assessing rightness); the act requires agency (initiating the transfer); the object requires relational capacity (attending to the other's condition). No individual faculty is the characteristic — but the characteristic integrates all of them in a coordinated whole. What this pair reveals: the definition of faithfulness-as-giving is not an abstract proposition but a faculty-integration event. The characteristic exists only when the full inner-being architecture — affective, volitional, agentive, relational — is engaged together. This is why the apex instance (Job 1:21, Isa 50:6) represents the highest form: all faculties operating in unified inner-being act.

Four modes: (1) **Concealment mode** — hatred operates within while the person presents a false exterior (Pro 10:18: "the one who conceals hatred has lying lips"; Pro 26:24: "whoever hates disguises himself with his lips and harbours deceit in his heart"). (2) **Accumulation mode** — hatred intensifies when fed by new provocations (Gen 37:5, 8: "they hated him even more"). (3) **Settlement mode** — sa.tam: the hatred settles into a plan (Gen 27:41: Esau says internally "then I will kill my brother Jacob"). (4) **Expression mode** — hatred breaks through into visible behaviour when restraint fails (Eze 35:11: "the anger and envy that you showed because of your hatred against them").

Four modes: (1) **Inner speech mode** — the contempt is articulated privately (Psa 10:13: "say in his heart, 'You will not call to account'"). (2) **Behavioural mode** — the inner verdict produces action in accordance with it (Num 15:31: "because he has despised the word...he has broken his commandment"). (3) **Speech-act mode** — ne.a.tsah: blasphemous contempt expressed outward in speech (Neh 9:18, 9:26, Eze 35:12). (4) **Contagion mode** — biz.za.von: contempt spreading from one person's act through a community (Est 1:18).

Three modes: (1) **Righteous abhorrence** — the person's visceral recoil from evil, falsehood, and what violates moral truth, aligned with God's own (Psa 119:163). (2) **Inverted abhorrence** — the same capacity directed against justice and truth (Amo 5:10, Mic 3:9). (3) **Divine sustained abhorrence** — God's settled inner revulsion toward those who have persistently corrupted themselves (Psa 106:40, Amo 6:8).

Three modes: (1) **Character-quality mode** — cruelty as the persistent inner quality characterising the person (Pro 12:10: "the mercy of the wicked is cruel"). (2) **Oppressor-disposition mode** — ruthlessness as the inner character of those who do not set God before themselves (Psa 54:3). (3) **Terror-as-instrument mode** — the ruthless nations deployed by God as instruments of judgment (Eze 28:7, 30:11, 32:12 — "the most ruthless of nations").

Four modes: (1) **Personal acute mode** — ne.a.tsah: the overwhelming shame-experience in a moment of crisis (2Ki 19:3). (2) **Personal chronic mode** — cher.pah (individual): the sustained inner-social condition of the person publicly designated as shameful (Psa 69:7). (3) **Corporate-covenantal mode** — cher.pah (communal): reproach as the condition of a whole people among the nations (Eze 5:14). **[A1 — God Righteousness]** God's righteousness operates in the human context through: (1) appeal — the psalmist appeals to God's righteousness as the ground for deliverance (A1-004); (2) exposure — it exposes human unrighteousness by contrast (A1-006; Act 24:25: Felix alarmed); (3) proclamation — it must be declared and testified to (A1-005); (4) covenant — as the ground of God's faithfulness toward his people (A1-003).

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Human righteousness operates through at least seven distinct inner modes: (1) governing state structuring the whole inner life; (2) orientation toward God (A2-014: walking with him, born of him); (3) orientation toward others (A2-012: flowing outward); (4) response — gladness, exultation, praise (3246-003); (5) pursuit — hungered for, actively sought (A2-006); (6) identity — worn, carried, defining characterisation (A2-009); (7) life path — recognisable trajectory (A2-017).

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Uprightness operates through: (1) direction of speech — speaking what is right and true (Isa 33:15; Isa 45:19); (2) direction of the will — choosing the straight path (Pro 2:13–14); (3) orientation of the heart — uprightness of heart as inner state (1211-001); (4) recognition of what is right — enabling discernment of right paths (Pro 2:9).

**[C — Justification]** Operates: (1) as divine declaration — the verdict is passed and the person's standing changes (3194-001); (2) as received condition — received by faith (Gal 3:24; Tit 3:7); (3) as historical precedent extended — Abraham's case becomes the pattern for all believers (3410-001 cross-reference); (4) as inner transformation of self-understanding — the justified person can count themselves as one who stands rightly before God.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Operates through: (1) the cry — the inner movement of the wronged person toward God in petition (944-001); (2) the commission — the inner acceptance of delegated authority to execute retribution (3250-001); (3) the relinquishment — the inner act of entrusting personal vengeance to God (6841-002); (4) the inner recognition of God's freedom from human claims (6841-004).

**[E — Condemnation]** Operates through: (1) the external verdict — judicial sentence directed at the person from outside (4846-001); (2) the inner weight — the person's experience of being under verdict; (3) the reflexive self-verdict — the inner being condemning itself (4848-001); (4) the release — the inner experience of freedom when the verdict is lifted (4846-002: Joh 8:10–11); (5) the moral testimony — the righteous generation condemning the unrighteous by comparison (4846-001: Ninevites).

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** The reckoning faculty operates through: (1) theological accounting — crediting faith as righteousness, counting status before God (3410-001: Rom 4); (2) ethical self-application — counting oneself dead to sin, alive to God (Rom 6:11); (3) comparative weighing — present suffering against future glory (Rom 8:18); (4) practical deliberation — reasoning about specific decisions (Mar 11:31; Joh 11:50); (5) moral valuation — deeming worthy or unworthy (1185-001: axioō); (6) devotional orientation — preparing oneself before God in prayer (6753-003: a.rakh).

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Wickedness operates through: (1) systemic injustice — oppressing the righteous through corrupt systems (M26-A2-010 cross-reference); (2) active opposition — plotting against and persecuting the righteous (M26-A2-016); (3) suppression of uprightness — demanding smooth things instead of what is right (Isa 30:10, VSG 1214-001); (4) occupation of righteous space — "wickedness is in the place of justice" (Ecc 3:16).

**[CLUSTER]** The cluster reveals that righteousness operates through a remarkably diverse set of inner modes: as appeal, as proclamation, as governing state, as pursuit, as identity, as orientation, as verdict, as self-application, as valuation, as entrusting. The diversity of modes is itself an analytical finding — righteousness does not operate in one way but engages the whole inner person through multiple faculties and in multiple directional vectors.

Five modes: constituted character (VCG03: Pro 16:23), directional orientation (VCG04: Rom 8:5), intelligibility/perceptive grasping (VCG08: Neh 8:8), covenantal formation (VCG09: Psa 111:10), creative-design inner forming (VCG10: Exo 31:4).

findings.finding_value: M46-A operates in two distinct modes. Mode 1: gradual satiation-produced dulling — the progressive process by which material abundance removes the edge of inner hunger, eventually producing a closed, fat heart. This is the sha.men verb pattern (Deu 32:15; Jer 5:28). Mode 2: false self-assessment anchoring — the inner act of grounding identity and security in material condition, producing blindness to actual inner state. This is the Rev 3:17 / Hos 12:8 pattern. Mode 1 is a process; Mode 2 is a stable (though false) inner orientation.

findings.finding_value: M01-A operates in at least five distinct ways: (1) as moral restraint — substituting for external accountability where no human observer is present (Lev 19:14; Lev 25:43); (2) as epistemic foundation — ordering the cognitive life toward genuine knowledge (Pro 1:7; Pro 9:10; Psa 111:10); (3) as relational posture — positioning the person for covenant intimacy with God (Psa 25:14; Psa 103:11-13); (4) as identity marker — defining who the person is within a covenant community (Job 1:1; 1Ki 18:3; Neh 7:2); (5) as moral compass — redirecting the will away from evil and toward wisdom's path (Pro 8:13: "fear of God is the inner hatred of evil"; Pro 16:6; Pro 14:27).

M01-B operates as: (1) a will-governing impulse — driving flight, deception, or submission in response to threat (Gen 32:7 anchor; Gen 3:10; 1Sa 17:24); (2) a social moderator — shaping what is said and done in public through fear of crowd opinion (Mat 21:26 anchor; Joh 7:13; Gal 2:12); (3) an awe-register — producing worship-adjacent responses to divine or miraculous power (Mar 4:41 anchor; Act 2:43).

ya.re (H3372G) groups add the divine 'Fear not' command (298-001) as a structuring element — showing the divine address to inner fear as a distinct inner-being category. The reassurance pattern (divine declaration of presence + commanded displacement of fear) is significant for understanding how the inner-being state of fear is meant to be transformed.

M01-C operates as: (1) a divine weapon — actively deployed by God to paralyse enemy resistance (Exo 23:27 anchor); (2) an encircling force — surrounding and pursuing the wicked with no escape (Job 18:11 anchor); (3) a quality projected by powerful entities that radiates outward (Hab 1:7 anchor; Song 6:4); (4) an instrument of imperial domination — the defining power of military empires over their subjects (Eze 32:23 anchor).

M01-D operates as: (1) a response to catastrophic news — collapsing confidence when the assumed order shatters (Psa 6:3 anchor; Gen 45:3); (2) a divine judicial instrument — God imposing inner collapse on rebels (Psa 2:5; Jer 49:37 anchor); (3) a bodily-manifest collapse — the inner shattering becoming visible on the body (Dan 5:6 anchor); (4) a rash agitation — the ba.hal register of impulsive urgency (Pro 28:22 anchor, D-VCG-05).

M01-E operates as: (1) involuntary theophanic trembling — the body's response to divine presence (Exo 19:16 anchor); (2) reverential somatic sobriety before God's word (Isa 66:2 anchor); (3) body-register of witnessed catastrophe (Eze 26:16 anchor); (4) military panic trembling — spreading contagiously through groups (1Sa 14:15 anchor); (5) visceral shuddering of flesh (Job 21:6 anchor); (6) NT somatic gravity in worship and ministry (Phili 2:12 anchor).

M01-F operates as: (1) pervasive daily anxiety — saturating ordinary activities (Eze 12:18 anchor); (2) anticipatory dread that materializes — the feared event arriving (Job 3:25 anchor); (3) covenantal curse-dread — chronic unrelenting anxiety as divine punishment (Deu 28:66 anchor); (4) dread of divine judgment — anticipatory fear of condemnation (Heb 10:27 anchor); (5) pastoral anxiety — protective forward-looking concern for others (2Cor 12:20 anchor).

M01-G operates as: (1) spirit-level constitutional deficiency — a settled inner posture of cowardly shrinking (2Ti 1:7 anchor); (2) will-suppression — paralysing faithful action (Mat 25:25; Luk 19:21); (3) apostasy-under-pressure — the social/political dimension of yielding to threat (Rev 21:8).

Across M01, fear operates in at least ten distinct modes: as moral restraint, epistemic foundation, relational posture, identity marker, moral compass (M01-A); as will-governing impulse, social moderator, and awe-register (M01-B); as weapon, encircling force, and projected quality (M01-C); as catastrophe-response, judicial instrument, and bodily collapse (M01-D); as theophanic trembling, reverential sobriety, and panic-contagion (M01-E); as chronic anxiety, anticipatory dread, and pastoral concern (M01-F); and as constitutional failure under pressure (M01-G). The volitional faculty is engaged across every mode.
As judicial verdict: wrath operates as a stored moral verdict that issues in binding consequences — Heb 3:11 (oath of exclusion); Deu 29:28 (exile).
As covenant discipline: burning anger operates as a directed disciplinary heat that drives historical consequences — Judg 2:14; Judg 3:8 (subjugation as consequence of kindled anger).
As action-driving impulse: incensed anger erupts into immediate outward action — Exo 32:19 (Moses smashing tablets); 2Ch 16:10 (Asa imprisoning the prophet).

As possessing force: rage fills and takes possession of the inner person, displacing other faculties — Est 3:5 (Haman filled with fury); Dan 3:19 (Nebuchadnezzar filled with fury, change visible on face).

As a state requiring restraint: anger is present but held in check — Psa 78:38 (God's compassion repeatedly restraining his warranted rage); Eph 4:26 (anger acknowledged as legitimate, requiring governance).
As sustained moral stance: indignation as a persistent inner posture maintained toward wrongdoing without necessarily erupting — Psa 7:11.
As a relational arousal-dynamic: the provocation mechanism by which another's action stirs anger within the person — Jer 11:17 (idolatry provoking God to anger).
As identity-level exclusive claim: jealousy as a constitutional attribute that fires with protective passion when its claim is violated — Exo 34:14; Eze 36:5.

Eight distinct operational modes are evidenced across the cluster: judicial verdict, covenant discipline, action-driving impulse, possessing force, restrained-but-present state, sustained moral stance, arousal-dynamic, and identity-level exclusive claim.

The corpus reveals five distinct modes. (1) Receptive-passive mode: grief arrives as an overwhelming inner condition from outside — anguish seizes the person (Jer 49:24 — M03-D-VCG-04), mourning falls upon the city (Isa 29:2 — M03-B-VCG-03), distress finds the psalmist (Psa 119:143 — M03-D-VCG-01). (2) Expressive-outward mode: grief overflows from the inner being into tears (M03-A), groaning (M03-E), and structured mourning acts (M03-B). (3) Generative mode: grief produces inner-being change — repentance (2Cor 7:9 — M03-C-VCG-02), prayer (Psa 18:6 — M03-D-VCG-01), zeal (2Cor 7:11), and moral reformation. (4) Sustained-condition mode: grief settles as a persistent inner weight that drains vitality over time — sorrow spending the psalmist's life (Psa 31:10 — M03-C-VCG-01); pain as a constant inward presence (Psa 38:17 — M03-F-VCG-01). **[CHAR-14]** E — Three distinct inner modes. (1) *As volitional turning toward God*: Act 2:38 — "repent" (metanoeō — a change of mind and direction); Exo 32:30 — "I will go up to the Lord" — the will's movement toward God as the source of forgiveness is the primary inner mode; (2) *As self-affliction in seeking*: Lev 23:27 — "you shall afflict yourselves" — the Day of Atonement requires inner self-affliction as the seeking posture; (3) *As faith receiving the declaration*: Act 10:43 — "everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name" — belief is the inner receptive mode in the NT register; Luk 7:47 — "her sins... are forgiven — for she loved much" — love is the inner receptive disposition evidencing that forgiveness has been received.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Three inner modes evidenced. (1) *As an inherited unbelief disposition*: Psa 78:32 — "despite his wonders, they did not believe" — the sinning pattern is rooted in an inherited capacity for unbelief that does not yield to experienced divine power; (2) *As a prolonged inner condition*: Isa 64:5 — "in our sins we have been a long time" — the condition is not episodic but characterises the inner-being state over an extended time; (3) *As a pattern recognised and confessed corporately*: 1Ki 8:47 — "we have sinned and have acted perversely and wickedly" — the corporate inner recognition of the generational pattern is the conscience's response.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Three distinct inner modes. (1) *As self-recognised identity*: Luk 5:8 — "I am a sinful man, O Lord" — Peter's spontaneous inner recognition of his sinner-identity in the presence of holiness; Luk 18:13 — "be merciful to me, a sinner" — the tax collector's self-confession of the sinner-identity; 1Ti 1:15 — Paul's "of whom I am the foremost" — the inward claim of the worst-sinner identity; (2) *As externally assigned identity*: Mat 9:11 — "why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?" — others name the category; Joh 9:24 — "we know that this man is a sinner" — authoritative external declaration; (3) *As constituted imputed standing*: Rom 5:19 — "made sinners through Adam's disobedience" — the identity is constituted from outside the person.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Five distinct inner modes corresponding to the five VCGs. (1) *As conscience-recognition event*: Lev 5:5 — "when he realizes his guilt... and confesses" — the guilt operates as a moment of dawning inner recognition; (2) *As mounting accumulation*: Ezr 9:6 — "guilt has mounted up to the heavens" — guilt operates as a growing weight that progressively overwhelms; (3) *As unbearable burden*: Gen 4:13 — "my punishment is greater than I can bear" — guilt-as-punitive-weight operates as an inner load exceeding capacity; (4) *As conscience-stagger*: 1Sa 25:31 (pu.qah) — "pangs of conscience" — guilt operates as an inner stumbling that destabilises moral footing; (5) *As indelible stain*: Jer 2:22 — "the stain of your guilt is still before me" — guilt operates as an inner defilement that no self-generated effort removes.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Five distinct inner modes. (1) *As a measured, accumulating store*: Gen 15:16 — "not yet complete" — iniquity accumulates toward a threshold; 2Ch 33:23 (cross-ref) and Jer 25:12 — the store builds until judgment; (2) *As an overwhelming weight*: Psa 38:4 — "gone over my head; like a heavy burden, they are too heavy for me" — the weight presses on the whole person; (3) *As a heart-seated originating force*: Eze 14:3 — "taken their idols into their hearts... stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces" — the iniquity begins in the heart's chosen orientation; (4) *As a self-destructive ensnaring force*: Pro 5:22 — "the iniquities of the wicked ensnare him, and he is held fast in the cords of his sin"; (5) *As a separating barrier*: Isa 59:2 — "your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God" — iniquity operates as a structural relational barrier.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Five distinct inner modes. (1) *As an inner voice*: Psa 36:1 — "transgression speaks to the wicked deep in his heart" — transgression operates as an internal counselling voice that drives out the fear of God; (2) *As a threshold-crossing act*: Amos 1:3/6/9 — the counted transgressions that reach the threshold; Rom 4:15 — the law-violation as specific crossing; (3) *As a dominating power*: Psa 19:13 — "great transgression" exercising dominion; Pro 29:6 — transgression ensnaring the evil man; (4) *As identity-level character*: Isa 48:8 — "called a rebel from birth"; Isa 57:4 — "children of transgression"; (5) *As relational rupture*: Isa 59:13 — "transgressing, and denying the Lord, and turning back from following our God" — the inner act of turning away is constitutive.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Two distinct modes of operation within the personal-moral register (VCG-01). (1) *The ignorance mode*: the person acts without any awareness of the moral status of the act — Lev 4:2 ("sins unintentionally"), Num 15:27 ("sins unintentionally"). The conscience is not engaged at the moment of action because the morally relevant fact is not yet known. This is the purest form of the characteristic: the will acts, but not against a registered moral reality. (2) *The disclosure mode*: the sin becomes known — "when he realizes his guilt" (Lev 5:5), "the sin which they have committed becomes known" (Lev 4:14, adjacent to this corpus), "the sin which he has committed is made known to him" (Lev 4:23). At this point conscience engages and the person moves into the confession-and-remedy sequence. The characteristic thus operates in a before-awareness and after-awareness mode, with the transition point being the moment of disclosure or realisation.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Five distinct inner modes. (1) *As settled inner disposition*: Isa 48:8 — foreknown constitutional bent of the will; 2Ch 28:22 — deepening under distress rather than breaking; (2) *As act of inner allegiance-transfer*: 1Ch 5:25 — "broke faith with the God of their fathers, and whored after the gods of the peoples" — the will's active transfer of loyalty to false objects; (3) *As hidden inner duplicity*: Jer 12:6 — "though they speak friendly words to you" — the treachery is concealed behind friendly appearance; (4) *As inner hardening*: 2Ch 28:22 — "in the time of his distress he became yet more faithless to the Lord" — the will deepens its unfaithfulness under circumstances that would normally generate repentance; (5) *As spirit-level orientation*: Mal 2:15/16 — "guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not be faithless" — the spirit is the named locus requiring vigilance against faithlessness.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Five distinct inner modes. (1) *As a perverted heart continually devising evil*: Pro 6:14 — "with perverted heart devises evil, continually sowing discord" — the heart is the origin of the continuous evil-devising; (2) *As a depraved mind robbed of truth*: 1Ti 6:5 — "depraved in mind and deprived of the truth" — the cognitive faculty is corrupted at its root; (3) *As corruption through deceitful desire*: Eph 4:22 — "corrupt through deceitful desires" — the desire-faculty is the active agent of the corruption; (4) *As cognitive-relational inversion*: Isa 29:16 — the creature denying the creator — the mind inverts the proper creature-creator relationship; (5) *As degenerative transformation*: Jer 2:21 — "turned degenerate and become a wild vine" — a process of inner moral transformation in the wrong direction.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Four distinct inner modes. (1) *As a heart-devised scheme*: Psa 58:2 — "in your hearts you devise wrongs" — injustice is planned from the heart's deliberating centre; Psa 64:6 — "they search out injustice" with "diligent search" — deliberately planned; (2) *As a thoroughly internalised appetite*: Job 15:16 — "a man who drinks injustice like water" — the characteristic has become the person's natural sustenance; (3) *As shameless character*: Zep 3:5 — "the unjust knows no shame" — the inner moral-response faculty is insensible; (4) *As a fixed scalar trait*: Luk 16:10 — "dishonest in very little is also dishonest in much" — the inner character is consistent at every scale.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Three distinct modes. (1) *Conscience-initiated, spontaneous confession*: 2Sa 24:10 — "David's heart struck him" — conscience moves inward before any external prompt, and confession follows. This is confession in its purest inner-being form: the moral witness within the person activates unprompted and drives the speech-act. (2) *Externally-prompted confession*: Exo 9:27/10:16 (Pharaoh — confession under plague judgment), Num 21:7 (people — confession under serpent judgment), 1Sa 26:21 (Saul — confession after David's mercy). These operate through external events triggering recognition and naming. (3) *Sustained, extended intercession-confession*: Neh 1:6 ("confessing the sins... day and night"), Dan 9:5/8/11/15 — sustained comprehensive naming across multiple dimensions. This mode is not a single moment but a prolonged practice of naming before God. The three modes differ in origin (inner/external) and duration (single moment/sustained) but share the naming structure.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Three evidenced modes. (1) *Active verbal denial*: Jer 2:35 — "I have not sinned" / "I am innocent" — conscience suppression externalised in a speech-act that falsely claims moral standing. This is the most active mode: the person speaks against the conscience's verdict even where it dimly exists. (2) *Perceptual self-blindness*: Jer 16:10 — the people's "what sin have we committed?" — the conscience is not firing at all; the question is genuine. This is the most passive mode: the moral-witness faculty simply does not produce the signal. (3) *Habituation producing moral stupor*: Ecc 8:12; 1Cor 15:34 — repeated sinning or continued sinning under ignorance of God. This is the developmental mode: the conscience has been progressively suppressed through habit and lack of God-knowledge until it operates at minimal capacity.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Three modes. (1) *Passive continuation*: the will remains on the sinful course by default — the Kings pattern "did not depart from" (2Ki 13:2; 14:24; 15:9) presents an apparently passive mode: the will simply continues without turning. (2) *Active clinging*: 2Ki 3:3 — "he *clung* to the sin of Jeroboam" — the will actively holds the sinful course, making the refusal an act of attachment. (3) *Active hardening against correction*: Neh 9:29 — "stubborn shoulder and stiffened their neck and would not obey" — the will actively resists the call to turn; the refusal is not passive but a stiffening against God's word. These three modes share the common feature of the will not departing, but differ in the will's active contribution to the non-departure.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Three modes. (1) *Will-hardening through repetition*: Exo 9:34 — "sinned yet again and hardened his heart" — the act of sinning again hardened the will's resistance capacity; each repetition makes the will more disposed toward the next sinning act. (2) *Self-reinforcing institutional embedding*: Hos 8:11 — "altars multiplied for sinning, they have become to him altars for sinning" — the sinning pattern builds structures (altars, institutions, practices) that produce more sinning; the inner disposition externalises into structures that feed back and deepen the inner disposition. (3) *Historical-generational entrenchment*: Hos 10:9 — "from the days of Gibeah, you have sinned... there they have continued" — the pattern persists across time and generations as an unbroken inner orientation that each generation receives and sustains.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Three modes within the *leader* (source): (1) *Walking in the sinful course as the leader's own inner commitment*: 1Ki 16:26 — "walked in all the way of Jeroboam" — the leader's personal inner alignment to the sinful path is the prerequisite for transmission; (2) *Misusing the authority position*: 1Ki 16:2 — "I... made you leader... and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam" — God names the misuse of the given authority as the indictment; (3) *Building structures that transmit the sinning*: Jer 32:35 — "they built the high places of Baal... to cause Judah to sin" — the constructive agentive act embeds the transmission into a permanent structure. Within the *community* (recipient): the inner moral direction is bent — 2Ki 17:21 — "drove Israel from following the Lord" — the community's inner God-orientation is replaced by the sinning direction transmitted through the leader's authority.

**[CHAR-8]** E — The corpus evidences two inner modes. (1) *Opportunistic-volitional mode*: 2Ki 1:1 and 2Ki 3:5 — both Moab revolts occur "after the death of Ahab" — the death of the governing authority creates an opportunity that the subject-people's will seizes for revolt. The inner mode is: assessing the weakened authority position and choosing to break submission at the opportune moment. (2) *Spiritually-grounded mode*: 2Ch 21:10 — Libnah's revolt linked to Jehoram forsaking the Lord — the inner ground for revolt is the ruler's own spiritual abandonment; the revolt appears to arise from the vacuum of legitimate spiritual authority that Jehoram's forsaking created. These two modes represent different inner dynamics: opportunistic calculation vs response to spiritual-authority vacuum.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Three inner modes. (1) *Heart-corruption externalised through speech (VCG-01)*: the characteristic operates as the externalisation of the heart's moral corruption — Mat 15:19 — the heart generates evil thoughts, and slander is their verbal expression. The inner mode is: corrupt heart → corrupting speech. (2) *Presumptuous will claiming divine status (VCG-02)*: the characteristic operates through the will's presumption — claiming for oneself (or treating others as claiming) what belongs to God alone (Mar 2:7; Joh 10:33). The inner mode is: presumptuous will → blasphemous claim. (3) *Constitutive identity-level defiance (VCG-03)*: the characteristic is not an act at all but the creature's total orientation against God — Rev 13:1 — blasphemy as the constitutive character. The inner mode is: total anti-God orientation → defiant speech as the self's expression.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence maps at least four distinct modes of inner operation. (1) As a voice — Psa 36:1: "transgression speaks to the wicked deep in his heart" — wickedness operates as an internal governance voice that displaces the divine fear. (2) As a treasury — the wicked person's soul and heart function as a store of evil from which conduct flows (Pro 21:10 "the soul of the wicked desires evil"; implied in VCG-08 speech-revealing cluster — Pro 12:6, 10:6). (3) As a way — wickedness operates as a directional orientation of the will (Eze 3:18; 33:11; Isa 55:7; Pro 4:14) — the inner person is on a trajectory. (4) As a self-generating bondage — Pro 5:22 "the iniquities of the wicked ensnare him, and he is held fast in the cords of his sin" — wickedness feeds itself through the acts it generates, creating a closed inner feedback loop. These four modes are distinct but co-present in the settled wicked person.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The evidence maps four distinct modes of inner operation. (1) As a treasury — the inner person actively draws from an inner store of evil (Mat 12:35 — VCG-03: "out of his evil treasure brings forth evil"; Luk 6:45 — VCG-03: "out of his evil treasure produces evil"). (2) As leaven — the characteristic spreads and corrupts the whole from within (1Cor 5:8 — VCG-05: "the old leaven, the leaven of malice and evil"). (3) As saturation — the inner person is filled with the characteristic (Rom 1:29 — VCG-05: "filled with all manner of unrighteousness, evil, covetousness, malice"; Luk 11:39 — VCG-05: "inside you are full of greed and wickedness"). (4) As a generative source — all evil things come from within the person (Mar 7:23 — VCG-03: "all these evil things come from within, and they defile a person"). These four modes — treasury, leaven, saturation, and generative-source — describe different aspects of the same constitutional condition.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The evidence maps four distinct modes of inner operation. (1) As a heart-level inner condition — the abominable quality is located in the heart itself: Pro 11:20 (vc=1677 — VCG-01 — crooked heart), Pro 16:5 (vc=1689 — VCG-02 — arrogant heart), Pro 26:25 (vc=1694 — VCG-02 — seven abominations in his heart). (2) As a cognitive-inner operation — the thoughts of the wicked are abominable (Pro 15:26 — vc=1679 — VCG-02 — "the thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord"), meaning cognition itself, when wicked, enters the category of abomination. (3) As a conscience-silencing dynamic — the characteristic operates by suppressing the inner moral faculty of shame (Jer 6:15; Jer 8:12 — VCG-04): the conscience that should produce shame and blushing is rendered wholly non-functional. (4) As an identity-constituting dynamic — the characteristic moves beyond individual acts or states to constitute entire identity: Rev 17:5 (vc=65878 — VCG-05 — the mother of abominations) and Pro 13:19 (vc=1687 — VCG-05 — fools find departing from evil abominable) show abomination as a totalising identity orientation.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The evidence maps four distinct inner modes of operation. (1) As heart-attachment — the heart as the directional inner faculty goes after idol-objects (Eze 11:21 — vc=1631/65982 — VCG-05: "whose heart goes after their detestable things and their abominations"); (2) As soul-delight — the soul's delight-faculty is attached to abominations (Isa 66:3 — vc=1633 — VCG-04: "their soul delights in their abominations") — the appropriate affective faculty of delight, designed for the divine, is inverted; (3) As eye-feasting — the eyes as perceptive-desire faculty feed on detestable things (Eze 20:7 — vc=1634 — VCG-05: "the detestable things your eyes feast on"; Eze 20:8 — vc=65911 — VCG-05: "detestable things their eyes feasted on, nor did they forsake the idols"); (4) As will-stubbornness — the will that persistently refuses to cast away the detestable things (Eze 20:8 — VCG-05; Jer 44:4 — VCG-04: stubbornness despite repeated prophetic warning). These four modes — heart, soul, eyes, will — show the characteristic as engaging all the major inner-being faculties through the single channel of false devotion.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The evidence maps four distinct inner modes of operation. (1) As active cognitive scheming — the mind engaged in planning evil: Eze 11:2 (vc=38193 — VCG-02): "men who devise iniquity and who give wicked counsel"; Mic 2:1 (vc=38217 — VCG-02): "devise wickedness… on their beds"; Psa 36:4 (vc=38235 — VCG-02): "plots trouble while on his bed." (2) As heart-conceiving/generating — evil conceived as an inner birth: Psa 7:14 (vc=38245 — VCG-02): "conceives evil… gives birth to lies"; Job 15:35 (vc=38208 — VCG-02): "conceive trouble and give birth to evil." (3) As stored/harboured inner condition — iniquity held and accumulated: Psa 66:18 (vc=38182 — VCG-04): "cherished iniquity in my heart"; Psa 41:6 (vc=38236 — VCG-04): "his heart gathers iniquity"; Psa 119:133 (vc=38227 — VCG-04): iniquity seeking dominion. (4) As habitual character-orientation — the evildoer's settled way: Pro 17:4 (vc=38219 — VCG-03): "an evildoer listens to wicked lips" — the inner appetite drawn toward harmful content. These four modes — scheming, conceiving, storing, habituating — show iniquity as operating at multiple inner levels simultaneously.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Three distinct inner modes of operation emerge. (1) As defiant will expressing contempt through cursing — the hardened inner will venting its rebellion against God through verbal blasphemy: Rev 16:9/11/21 (VCG-01): scorched, in pain, struck — yet the will curses rather than yields; Rev 13:6 (VCG-01): sustained deliberate blasphemy as total inner orientation. (2) As malicious false judgment expressed through accusation — the hostile inner evaluation of another producing verbal charges: Joh 18:30 (vc=14378 — VCG-03): "if this man were not doing evil, we would not have delivered him over" — the accusers' malicious inner assessment expressed as verbal charge. (3) As conduct-shaped testimony — the inner moral state (of failure or faithfulness) producing speech consequences for others: Rom 2:24 (vc=14357 — VCG-02): the believer's moral failure causes God's name to be blasphemed; 1Pe 2:12 (vc=14377 — VCG-03): honourable conduct causes former accusers to glorify God. Mode 3 operates indirectly — the inner character shapes how others speak about God.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster maps six distinct modes of inner operation, one per characteristic: (1) Directional-dispositional orientation (Char 1 — the wicked person's inner way directed away from God); (2) Constitutional generative output (Char 2 — the inner nature producing evil by constitution, as a diseased tree produces bad fruit — Mat 7:17-18); (3) Divine-verdict provocation through moral conditions (Char 3 — specific inner conditions of the heart provoking divine revulsion); (4) Devotional attachment to false objects (Char 4 — the heart/soul/eyes going after idol-objects); (5) Active cognitive-volitional scheming process (Char 5 — the heart busy with iniquity, devising on the bed — Isa 32:6; Psa 36:4); (6) Volitional speech-expression (Char 6 — the will generating blasphemy and false accusation through the mouth). These six modes are not mutually exclusive — a person may simultaneously exhibit multiple M10b characteristics in combined form — but each represents a distinct inner-being mechanism through which evil operates.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The ritual defilement-state operates in the inner person in at least four distinct ways evidenced across the 133 verses. (1) As a conscience-awakening signal: Lev 5:2-3 (M10c-A-VCG-01) — defilement may be incurred unknowingly, but when the person "comes to know it and realises his guilt," the conscience surfaces the condition. The defilement arrives before the inner recognition; recognition is its own distinct event. (2) As a duty-forming constraint on the will: the person in the defilement-state must not transmit it (Lev 15:11, M10c-A-VCG-06), must wash and wait, must present for examination, must not enter the tabernacle. The will operates under a structured set of obligations arising from the state. (3) As a grief-producing exclusion: Num 9:7 (M10c-A-VCG-07) — "why are we kept from bringing the Lord's offering?" The men's grief shows the defilement-state operating in the affective dimension — the desire for worship blocked by the condition they are in. (4) As a discernment-forming discipline: M10c-B-VCG-01 — the cultivation of the clean/unclean distinction is a perceptual and volitional discipline formed through sustained engagement with the characteristic's categorical structure.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The moral-inner defilement-state operates in at least four distinct ways within the inner person. (1) As constitutional ontological condition: Job 14:4 (VCG-01) — the impossibility of a clean thing from an unclean origin; the defilement is the person's constituted inner state before action. (2) As habitual flesh-dominion: Rom 6:19 (VCG-02) — "slaves to impurity" — the will's freedom is constrained by the defilement as a prior master; the person is not free but bound toward escalating moral disorder. (3) As silenced conscience leading to active greed: Eph 4:19 (VCG-02) — "become callous and have given themselves up to sensuality, greedy to practice every kind of impurity" — the conscience's silencing enables an active, appetitive pursuit of defilement. (4) As defiled conscience that makes the person's inner moral assessment unreliable: 1Cor 8:7 (VCG-03) — the weak person's conscience is defiled by eating food associated with idols; the defiled conscience cannot form correct moral assessment because the standard itself has been compromised.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The corporate/covenantal defilement-state operates in the inner person in four distinct ways. (1) As a condition of the corporate will in sustained defection: Eze 14:11 (VCG-02) — "that the house of Israel may no more go astray from me, nor defile themselves anymore with all their transgressions" — the defilement-state is the inner expression of a repeatedly straying will. (2) As self-deception regarding one's own condition: Jer 2:23 (VCG-02) — "how can you say, 'I am not unclean, I have not gone after the Baals'?" — the defiled inner condition is denied by the will that is in it; the characteristic includes self-deceived non-recognition of the defilement. (3) As memory functioning as repentance mechanism: Eze 20:43 (VCG-02) — "there you shall remember your ways and all your deeds with which you have defiled yourselves, and you shall loathe yourselves for all the evils that you have committed" — the memory of the defilement-state in exile becomes the inner generative mechanism of self-loathing and repentance. (4) As a condition observed and held by God: Eze 23:13 (VCG-02) — "I saw that she was defiled" — God's divine perception holds the defilement as an objective spiritual reality.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Four distinct ways. (1) Will-domination: Luk 8:29 (VCG-01) — "repeatedly seized him, overpowering all human restraint" and "driven by the demon" — the spirit overrides the person's own volitional direction. (2) Faculty-suppression: Mar 9:25 (VCG-01) — "mute and deaf spirit" — speech and hearing are suppressed, cutting off communicative capacity. (3) Communal-severance: Mar 5:2 (VCG-01) — the man among the tombs utterly cut off; Mar 7:25 — the child's affliction drives the mother to seek external help. (4) Violent bodily affliction: Mar 1:26 (VCG-02): "convulsing him and crying out"; Luk 9:42 (VCG-01): "the demon threw him to the ground and convulsed him."

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four operation-modes across the cluster cover every major inner-being faculty and every constitutional level. Characteristic 1 operates: as a conscience-awakening signal (Lev 5:2-3 — defilement precedes awareness; recognition is the inner event); as a duty-forming constraint on the will; as a grief-producing exclusion (Num 9:7); and as a discernment-forming discipline (M10c-B-VCG-01). Characteristic 2 operates: as constitutional ontological condition (Job 14:4 — no clean thing from an unclean source); as habitual flesh-dominion (Rom 6:19 — slaves to impurity); as silenced conscience leading to active greed (Eph 4:19); and as defiled conscience making moral assessment unreliable (1Cor 8:7). Characteristic 3 operates: as corporate-will-in-sustained-defection (Eze 14:11); as self-deception (Jer 2:23); as memory functioning as repentance mechanism (Eze 20:43); and as divinely-observed objective reality (Eze 23:13). Characteristic 4 operates: as will-domination (Luk 8:29); as faculty-suppression (Mar 9:25); as communal-severance (Mar 5:2); and as violent bodily affliction (Luk 9:42). The cluster covers the full inner-being operational range: conscience (Chars 1, 2), will (Chars 1, 2, 3, 4), memory (Char 3), discernment (Char 1), and the bodily-constitutive level (Chars 1, 4).

questions.question_text: Does the mode of operation vary by context, direction, or constitutional level; if so, how?

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the data establishes differentiation across all three axes:

**By context:**
- **Cultic/covenantal (OT):** Forgiveness operates through external mechanism — sacrifice, priestly mediation, atonement. No inner-being prerequisites named for the worshipper (Lev 4:20; OBS-064-014).
- **New covenant (NT):** Forgiveness operates through inner-being access-postures — repentance, faith, confession (F-005; OBS-064-014). The inner prerequisite is now named.
- **Intercessory (OT/NT):** Forgiveness operates through the inner act of dependence — the creature calling on God's character and covenant to grant release (group 5379-002; Dan 9:19).

**By direction:**
- **Vertical (God-to-human):** Primary direction in the Hebrew corpus and in the NT declaration vocabulary. God initiates; the human receives.
- **Horizontal (human-to-human):** Commanded direction in the NT. Human initiates in response to having received vertically. The vertical reception enables and obligates the horizontal extension.

**By constitutional level:**
- **Spirit level:** Origin of the divine disposition and act; the Spirit's role in creating inner openness for reception (OBS-064-024; Q036 answer).
- **Soul level:** The exercise-ground of human volitional forgiveness — "from the heart" (Mat 18:35; Q037 answer).
- **Interface:** The sb_classification names the spirit-soul interface as the primary location — the characteristic spans both levels and the relation between them.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the data reveals significant variation across all three axes:

**Context:** Compassion operates differently in contexts of physical suffering (healing miracles, splanchnizō toward the sick and blind), spiritual destitution (splanchnizō toward "sheep without a shepherd"), physical hunger (feeding crowds), relational/moral crisis (prodigal son, unforgiving servant), and eschatological suffering (sumpaschō within the context of glorification). The four semantic domains of splanchnizō mapped in Pass 1 confirm this contextual differentiation.

**Direction:** Compassion operates distinctly in the God-to-human direction (constitutive divine character, sovereign freedom, covenant faithfulness — ra.cham, chesed, oikteirō), in the human-to-human direction (responsive pity, participatory solidarity, almsgiving — chus, eleēmosunē, sumpatheō), and in the human-to-God direction (implicit in the supplication vocabulary: H8467 techinah, H8469 tahanun — the act of pleading for mercy assumes divine compassion as its ground, SD-021). The God-to-human direction is the most richly evidenced; the human-to-human direction produces the most action-language; the human-to-God direction is present but operates differently — as appeal and orientation rather than as extension.

**Constitutional level:** At the somatic level, compassion operates as visceral stirring (womb, entrails). At the soul level, it operates as settled character quality and affective disposition. At the volitional level, it operates as the impulse to spare, help, or give. The constitutional movement sequence (Mode 1 → Mode 2 → Mode 4 in T1.4 terms) runs from somatic to volitional. This is addressed more fully at T2.10.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the modes of operation identified at T1.4 Prompt 1 map onto different contexts and directions:

- **Context-dependence**: The penitential-relational mode requires a context of moral self-knowledge before God. The experiential-anguish mode requires a context of suffering or defeat. The substitutionary mode requires a context of vicarious bearing — it does not arise from personal moral failure.

- **Direction**: In the penitential-relational mode, the crushing is self-recognised (the person knows their condition) and the orientation is upward-to-God. In the experiential-anguish mode, the crushing is externally produced (enemy, God's chastisement, military defeat) and the inner state is produced by the blow, not by self-recognition. In the substitutionary mode, the direction inverts: the innocent receives what belongs to the guilty.

- **Constitutional level**: Spirit and heart are the consistent loci across all modes. The experiential-anguish mode also surfaces soul-language (Psa 143:3 — "he has crushed my life/soul to the ground"). The substitutionary mode produces its outcomes (peace, healing) at the relational level rather than specifying a constitutional location.

findings.session_b_note:
Yes, and the differentiation is substantial.

**By direction (vertical vs. horizontal):** Vertical fellowship (God to human or human to God: 873-001, 5367-001, 2Pe 1:4, Phili 3:10, 1Jo 1:3) operates at the ontological level — it constitutes the person's deepest relational status before God. Horizontal fellowship (human to human: 873-002, 7566-001, 7566-003, Ecc 4:10, Psa 119:63) operates at the moral-formation and mutual-support levels. These are not merely different expressions of the same phenomenon; they operate at different constitutional depths.

**By object (righteous vs. corrupted):** Fellowship with the fear-of-God community produces moral formation; fellowship with wickedness produces moral culpability; fellowship with idols produces spiritual bondage. The same constitutional faculty (the relational-joining capacity) produces radically different inner-being outcomes depending on the object.

**By temporal mode (initiating act vs. sustained condition):** Finding 062-TEMP-001 establishes that fellowship describes both one-time acts (divine promises enabling participation, God's joining of the sticks) and ongoing conditions (companionship with the fear-of-God community, covenantal companionship). The constitutional operation differs accordingly.

**New finding:** The constitutional level at which fellowship operates depends on the direction and object: divine-facing fellowship operates at the deepest constitutional level (ontological participation in divine nature), while human-facing fellowship operates at the moral-formation and mutual-support levels. This is a constitutional hierarchy within a single characteristic — not explored as a hierarchy in the existing findings.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-001: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanch…
findings.finding_value: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved), condition of its object (eleeinos — the pitiable state that calls compassion forth), and externalised act (almsgiving, mercy-act). No other characteristic in the programme review set operates across all four kinds simultaneously. The four root families (RACHAM, CHASAD, SPLANCHN, OIKTIROM) identify four constituent dimensions of the single characteristic, each naming a distinct register — somatic-maternal, covenantal-relational, visceral-immediate, and deliberative-pitying respectively. The structural opposites are two distinct kinds: willed judicial hardness (the hardened heart that refuses compassion) and unwilled prosperity-blindness (Eze 16:49 — the one who does not see the need because they are satiated). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed by the consistent outward-facing structure: compassion cannot exist without a suffering other. The definitional tier's most critical gap — the receiver's inner-being experience — is entirely absent from the data, affecting T1.5, T1.6, and T1.7 throughout. This gap is the single most significant analytical absence in the registry.

findings.finding_value: T1's four-kind structure (character quality, inner event, condition of object, externalised act) maps precisely onto T2's constitutional levels. The character-quality kind (ra.chum — dispositional compassionate character) operates at the soul level (T2.2 — chesed as soul-character). The inner-event kind (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved) operates at the somatic level (T2.6 — the gut as the site of the stirring). The condition-of-object kind (eleeinos — the pitiable state) is the constitutional trigger that activates the somatic-constitutional movement. The externalised-act kind is the constitutional endpoint of T2.10's four-stage movement sequence. T1's definition and T2's constitutional account are co-determining: the characteristic cannot be adequately defined without specifying the constitutional levels at which its four kinds operate.

findings.finding_value: T1's four kinds explain T3's most distinctive finding: that affect and moral action are structurally unified rather than sequential. In T1 terms, compassion-as-inner-event (splanchnizō) and compassion-as-externalised-act are not two separate kinds but a continuous movement — the felt-movement is the beginning of the act. T3 confirms this: affect is the mechanism of movement, not its precursor. T1's finding that compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action (the unique position as motivational ground of conscientiousness) maps onto T3.10's finding of the same: the definitional claim (T1) that compassion is constitutively outward-facing explains T3's finding that it is the driving faculty between moral knowledge and moral action.

findings.finding_value: T1's scope finding (compassion requires a suffering other; scope is determined by perceived need, not moral standing) is precisely confirmed in T4's relational analysis. The explicit crossing of covenantal boundaries (Nineveh, Samaritan/Jew) evidenced in T4 is the relational expression of T1's boundary-definition: compassion ends where the condition (pitiable need) is absent, not where covenantal membership ends. T1's four modes of operation (T1.4) — intra-covenantal, cross-boundary, anticipatory, Christological — map onto T4's chesed/splanchnizō distinction (within-bond sustaining vs across-distance extending) and the scope analysis (covenantal and transcovenantal registers). Definition and relational scope are structurally co-determining.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-001: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition of being in favour — charis as inhabited state), enabling capacity (the specific power given for specific tasks — 2Cor 12:9), and character quality (gracious speech, gracious conduct — chen in 889-003). No single English equivalent captures all four. The four modes of operation (sovereign bestowal, covenantal-relational sustaining, capacity-conferring, character-forming) correspond to the four kinds without collapsing them. Two structural opposites are identified: pride (the self-elevation that refuses the favour of the greater, active and willed) and ingratitude/gracelessness (acharistos — the failure to register and respond to grace received, which T3 confirms as image-impairment). The immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response before positive states settle) is a T1.5 finding confirming that grace does not bypass creaturely recognition but requires and produces it as a transitional state. The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed throughout: grace is constitutively directional — it flows from the greater to the lesser and requires the receptor's inner-being engagement to complete its operation.

The divine-disposition kind operates at the level of grace's origin (T2.9 — God's own disposition; not a human constitutional level). The standing kind operates at the soul level (T2.2 — Rom 5:2 "this grace in which we stand"). The capacity kind operates at the spirit-soul interface — the specific enabling for specific tasks (2Cor 12:9) is received at the deepest level and expressed through specific faculties. The character-quality kind operates at the soul-to-body level (T2.7 — gracious conduct and speech expressing the received inner character outward). T1's constitutional movement finding (SD021 four-faces sequence) is the longitudinal form of T2's spatial map: T2 identifies the constitutional levels; T1 identifies the movement between them.

**BOUNDARY characterisation — Category 3: Freedom from disordered love.** Term: G0866 afilarguros (not greedy / not a lover of money / free from love of money). Names the inner character quality of freedom from the love of money — required of leaders (1Ti 3:3 — Group 1549; Heb 13:5 — Group 1549). Why BOUNDARY: afilarguros is a negative qualifier — it names the absence of a disordered love orientation rather than the presence of a positive one. The positive love characteristic is in M05-A; afilarguros names the removal of an obstacle to that love. What this reveals: love-of-money is a structural distortion of the love characteristic — a misdirection of the love-orientation toward material goods. Genuine love-orientation requires a cleared inner space — the love-of-money must be absent before the love of God and community can be primary. This confirms M05's understanding of love as constitutively directional: the wrong direction (money) structurally crowds out the right direction (God, neighbour).

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — toward his covenant people (A1-003: faithfulness), toward the wicked (A1-006: exposing and judging), toward the Messiah (A1-007: the defining quality that becomes incarnate), toward the world (A1-002: righteous judgment). Same quality, different modes depending on relational direction.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — the OT mode is primarily conditional and forfeitable (A2-002: Ezekiel); the NT mode introduces received-through-faith righteousness (950-001) as a new mode. The characteristic operates differently at different points in the redemptive narrative.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Yes — uprightness operates at the level of speech (what one says), conduct (how one walks), and inner orientation (what one's heart is directed toward). At each level the same inner disposition manifests differently in practice.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — OT mode (947-002: acquitting the innocent in a human court) versus NT mode (3194-001: justifying the ungodly by faith). The OT mode presupposes actual innocence; the NT mode operates on the guilty made righteous through Christ. Same term, different constitutional logic.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — operates differently for: the private person (not to avenge oneself), the commissioned human authority (Rom 13:4: may and must execute wrath), and God himself (the exclusive and final avenger). Same impulse toward justice operates under different rules depending on the agent's position.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — condemnation as external verdict (4846-001), as inner weight (the experience of condemnation), and as reflexive self-verdict (4848-001: autokatakritos) are three different modes of operation.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — the logizomai faculty operates in theological mode (crediting righteousness), ethical mode (self-application to sin/life), comparative mode (suffering vs. glory), and practical deliberative mode. The faculty is the same; the content and direction of its exercise differ significantly.
**[G — Structural Opposites]** Yes — wickedness operates at individual, communal, and systemic levels. The constitutional level at which wickedness operates determines the scope of its impact.
**[CLUSTER]** Every sub-group shows context-dependence in operation. This context-dependence is a structural feature of righteousness in M26, not a defect of description.

Context differences: in bereavement, grief is primarily relational and personal (M03-A-VCG-01); in national catastrophe, it is collective and civic (M03-A-VCG-03, M03-B-VCG-02); in eschatological judgment, it is the condition of the condemned (M03-A-VCG-05); in penitential contexts, it is Godward and generative (M03-A-VCG-02, M03-C-VCG-02). Directional differences: grief directed toward God (prayer, intercession, lament) operates through the distress-drives-prayer pattern (M03-D-VCG-01); grief directed toward another person (empathic solidarity) operates through weeping-with (Rom 12:15 — M03-A-VCG-05) and compassionate presence. Constitutional level differences: spirit-level grief is evidenced in Job 7:11 ("anguish of my spirit" — M03-D-VCG-02) and the Spirit's interceding groaning (Rom 8:26 — M03-E-VCG-02); soul-level grief is evidenced in the perilupos passages (Mat 26:38 — M03-C-VCG-03) and the ya.gon corpus (M03-C-VCG-01); heart-level grief in the tsa.rah/heart location (Psa 25:17; 2Cor 2:4; Psa 13:2).

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, in two observable ways. First, **by object**: exultation directed at God's salvation (Psa 35:9; Isa 25:9; Hab 3:18) has an explicitly eschatological quality — it follows rescue and anticipates fullness. Exultation directed at God's reign (Psa 97:1; 1Ch 16:31) has a cosmic-declarative quality — it participates in the universe's recognition of divine sovereignty. Second, **by inversion**: when exultation is directed at wrong objects (evil — Pro 2:14; idols — Hos 10:5; an enemy's fall — Hab 1:15), it operates as the same inner-state capacity but distorted in direction and morally condemned. The constitutional locus does not appear to differ by context — the heart and soul are consistently named regardless of whether the exultation is spontaneous or cultivated.
