findings.finding_value: M01-A reverential fear produces over time: (1) wisdom — Pro 2:5 ("fear of God is the fruit of earnest seeking after wisdom — an inner understanding arrived at through diligent pursuit"); (2) life — Pro 10:27 ("fear of the Lord extends life"); Pro 19:23 ("fear of the Lord leads to life and produces a restful inner satisfaction"); (3) confidence — Pro 14:26 ("fear of the Lord functions as an inner foundation of strong confidence, not anxiety"); (4) ethical character — the person who sustains this fear develops trustworthiness, integrity, and justice (Exo 18:21; 2Ch 19:9); (5) community identity — the God-fearers form a recognizable community (Mal 3:16; Act 10:2; Ecc 8:12-13).

M01-B acute fear in its ongoing form (where dread persists) produces avoidance behaviors and sustained enmity: 1Sa 18:29 ("Saul's fear of David intensifies and becomes permanent — it is the inner root of his sustained enmity"). The commanded-release pattern (B-VCG-06) aims to prevent the sustained negative effect of unresolved fear.

M01-F-VCG-03 shows covenantal-curse dread producing over time: temporal distortion ("the sufferer constantly wishes the present moment away," Deu 28:67), insomnia, and the total colonization of daily life by dread (Eze 12:18-19 anchor).

M01-G timidity sustained produces apostasy (Rev 21:8: the coward is listed among those consigned to the lake of fire in a context suggesting sustained failure under pressure) and the paralysis of gifts and callings (2Ti 1:7).

Over time, fear in its ordered form (M01-A) produces wisdom, life, confidence, ethical character, and community. In its disordered forms (M01-F, G), fear produces: temporal distortion, life-colonization by dread, and apostasy. The sustained effect of fear depends entirely on whether it is ordered (directed toward God) or disordered (directed toward threat, punishment, or human opinion).

Sustained wrath produces permanent exclusion and relational rupture. Heb 3:11; 4:3 show that wrath as the ground of an oath produces a permanent closure: the rest remains inaccessible. This is wrath's sustained effect — not a temporary correction but a definitive relational verdict.

Sustained possession by rage displaces other faculties: Est 2:1 shows that after Ahasuerus's rage abated, memory and reflection could return — confirming that during the possession, these faculties were displaced. Rage's sustained presence crowds out the rational and relational.

Sustained ungoverned rage produces ingrained disposition: Pro 19:19 (M02-B-VCG-05) shows a man of great rage bearing inescapable consequences — the cycle perpetuates itself. The sustained effect of ungoverned anger is a deepening groove of reactivity that becomes its own trap.

Sustained covetous jealousy produces physical deterioration: Pro 14:30 (M02-E-VCG-04) names envy as rotting the bones — the sustained inner state of covetous jealousy destroys the person who harbours it. Pro 27:4 calls it the most irresistible and devastating of destructive passions.

Six sustained effects are evidenced across the corpus. (1) Depletion of inner vitality: grief spends the psalmist's life (Psa 31:10 — M03-C-VCG-01), pain fills all days (Ecc 2:23 — M03-F-VCG-01), sighing exhausts (Psa 6:6 — M03-E-VCG-03), sorrow sits upon the heart (Jer 8:18 — M03-C-VCG-01). (2) Prayer and God-seeking: distress becomes the regular occasion for petition (Psa 86:7; 50:15 — M03-D-VCG-01). (3) Moral reformation: godly grief produces earnestness, indignation, fear, longing, zeal (2Cor 7:11 — M03-C-VCG-02). (4) Transformation of the inner landscape: mourning reshapes music (Job 30:31 — M03-B-VCG-01/02), grief colors all expression. (5) Eschatological readiness: sustained grief orients the inner person toward the coming joy — exiles who sow in tears will reap in joy (Psa 126:5-6 — M03-A-VCG-04). (6) Bodily deterioration: prolonged sighing wastes the body (Psa 102:5 — M03-E-VCG-03); weeping so intense it exhausts the body's capacity to weep (1Sa 30:4 — M03-A-VCG-01).

**[CHAR-1]** E — The sustained-exultation passages (Psa 89:16 — "all the day"; Isa 65:18 — "forever") and the eschatological-joy passages suggest that sustained exultation produces: (1) a settled Godward inner orientation — the person whose exultation is habituated orients all of life toward God as its ground and object; (2) stability under adversity — Hab 3:18's "yet I will rejoice" in the face of total material loss shows that practiced exultation produces an inner stability not dependent on circumstance; (3) proclamation — sustained exultation generates the ongoing declaration of God's greatness (Psa 40:16; 70:4: "may those who love your salvation say evermore, 'God is great!'" — the continuous triumphing cry).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The sustained-joy evidence produces: (1) **Strength** — Neh 8:10 ("the joy of the Lord is your strength") — sustained Godward joy produces inner resilience; (2) **Health** — Pro 17:22 ("a joyful heart is good medicine") — the joyful heart has a medicinal effect on the inner being; (3) **Generosity** — 2Cor 8:2 (joy in severe affliction and extreme poverty overflowing into generous giving) — sustained joy expands the person's giving capacity; (4) **Stability in suffering** — 2Cor 6:10; Col 1:11; Phili 2:17 — sustained joy enables endurance; (5) **Prayer and worship** — the commanded feast-joy (Deu 16:11; Neh 8:12) over time forms the person into a worshipper; sustained joy produces and sustains the inner posture of worship; (6) **Completeness** — 2Jo 12; 1Jo 1:4; Joh 15:11; 16:24 — sustained joy in community moves toward fullness; it grows toward completion.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The sustained evidence shows Suffering-Joy producing: (1) **Proven character** — Jas 1:3–4 (the testing of faith through trials → steadfastness → completeness) — Suffering-Joy enables the trials to accomplish their formative work over time; (2) **Resilience across increasing adversity** — Act 5:41 (apostles rejoicing in their suffering → continuing to teach daily) — Suffering-Joy produces the sustained agency to continue mission under opposition; (3) **Eschatological orientation** — 1Pe 1:6–9 (present joy in salvation, trials, tested faith → "the outcome of your faith, the salvation of your souls") — sustained Suffering-Joy deepens the eschatological orientation of the inner being; (4) **Freedom from circumstantial dependence** — 2Cor 6:10 (adjacent, confirmed as Suffering-Joy territory: "sorrowful yet always rejoicing") — sustained Suffering-Joy produces a joy that is not contingent on circumstances improving.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Sustained Gladness produces: (1) **Moral formation** — M04-L-VCG-02's persistent evaluative engagement with what is good and not-good forms the inner person's moral discernment capacity over time; Pro 2:20 ("walk in the way of the good") — sustained recognition of goodness as the standard shapes the path one walks; (2) **Covenantal stability** — M04-O-VCG-04's "good hand of God" awareness (Ezr 7:9; 8:18; Neh 2:8, 18) produces stable confidence in divine providential care; sustained recognition of God's good faithfulness builds inner resilience; (3) **Doxological orientation** — sustained engagement with the ki-tov declarations produces a person whose default inner posture toward God is thanksgiving and praise; (4) **Generosity** — M04-O-VCG-03: Psa 112:5 ("it is well with the man who deals generously") — sustained wellbeing produces generous disposition.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Sustained Delight produces: (1) **Life-preservation under adversity** — Psa 119:92 ("if your law had not been my delight, I would have perished in my affliction") — the single most striking sustained-effect statement in the corpus; (2) **Aligned desires** — Psa 37:4 ("delight yourself in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart") — sustained Delight in God restructures the heart's desires to align with his giving; (3) **Sustained meditation and wisdom** — Psa 1:2 (delight in the law → meditating day and night → the blessed man's formation); Ecc 12:10 (the Preacher seeking words of delight → finding truth in delightful form); (4) **Productive will** — Isa 44:28; 46:10; 55:11 — God's sustained sovereign cha.phets producing accomplished purpose; (5) **Moral integrity** — Joh 8:29 (always pleasing the Father — the sustained effect of Delight-in-God's-pleasure producing consistent moral integrity); (6) **Corrupt formation** — Isa 66:3 ("their soul delights in their abominations") — sustained misdirected Delight forms a person deeply embedded in the wrong object.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Sustained genuine Pleasure produces: (1) **Relational depth** — 2Sa 1:26's sustained friendship with Jonathan is the deepest relational pleasantness evidenced in the corpus; sustained experience of genuine relational Pleasure deepens the bond and its inner satisfaction; (2) **Nourishment and health** — Pro 16:24 ("sweetness to the soul and health to the body") — sustained gracious speech and its Pleasure nourishes the inner and outer person; (3) **Wisdom formation** — Pro 2:10's "knowledge will be pleasant to your soul" presupposes wisdom already dwelling in the heart; sustained Pleasure in wisdom produces the person formed by its ways (Pro 3:17 — "ways of pleasantness"); (4) **Worship relationship** — the twice-daily ni.cho.ach corpus (Exo 29:38–41 — morning and evening) sustains an ongoing relationship of divine favour; sustained right worship produces a continuous pleasantness of divine reception; (5) **Eschatological orientation** — Psa 16:11 (pleasures at God's right hand forevermore) implies a sustained present orientation toward God's presence producing the eschatological fullness.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Sustained Wonder produces: (1) **Praise and proclamation** — the entire VCG-01 corpus shows Wonder producing proclamation as its sustained expression: "I will recount all of your wonderful deeds" (Psa 9:1); "I still proclaim your wondrous deeds" (Psa 71:17 — from youth to old age); (2) **Faithful memory** — 1Ch 16:12; Psa 77:11; 105:5 — Wonder sustains faithful memorial of God's acts through the inner act of deliberate remembrance; (3) **Epistemological humility** — Job 42:3; Psa 131:1 — sustained Wonder produces a stable inner posture of not-overreaching, recognising the limits of human knowledge before God's incomprehensibility; (4) **Moral faithfulness** — conversely, the absence of sustained Wonder correlates with moral failure: Neh 9:17 ("not mindful of the wonders… they rebelled"); Psa 78:32 ("despite his wonders, they did not believe") — sustained Wonder is implied as the condition for sustained faithfulness.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The sustained effects across the seven reveal the cluster's formative power as an ensemble: (1) **Strength and resilience** — Joy (Char 2): "the joy of the Lord is your strength" (Neh 8:10); Suffering-Joy (Char 7): proven character through trials (Jas 1:3–4); Delight (Char 4): life-preservation through adversity (Psa 119:92); (2) **Aligned desires and formed will** — Delight (Char 4) is the primary will-aligning characteristic: Psa 37:4's desires restructured; Psa 40:8's law internalized; (3) **Wisdom and moral formation** — Gladness (Char 3): sustained evaluative engagement forms moral clarity; Delight (Char 4): sustained law-delight drives meditation → wisdom (Psa 1:2); Wonder (Char 6): sustained Wonder produces epistemological humility (Psa 131:1); (4) **Communal and generational transmission** — Wonder (Char 6) is the most explicitly generational: "we will not hide them from their children" (Psa 78:4); Joy (Char 2): the feast-joy practices form communal identity across generations; (5) **Eschatological orientation** — Suffering-Joy (Char 7): sustained Suffering-Joy produces eschatological confidence; Delight (Char 4): sustained law-delight establishes forward eschatological orientation. The cluster's sustained effects together constitute a complete formative programme: strength, aligned desires, wisdom, communal identity, and eschatological orientation — each characteristic contributing a distinct strand to the formation of the whole person.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Three long-term patterns emerge from the evidence. (1) **Sustained inner wound** — Psa 44:15 (vc=37310/37473): "all day long my disgrace is before me, and shame has covered my face" — shame as perpetual condition. Jer 20:18 (vc=37316): "spend my days in shame" — shame as the chronic condition of Jeremiah's existence. The ke.lim.mah passages in Eze 32:24-30 (shame "carried into death") show shame persisting as an inner-social verdict even beyond life. (2) **Moral desensitisation** — sustained absence of appropriate shame produces the seared conscience (Jer 6:15; 8:12). The long-term effect of refusing corrective shame is hardening: "brazen forehead, refuses to be ashamed" (Jer 3:3, vc=38501). (3) **Identity formation** — Jeremiah's chronic shame becomes part of his identity (Jer 20:18); Israel's shame is carried generationally (Ezr 9:7 — "from the days of our fathers to this day"). Sustained shame either wounds identity (chronic inner burden) or is consciously borne (VCG-03 register) or is resolved by divine act.

**[CHAR-2]** E — In the enduring-burden mode (VCG-04), CHAR-2 produces an identity-constituting shame-condition that outlasts the immediate humiliation event. Eze 32's warriors "bearing their shame" into death — the humiliation becomes permanently attached to their identity-record. **[CHAR-3]** E — The sustained operation of abominable inner conditions produces: (1) permanent exclusion from divine intimacy — Pro 3:32 (vc=1686 — VCG-02): the devious person is an abomination and excluded from divine confidence, a structural relational consequence that persists; (2) the progressive silencing of the conscience — Jer 6:15 and Jer 8:12 (VCG-04) describe a state of total conscience-silencing where even abomination produces no shame — this is the result of sustained abomination without inner resistance; (3) the permanent weight of shame — Eze 44:13 (vc=66003 — VCG-04): those who committed abominations "shall bear their shame and the abominations that they have committed" — the abominations become a permanent inner weight they carry; (4) identity-constitution by abomination — Rev 17:5 (vc=65878 — VCG-05): sustained generation of abomination produces an identity that is wholly constituted by it. The sustained effect is deepening relational exclusion and identity corruption.

**[CHAR-4]** E — VCG-05 (Ezekiel — 43V) documents the sustained inner consequences in detail. (1) Progressive deepening: Eze 8:13 (vc=65978 — VCG-05): "You will see still greater abominations than these" — each stage surpasses the last; (2) Constitutional transformation: Hos 9:10 (vc=1632 — VCG-04): "they became detestable like the thing they loved" — the devotion-to-idols transforms the person's own inner character toward the image of what they worship; (3) Moral numbness: Eze 8:17 (vc=65980 — VCG-05): "is it too light a thing for the house of Judah to commit the abominations that they commit here" — they treat abomination as a minor matter, showing deepening moral insensitivity; (4) Memory loss: Eze 16:22 (vc=65985 — VCG-05): "in all your abominations and your whorings you did not remember the days of your youth" — the faculty of covenantal memory is suppressed; (5) Divine-presence loss: Eze 5:11 (vc=65969 — VCG-05): God withdraws from the defiled sanctuary.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The evidence documents a trajectory of progressive inner degradation. (1) Wisdom displaced: Psa 36:3 (vc=38234 — VCG-04): "he has ceased to act wisely and do good" — over time, the characteristic crowds out wisdom from the inner life. (2) Conscience deadened: Pro 30:20 (vc=38222 — VCG-04): the adulteress "wipes her mouth and says, 'I have done no wrong'" — the conscience that should register iniquity has been entirely silenced through habitual commission. (3) Inner appetite increasingly attuned to evil: Pro 17:4 (vc=38219 — VCG-03): "an evildoer listens to wicked lips" — the inner ear becomes preferentially attuned to evil speech; Pro 19:28 (vc=38220 — VCG-03): "the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity" — the appetite actively feeds on wrongdoing. (4) Irrecoverable collapse: Psa 36:12 (vc=38233 — VCG-04): "there the evildoers lie fallen; they are thrust down, unable to rise" — the sustained trajectory terminates in total ruin.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The VCG-01 corpus documents the sustained inner consequences with particular intensity. Rev 16:9 → 16:11 → 16:21 (VCG-01): the sequence across three plague events shows escalating defiance — each judgment produces not repentance but more cursing. The sustained effect is progressive hardening of the will against God: the more judgment falls, the more the characteristic deepens. Rev 13:6 (vc=14356 — VCG-01): "a total inner orientation of defiant contempt toward the divine" — sustained blasphemy establishes a comprehensive inner stance of contempt that defines the person's entire orientation toward God. For those falsely accused (VCG-03): 1Pe 2:12 (vc=14377 — VCG-03) and 1Pe 3:16 (vc=14380 — VCG-03): the sustained effect on the target of false accusation is the patient maintenance of good conscience and honourable conduct — the opposite of the characteristic producing counter-formation in the victim.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster maps a consistent progression across all six characteristics from initial inner-evil condition through deepening to terminal consequence. Common sustained effects across the cluster: (1) wisdom-displacement — Chars 1 (Psa 36:3 — "ceased to act wisely"), 2 (2Ti 3:13 — "deceiving and being deceived"), and 5 (same Psa 36:3); (2) conscience-silencing — Chars 1 (Psa 10:4 — no fear of God before eyes), 2 (moral blindness — Tit 3:3 — former life in malice), 3 (Jer 6:15 — no shame or blush), 4 (Eze 8:17 — treating abomination as trivial), 5 (Pro 30:20 — "I have done no wrong"), 6 (Rev 16:9 — did not repent); (3) divine-relationship severed — all six characteristics evidence this as a sustained consequence. The cluster's most extreme sustained-effect evidence is in Char 6 VCG-01 (Rev 16:9/11/21 — hardened will becoming more fixed under judgment) and Char 4 VCG-05 (Eze 8:13/15 — "still greater abominations" as escalating trajectory). The cluster reveals that sustained possession of any M10b characteristic produces progressive inner deterioration through the same trajectory: wisdom displaced → conscience silenced → divine relationship severed → irrecoverable collapse.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Sustained engagement with the ritual defilement-state and its management produces two documented inner-being effects over time. First, a formed conscience shaped by the clean/unclean categorical system. M10c-B-VCG-01 (Lev 10:10, 11:47, 14:57, 20:25, Deu 26:14) shows this most clearly: the purity laws exist to cultivate "active moral discernment" — distinguishing clean from unclean becomes "a perceptual and volitional discipline central to covenant life" (Lev 11:47). Peter's conviction at Act 10:14 (M10c-B-VCG-05) — "I have never eaten anything that is common or unclean" — shows the accumulated effect of a lifetime of categorical formation: the conviction is so deeply embedded it resists even divine instruction at first. Second, a vigilant bodily discipline — the duty of watchfulness over bodily actions near defiling agents (Lev 11:24-40, M10c-A-VCG-02; Lev 15:11, M10c-A-VCG-06) becomes an ongoing orientation of the person toward their bodily life and its sacral consequence.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The verse evidence documents a specific trajectory of inner-being deterioration from sustained moral-inner defilement. Rom 1:24 (VCG-02): God "gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to impurity, to the dishonoring of their bodies" — the impurity deepens and expands outward to bodily dishonour when unchecked. Rom 6:19 (VCG-02): "lawlessness leading to more lawlessness" — the defilement-state produces escalating moral disorder over time; the trajectory is intensification. Eph 4:19 (VCG-02): "become callous... greedy to practice every kind of impurity" — the sustained state produces a progressive hardening of the conscience (callousness) and an active appetite for more defilement (greed). The sequence evidenced by these three verses together: initial defilement → unchecked desire → God's judicial abandonment → bodily dishonour → moral escalation → conscience hardened → active seeking of defilement. The characteristic produces, over time, a person whose inner life is progressively oriented away from God and toward deepening corruption.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Sustained corporate/covenantal defilement produces several documented inner-being consequences over time. Eze 20:26/31 (VCG-02): God allows the defilement to deepen through judicial release ("I defiled them through their very gifts") and persistent self-defilement results in God refusing to be inquired of — over time the defilement closes relational access with God. Eze 22:3-4 (VCG-02): the city "makes idols to defile herself" — the defilement becomes self-directed and deliberate over time, evolving from an incidental consequence to an intentional act. Jer 2:23 (VCG-02): sustained self-deception about one's own defilement develops — the community can no longer perceive its own condition. Lam 1:17/4:15 (VCG-05): the sustained defilement produces the outcome of being named "a filthy thing among the nations" and expelled — corporate moral identity becomes publicly defiled over time.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Two forms of sustained effect. (1) Progressive entrenchment of domination: Luk 8:29 (VCG-01) — "for many a time it had seized him" — sustained operation is a repeated pattern of seizure; all human attempts at restraint fail. The domination extends to all external remedies ("bound with chains and shackles, but he would break the bonds"). (2) Social and relational deterioration: Mar 5:2 (VCG-01) — the man among the tombs thoroughly isolated from communal life; sustained possession has reduced him to dwelling in a place of death. The sustained effect of the characteristic is total: will, faculties, communal belonging, and bodily agency all subsumed under the spirit's domination.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four characteristics produce distinct sustained trajectories that together map the defilement condition's inner-being consequence spectrum. Characteristic 1 produces formational effects: a conscience shaped by the clean/unclean categorical system (Act 10:14 — Peter's deep conviction is the product of a lifetime of categorical formation), and a vigilant bodily discipline (Lev 11:47 — "to make a distinction" as a cultivated capacity). Characteristic 2 produces a deterioration arc: initial defilement → unchecked desire → God's judicial abandonment → bodily dishonour → escalating lawlessness (Rom 6:19) → callousness (Eph 4:19) → active greedy pursuit of more defilement — a self-reinforcing downward trajectory. Characteristic 3 produces comprehensive corporate deterioration: self-deception solidifying, divine access closing (Eze 20:31), land rendered uninhabitable (Mic 2:10), sanctuary destroyed (Psa 79:1), name defiled (Eze 22:5), community expelled (Lam 4:15). Characteristic 4 produces total existential domination: sustained possession becomes a settled condition of the person's whole existence — will bound, faculties suppressed, community severed, body subjugated (Luk 8:29, Mar 5:2). Cluster pattern: Characteristic 1 alone produces formative positive effects from sustained engagement. Characteristics 2, 3, and 4 all produce deterioration trajectories — but the mechanisms differ (internal conscience-suppression for Char 2, corporate-spatial expansion for Char 3, external spiritual domination for Char 4).

findings.session_b_note:
Drawing from the full data set, sustained engagement with forgiveness (as recipient and as forgiver) establishes:

**States:**
- Release from guilt (afesis — the condition of being forgiven, 879-001)
- Standing restored before God (group 879-001 description: "inner standing of the person before God")

**Qualities:**
- A readiness-to-pardon that mirrors divine sal.lach — the person who habitually forgives develops an abiding disposition of relational generosity
- Reverence/awe (Psa 130:4) — sustained as a quality of orientation toward God

**Capacities:**
- Capacity to extend forgiveness horizontally (F-003 — the structural enablement)
- Capacity to break relational cycles that would otherwise escalate (F-008 answer — "what the word makes possible in a relationship that would otherwise be closed or broken")

**Orientations:**
- Love-orientation toward others (Luk 7:47)
- Hope-orientation toward the future (Psa 130:5-7)
- The inner ordering of horizontal reconciliation before vertical worship (Mat 5:24; OBS-064-028)

findings.session_b_note:
From the data:

**Sustained possession** of compassion appears to produce: a character orientation toward the suffering other (the chasid type — devoted, loyal, responsive); a constitutive outward-facing inner disposition (ra.chum as adjective, sumpathēs as adjective); and an integration of inner movement with outer act (eleēmosunē as the normalised social form of sustained compassion).

**Sustained exposure** (being the recipient of divine compassion) appears to produce, by implication: the capacity for supplication (the XREF supplication vocabulary assumes a recipient who has learned to return to the compassionate God); a trust orientation (Psa 25:7 — "according to your steadfast love remember me"; Psa 48:9 — "we have thought on your steadfast love"); and a corresponding compassionate character (the mirroring principle of 2 Sam 22:26).

**What is missing (P):** The data does not trace this developmental arc explicitly. These observations are assembled from adjacent data rather than from direct statements. The sustained-effect question is genuinely underdeveloped in the current data for this registry.

findings.session_b_note:
The same data as T1.6 Prompt 1 applies. The states and qualities associated with contrition's sustained presence: **lowliness, humility, receptivity to God's word, and openness to divine revival**. These are presented as accompanying characteristics (Isa 66:2) rather than effects produced by contrition over time.

There is a suggestive sequence in the verse evidence: Psa 51:8 presents the contrite person longing for joy and gladness from their broken state. If divine revival follows (Isa 57:15), then the sustained effect of the contrition-revival sequence might be a capacity for deeper joy — the broken bones that rejoice. This is interpretive rather than directly stated.

*Partial: the data evidences accompanying orientations (lowliness, receptivity) but does not trace sustained effects over time in a way the data directly supports.*

findings.session_b_note: Sustained mercy-reception establishes: (1) The capacity to extend mercy to others (Mat 18:33 — the obligation to extend received mercy implies the received mercy creates the capacity). (2) A pastoral capacity — 2Cor 1:3–4 implies that those who receive comfort from the Father of mercies acquire the capacity to comfort others in the same affliction. (3) The identity of "God's people" — 1Pe 2:10 (received mercy constitutes corporate identity). *New finding: sustained mercy-reception produces three distinct capacities: extension capacity (mercy can be given because it was received), pastoral capacity (comfort received enables comfort extended), and identity constitution (mercy reception is the act that makes one part of God's people).* OBS-111-053, OBS-111-055, OBS-111-068.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-001: Mercy's definition is irreducibly complex — it cannot be reduced to a single act, disposition, or condition. Reading T1 as a whole reveals a four-element structure (Q&A-017: felt disposition, institut…
findings.finding_value: Mercy's definition is irreducibly complex — it cannot be reduced to a single act, disposition, or condition. Reading T1 as a whole reveals a four-element structure (Q&A-017: felt disposition, institutional mechanism, petition-response, spatial locus) operating across four distinct modes (Q&A-022: dispositional, mechanical, dialogic, institutional) with a two-pole boundary structure (mercy as character quality / mercilessness as constitutional collapse). The definitional synthesis is: mercy is the compassionate inner orientation of the greater toward the lesser in need or guilt, expressed through a structured range of mechanisms (atoning, supplicatory, dialogic, institutional), received through specific enabling inner postures (guilt-awareness, humility, persistence), and producing specific inner-state sequences (joy, shame, identity, belonging). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition primary, Transformation/GOD secondary) holds the two poles of the definition together: mercy is a disposition that is also a transforming mechanism.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-011: T1 identifies mercy as both disposition and act (Q&A-016), with immediate responses (joy, shame) and sustained effects (extension capacity, pastoral capacity, identity). T5 reveals that these sustaine…
findings.finding_value: T1 identifies mercy as both disposition and act (Q&A-016), with immediate responses (joy, shame) and sustained effects (extension capacity, pastoral capacity, identity). T5 reveals that these sustained effects are not automatic but developmental — they represent the formative arc that mercy initiates. Reading T1 and T5 together: mercy's definitional character (the distinction between disposition and act, immediate response and sustained effect in T1) is explained by T5's developmental logic — the immediate response (T1) is the first movement of the formative sequence (T5) that mercy initiates. Mercy is definitionally both a received event and a developmental process.

findings.session_b_note: Sustained contrition establishes: (1) Lowliness as character quality — the ongoing posture of the person who makes no merit-claim before God (OBS-030-017). (2) Permeability to divine word — Isa 66:2 pairs contrition with trembling at God's word; sustained contrition produces openness to divine address as a stable character orientation (OBS-030-060, OBS-030-061). (3) Receptivity to divine reviving — the contrite person is the one whom God specifically looks to with reviving intent; sustained contrition keeps the person in this receptive position (OBS-030-046). *New finding: sustained contrition produces three inter-related character capacities — lowliness, word-permeability, and divine-reviving receptivity — that together constitute the contrite person's stable inner orientation.* OBS-030-017, OBS-030-046, OBS-030-060.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-001: T1 as a whole reveals that contrition is a definitionally complex inner-being condition whose structure is determined by its origin (passive, produced by encounter), its constitutional location (spiri…
findings.finding_value: T1 as a whole reveals that contrition is a definitionally complex inner-being condition whose structure is determined by its origin (passive, produced by encounter), its constitutional location (spirit and heart), and its directional logic (downward into brokenness, then threshold toward divine response). The three-mode structure (penitential, anguish, substitutionary) is unified by the crushing metaphor but differentiated by the agent and relational context of the crushing. The definition tier establishes contrition's primary asymmetry: the person is not the author of their own contrition — they receive it from encounter with reality they cannot deflect — and this passivity is precisely what positions them for divine nearness. The structural opposite (inner self-enclosure) and the blocking condition (merit-claiming) together define contrition negatively as the absence of self-sufficiency before God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-001: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanch…
findings.finding_value: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved), condition of its object (eleeinos — the pitiable state that calls compassion forth), and externalised act (almsgiving, mercy-act). No other characteristic in the programme review set operates across all four kinds simultaneously. The four root families (RACHAM, CHASAD, SPLANCHN, OIKTIROM) identify four constituent dimensions of the single characteristic, each naming a distinct register — somatic-maternal, covenantal-relational, visceral-immediate, and deliberative-pitying respectively. The structural opposites are two distinct kinds: willed judicial hardness (the hardened heart that refuses compassion) and unwilled prosperity-blindness (Eze 16:49 — the one who does not see the need because they are satiated). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed by the consistent outward-facing structure: compassion cannot exist without a suffering other. The definitional tier's most critical gap — the receiver's inner-being experience — is entirely absent from the data, affecting T1.5, T1.6, and T1.7 throughout. This gap is the single most significant analytical absence in the registry.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-011: T1's sustained-effect analysis (largely P-rated because the receiver's inner-being experience is absent) and T5's formation arc together reveal a gap that is structurally significant: the formation pr…
findings.finding_value: T1's sustained-effect analysis (largely P-rated because the receiver's inner-being experience is absent) and T5's formation arc together reveal a gap that is structurally significant: the formation process from single compassion-event to compassion-character is the most important untraced developmental relationship in the registry. T5 provides the directional finding (the formative cycle feeds back from after-state to before-state) and names the three mechanisms (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological). T1 provides the definitional starting point (compassion as character quality is the endpoint of formation). Together they frame an arc that is identified but not filled: how does the moment of splanchnizō (T1 inner-event) accumulate into the settled character of ra.chum (T1 character quality)? T5's mechanisms suggest the answer but the data does not trace the path explicitly — a gap confirmed by both tiers.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-001: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition of being in favour — charis as inhabited state), enabling capacity (the specific power given for specific tasks — 2Cor 12:9), and character quality (gracious speech, gracious conduct — chen in 889-003). No single English equivalent captures all four. The four modes of operation (sovereign bestowal, covenantal-relational sustaining, capacity-conferring, character-forming) correspond to the four kinds without collapsing them. Two structural opposites are identified: pride (the self-elevation that refuses the favour of the greater, active and willed) and ingratitude/gracelessness (acharistos — the failure to register and respond to grace received, which T3 confirms as image-impairment). The immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response before positive states settle) is a T1.5 finding confirming that grace does not bypass creaturely recognition but requires and produces it as a transitional state. The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed throughout: grace is constitutively directional — it flows from the greater to the lesser and requires the receptor's inner-being engagement to complete its operation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-011: T1's sustained-effect finding (immediate/sustained contrast as qualitative, not merely temporal — what grace does immediately is creaturely recognition; what it does over time is constitution of ident…
findings.finding_value: T1's sustained-effect finding (immediate/sustained contrast as qualitative, not merely temporal — what grace does immediately is creaturely recognition; what it does over time is constitution of identity and character) maps onto T5's formation mechanisms. The encounter mechanism (T5) produces the immediate effects named in T1.5; the word, inference, and mediated-transformation mechanisms (T5) produce the sustained effects of T1.6. T5's five mechanisms collectively explain how the four kinds named in T1.2 are produced across different temporal and contextual registers: disposition-receipt is the encounter mechanism; standing is the spirit-outpouring mechanism; capacity is the mediated-transformation mechanism; character quality is the sustained word-and-inference mechanism. T1 names what is produced; T5 names how each kind is produced.

findings.session_b_note: Sustained absence of shalom produces progressive deterioration: (1) Somatic degradation — Psa 38:3 ("no soundness in my flesh... no health in my bones because of my sin") — sustained peacelessness shows in the body; (2) Exile and homelessness — Deu 28:65 ("you shall find no respite, and there shall be no resting place for the sole of your foot") — sustained peacelessness produces the ultimate displacement; (3) Universal desolation — Jer 12:12 ("no flesh has peace") — when shalom is withdrawn from a community, the deprivation becomes total; (4) The wicked's false prosperity — Job 21:9 ("their houses are safe from fear") reveals by contrast: the wicked have external safety but not genuine shalom — the sustained absence of authentic peace produces the counterfeit of complacent ease. The trajectory: inner → somatic → communal → eschatological.

Covenantal closure — the person is no longer capable of receiving what God or wisdom offers because the evaluative faculty has rendered those things as beneath regard.

Righteous form: reliable moral resistance to what is abhorred — the person is constitutionally opposed to corruption. Inverted form (group 252-002): constitutionally repelled by righteousness — an established moral reversal.

Pro 12:10: "the mercy of the wicked is cruel" — the character quality so thoroughly organised the person that even mercy-attempts are shaped by the cruelty. The sustained condition: an inner constitution in which every expression — including apparent mercy — is coloured by the absence of the restraining goods.

Fear: Isa 51:7 — "fear not the reproach of man" — the command implies sustained reproach has produced fear as a settled inner state. Identity fragmentation: Psa 22:6 — the sustained social designation has been internalised and restructures self-perception.
Sustained vigilance and persistent appeal — the characteristic establishes a posture of active spiritual alertness.
The "never-ending" quality of malice (Eze 25:15) names the self-sustaining inner orientation: the soul finds its pleasure in the object's destruction and seeks more occasions for that pleasure.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Capacity for confident appeal (the psalmist pattern), the orientation of testimony and proclamation (A1-005), and recognition of human inadequacy before the divine standard (A1-006). It establishes the orientation of the Messianic community: the proclamation of God's righteousness becomes the community's identity and vocation (Psa 22:31).

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Establishes: rootedness (A2-013), outward orientation toward others (A2-012), capacity for gladness and exultation in God (3246-003), stable community identity (A2-015), and the life-path of the righteous (A2-017). The person sustained in righteousness becomes recognisably a certain kind of person — not merely performing righteous acts but being righteous.

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Establishes: the capacity for accurate moral discernment (Pro 2:9), the habit of truthful speech (Isa 33:15), and the inner orientation toward what is right rather than what is smooth (Isa 30:10 — the contrast with those who demand smooth things).

**[C — Justification]** Establishes: heir-status (Tit 3:7), freedom from the weight of condemnation, and the capacity to count oneself rightly before God (the reckoning connection through F). Justified standing establishes the platform for all other inner-being development.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Establishes: the inner capacity for non-retaliation, the posture of prayer-petition toward God regarding injustice, and the recognition that God's authority over retribution is a relief rather than a constraint.

**[E — Condemnation]** Establishes: inner security before God's judgment, a conscience that no longer works against the self, and the orientation toward continued obedience that freedom from verdict makes possible ("go, and from now on sin no more," Joh 8:11).

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Establishes: increasing theological clarity (the capacity to count by faith, not by sight), moral realism about one's own condition (dead to sin, alive to God), and the orientation of endurance (weighing suffering against future glory).

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Establishes the hardened and impenitent heart (Rom 2:5) — a state that becomes increasingly resistant to righteousness. The accumulation of wrath is both a judicial reality and an inner-person developmental consequence.
Judicious speech, restraint, teachability, covenantal fidelity (evidence: Pro 16:23, Psa 111:10 as above).

findings.finding_value: Three major adjacencies from M39-A's verse landscape: (1) Compassion/mercy (R111): the cha.nan terms share root family with the mercy vocabulary (H2603A appears in the mercy registry as XREF). The distinction: grace (M39-A) operates from the greater initiating toward the lesser regardless of the lesser's need; mercy (adjacent) is specifically responsive to guilt or need. Psa 51:1 names both in one verse: "according to your steadfast love; according to your abundant mercy" — they are distinct aspects of the same divine orientation. (2) Love (R103): Lam 3:22 pairs chesed and rachamim in parallel — the steadfast-love/compassion boundary overlaps. M39-A approaches this but grace is distinguished by the merit-exclusive logic (Rom 11:6): love may be given within covenant obligation; grace by definition cannot be owed. (3) Goodness (M39-B, adjacent within the cluster): Gen 4:7 (ya.tav/goodness → ra.tsah/acceptance) links them sequentially: goodness produces the condition for grace-acceptance. Distinct: goodness is the inner quality of the person; grace is the sovereign gift from the other.

findings.finding_value: Sustained possession of M01-A reverential fear establishes: the capacity for genuine wisdom (Pro 1:7; 9:10); ethical reliability in positions of power (Exo 18:21; Neh 5:15); the relational posture that receives covenant love (Psa 103:11-17); multigenerational identity ("fear of the Lord" as the characteristic from which God's steadfast love runs across generations, Psa 103:17); and the inner integration that fear of God requires — Psa 86:11 ("fear of God requires inner integration; a divided heart is an obstacle to genuine reverence").

Sustained acute fear (unresolved) establishes permanent inner states of dread (1Sa 18:29: Saul's fear becoming permanent inner root of enmity) and speech-suppression (Joh 20:19: disciples' fear causing them to lock their doors). Sustained exposure to fear as the commanded-release corpus produces: trust (Psa 56:3-4), courage (1Ch 22:13; 28:20), and the capacity for mission (Mat 28:10).

Sustained M01-F dread establishes: the "spirit of slavery" (Rom 8:15 secondary: the spirit of slavery associated with fear, displaced by adoption) and lifelong inner bondage (Heb 2:15: "fear of death held people in lifelong inner slavery").
Sustained M01-G timidity establishes failure of stewardship (Mat 25:25-26: the buried talent) and ultimately the full apostasy pattern of Rev 21:8.

Sustained ordered fear (M01-A) establishes wisdom, integrity, and covenant identity. Sustained disordered fear (M01-F, G) establishes inner bondage, paralysis, and apostasy. The sustained effects confirm that fear is a formative characteristic — what the person fears over time shapes who the person becomes.

Sustained anger toward a person establishes lethal intent: 1Sa 20:7 (M02-B-VCG-02) shows Saul's anger as a diagnostic signal that harm toward David is already decided in the will — sustained anger crystallises into purposeful violence.

Sustained divine indignation establishes a period or era: Dan 8:19; 11:36 (M02-C-VCG-01) name indignation as defining a historical period with a fixed end point — the sustained inner disposition shapes the entire temporal structure of events within it.

Sustained quarrelsome disposition establishes a community character: 1Cor 3:3 (M02-F-VCG-01) shows quarreling as evidence of a fleshly community condition — it becomes the quality of the shared life. Strife is infectious and self-perpetuating.

Sustained grief establishes: a Godward orientation (the pattern of distress → prayer → God is repeated so often in M03-D that it becomes a characteristic inner disposition); empathic capacity (Job weeping for others, Job 30:25 — M03-A-VCG-04; commanded empathic weeping, Rom 12:15 — M03-A-VCG-05); wisdom (the wise heart dwells in the house of mourning, Ecc 7:2, 7:4 — M03-B-VCG-01, because grief confronts the person with truth); and patience (grief that does not resolve quickly is evidenced as legitimate — Samuel mourning Saul until death, 1Sa 15:35 — M03-B-VCG-02; Jacob mourning Joseph for many days, Gen 37:34 — M03-B-VCG-01).

(3) *Increasing entrenching of the will in the sinful direction*: 2Ki 3:3's "clung to" describes an active inner relationship with the sin — sustained refusal creates a bond between the will and the sinful course. (4) *Closed-off divine remedy*: Heb 10:26 — sustained deliberate sinning after knowing truth forecloses the sacrifice — the most severe consequence of refusal to repent.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Sustained habitual defection establishes: (1) *Moral identity as "the sinner"*: the Ecclesiastes person-type (Ecc 7:26; 9:2/18; Pro 11:31/13:22) describes someone whose moral identity has been constituted by the sinning pattern — the sinner is a type, a settled orientation, not merely an occasional actor. (2) *Vulnerability to entrapment*: Ecc 7:26 — "the sinner is taken by her" — the habitual sinner lacks the inner resource to escape the snare; the established sinning pattern has removed the dispositional capacity to resist. (3) *Destructive capacity*: Ecc 9:18 — "one sinner destroys much good" — the sustained sinning orientation gives the habitually sinning person a negative formative power disproportionate to their number: one established sinner can undo much accumulated good.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Sustained contagious sin establishes: (1) *Institutional structures that become self-perpetuating*: 2Ki 23:15 — Jeroboam's altar at Bethel is still standing generations after Jeroboam's death, still transmitting the sinning orientation; (2) *Communal identity shaped around the sinning direction*: 2Ki 21:11 — Manasseh's abominations have shaped Judah's communal moral identity — "has made Judah also to sin with his idols"; (3) *Generational transmission*: 1Ki 22:52 — Ahaziah follows "the way of his father and... his mother and... Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin" — three generations of transmitted sinning orientation each contributing to the received pattern.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Sustained political revolt establishes: (1) *Settled political independence*: 2Ki 8:20 — "set up a king of their own" — the revolting community establishes its own governing structure as an ongoing reality; (2) *Permanent relational fracture*: the "to this day" markers (1Ki 12:19; 2Ki 8:22) name a fracture that has become the permanent state of the relationship; (3) *In 2Ch 21:10's causal context*: the fracture is embedded in a spiritual-moral framework — the ruler's forsaking of God has produced a political environment in which loyalty structures break down.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sustained sinful speech establishes: (1) *Diseased inner craving and conceit*: 1Ti 6:4 — sustained slander from conceit entrenches the conceit; the speaking reinforces the pride that generated it; (2) *Constitutive anti-God identity*: VCG-03 — the beast's sustained blasphemy (Rev 13:5 — "for forty-two months") establishes the creature's total identity around defiance of God; (3) *2Ti 3:2's end-times character*: the blasphemous disposition is the settled character of persons who have given themselves to self-love — the speech-pattern is the established character-type.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Sustained possession of wickedness-as-settled-person-identity establishes: (a) moral blindness as a perceptual state (Pro 4:19; Isa 26:10 — even grace cannot penetrate; Dan 12:10 — the wicked "cannot understand"); (b) spiritual restlessness as a persistent condition (Isa 57:20–21 — "like the tossing sea… there is no peace for the wicked"); (c) hardened defiance as an inner posture (Eze 3:19 — refusing to turn even when warned; Isa 26:10 — incorrigibility under favour); (d) an appetite for evil as a soul-level orientation (Pro 21:10 — "the soul of the wicked desires evil"); (e) a corrupted deliberative faculty (Job 21:16 — "the counsel of the wicked is far from me" — wickedness generates a morally alien mode of reasoning). These are stable states, not transient reactions.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Sustained possession of evil as constitutional inner nature establishes: (a) defiled conscience as a permanent inner state (Heb 10:22 — VCG-06 — making approach to God structurally impossible); (b) a hostile, alienated mind (Col 1:21 — VCG-06 — "hostile in mind, doing evil deeds" — a stable cognitive orientation of enmity); (c) inner saturation with vice clusters (Rom 1:29 — VCG-05 — "filled with all manner of unrighteousness, evil, covetousness, malice" — the saturation state is a stable condition of the whole inner person); (d) moral deterioration as a trajectory (2Ti 3:13 — VCG-06 — "from bad to worse" — the trajectory of sustained possession is downward); (e) the suppression of truth as a stable inner operation (Rom 1:18 — VCG-05 — "suppress the truth" as a sustained act of the unrighteous inner person). These are not episodic but stable states established over time.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Sustained possession of abominable inner conditions establishes: (a) a conscience wholly non-functional with respect to shame — Jer 6:15 (vc=1680 — VCG-04): "they did not know how to blush" — the sustained abomination has rendered the shame-faculty inoperative; (b) a will inverted regarding moral departure — Pro 13:19 (vc=1687 — VCG-05): "to turn away from evil is an abomination to fools" — the sustained character finds the very idea of departure from evil repugnant; (c) a hidden interior packed with multiple corrupt motivations — Pro 26:25 (vc=1694 — VCG-02): "seven abominations in his heart" behind gracious speech — the inner life becomes layered with multiple concurrent corrupt drives; (d) the accumulated weight of shame and disgrace — Eze 44:13 (vc=66003 — VCG-04): the abominations become an inner burden preventing sacred service.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Sustained possession of idolatrous abomination establishes: (a) constitutional transformation toward the image of idols — Hos 9:10 (vc=1632 — VCG-04): "became detestable like the thing they loved" — the person's inner character is re-shaped by sustained idolatrous attachment; (b) moral numbness toward the gravity of abomination — Eze 8:17 (vc=65980 — VCG-05): treating abomination as a light matter; (c) the suppression of covenantal memory — Eze 16:22 (vc=65985 — VCG-05): forgetting; Eze 16:43 (vc=65987 — VCG-05): failure to remember youth — the covenantal-gratitude memory is silenced; (d) an inverted affective delight — Isa 66:3 (vc=1633 — VCG-04): the soul delights in abominations rather than recoiling; (e) the acceleration of moral deterioration — Eze 16:47-48 (vc=65988 — VCG-05): "within a very little time you were more corrupt than they in all your ways" — the trajectory is one of deepening beyond comparable models.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Sustained possession of iniquity as active scheming establishes: (a) iniquity's dominion over the will — Psa 119:133 (vc=38227 — VCG-04): "let no iniquity get dominion over me" — the sustained inner presence of iniquity seeks to control the will's direction; (b) the old way of wicked men as an ingrained moral trajectory — Job 22:15 (vc=38210 — VCG-04): "the old way that wicked men have trod" — a worn inner path that becomes habitual and difficult to leave; (c) the inner capacity for self-deception about one's own iniquity — Pro 30:20 (vc=38222 — VCG-04): "I have done no wrong" — moral self-blindness as a settled orientation; (d) the severing of the prayer-relationship with God — Psa 66:18 (vc=38182 — VCG-04): cherished iniquity forecloses divine listening; (e) an appetite that actively seeks evil input — Pro 19:28 (vc=38220 — VCG-03): mouth devouring iniquity.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Sustained possession of evil expressed through speech establishes: (a) the hardened will as a fixed inner orientation — Rev 16:9/11/21 (VCG-01): across three separate divine judgments, the will maintains its defiant posture; the sustained characteristic has solidified the will against God; (b) the foreclosure of repentance — Rev 16:9 (VCG-01): "they did not repent"; Rev 16:11 (VCG-01): "they did not repent of their deeds" — sustained blasphemy has rendered the will incapable of the repentance that would reverse it; (c) contempt as the primary inner stance toward the divine and toward authority — Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): authority-rejection and glorious-ones-blasphemy as settled dispositions; (d) instinct-level operation without rational comprehension — Jude 10 (vc=14355 — VCG-01): "blaspheme all that they do not understand, destroyed by all that they… understand instinctively" — the characteristic has reduced operation to pre-rational instinct.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's six characteristics collectively document a shared set of sustained-possession consequences: (a) Moral blindness — inability to perceive the gravity or wrongness of the characteristic (Char 4: Eze 8:17 — treating abomination as trivial; Char 5: Psa 14:4 — no knowledge in evildoers; Char 6: Jude 10 — blaspheming what is not understood); (b) Inverted affective orientation — soul delighting in what should repulse it (Char 4: Isa 66:3 — soul delights in abominations; Char 5: Pro 19:28 — mouth devours iniquity); (c) Prayer foreclosure — the characteristic severs the divine-hearing relationship (Char 3: Pro 3:32 — excluded from divine confidence; Char 5: Psa 66:18 — cherished iniquity forecloses divine listening); (d) Self-reinforcing hardening — the characteristic entrenches itself through its own expression (Char 6 most extremely — Rev 16:9/11/21; Char 1 — Job 22:15 "the old way that wicked men have trod"). These four sustained-possession consequences are cross-cluster constants that together define the inner-being profile of the person fully constituted by M10b characteristics.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Sustained engagement with the ritual defilement-state establishes: (1) the orientation of sacral vigilance — the person habituated to the clean/unclean boundary becomes watchful over bodily actions, over what they touch, eat, and carry; (2) the capacity for discernment — the clean/unclean distinction is the base capacity on which more complex moral-spiritual perception builds (Lev 10:10, M10c-B-VCG-01); (3) the orientation of communal responsibility — the duty not to transmit one's state (Lev 15:11 M10c-A-VCG-06; the Lev 13:45 self-declaration requirement) forms the person in awareness of their relational impact; (4) humility before the body's creaturely vulnerability — the physiological defilement register (M10c-A-VCG-05: Lev 12 and Lev 15 menstrual) attaches defilement to natural processes, forming the person in acceptance of embodied limitation without moral shame; (5) dependence on prescribed remedy — the standing availability of cleansing (water of impurity, Num 19:9) forms the person in an orientation of ongoing reliance on divinely provided resolution.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Sustained moral-inner defilement establishes: (1) callousness — the progressive suppression of conscience (Eph 4:19, VCG-02: "become callous"); (2) lawlessness as an inner orientation — the will directed toward "lawlessness leading to more lawlessness" (Rom 6:19, VCG-02); (3) active moral appetite — "greedy to practice every kind of impurity" (Eph 4:19, VCG-02); (4) hardened will resistant to repentance — 2Cor 12:21 (VCG-02): those who "have not repented of the impurity... that they have practiced"; (5) a defiled cognitive-moral faculty — Tit 1:15 is cross-referenced at VCG-03: "to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; both their minds and their consciences are defiled." Over time the characteristic establishes an inner person in whom the faculties meant to orient the person toward God (conscience, mind, moral evaluation) are all compromised.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Sustained corporate/covenantal defilement establishes: (1) inability to approach God — Eze 20:31 (VCG-02): persistent self-defilement closes divine accessibility; (2) corporate moral blindness to the condition — Jer 2:23 (VCG-02): "I am not unclean" — the self-deceptive claim; (3) land rendered inhabitable — Mic 2:10 (VCG-04): "no place to rest, because of uncleanness"; (4) sacred space desecrated and eventually destroyed — Psa 79:1 (VCG-03): temple defiled and Jerusalem ruined; (5) the corporate name becoming a byword of defilement — Eze 22:5 (VCG-05): "your name is defiled"; (6) social expulsion from the covenant community and from the land (Lam 4:15, VCG-05; Hos 9:3, VCG-05: "they shall eat unclean food in Assyria").

**[CHAR-4]** E — Sustained possession establishes: (1) Total will-bondage without moral guilt — the person cannot break free (Luk 8:29 — breaking bonds yet "driven by the demon"); the will is externally overridden, not internally corrupted. (2) Communicative isolation — Mar 9:25 (VCG-01): "mute and deaf spirit" — sustained suppression of the communicative faculties enabling relationship with God and others. (3) Social-communal severance — Mar 5:2 (VCG-01): dwelling "among the tombs" in radical exclusion. (4) Bodily subjugation — the body becomes the instrument of the spirit's violent self-expression (convulsions — Luk 9:42; breaking chains — Luk 8:29; driven into the desert — Luk 8:29).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four sustained-state profiles together reveal the range of inner-being outcomes that sustained defilement produces. Characteristic 1 establishes (positively): sacral vigilance, active discernment capacity (Lev 10:10), communal responsibility, humility before embodied creaturely vulnerability (Lev 12/15), and dependence on prescribed divine remedy. Characteristic 2 establishes (negatively): callousness (Eph 4:19), lawlessness as inner orientation (Rom 6:19), active moral appetite for more defilement, hardened will resistant to repentance (2Cor 12:21), and defiled cognitive-moral faculty. Characteristic 3 establishes: inability to approach God (Eze 20:31), corporate moral blindness (Jer 2:23), land rendered uninhabitable (Mic 2:10), sacred space destroyed (Psa 79:1), corporate name as byword of defilement (Eze 22:5), social expulsion (Lam 4:15). Characteristic 4 establishes: total will-bondage without moral guilt (Luk 8:29), communicative isolation (Mar 9:25), social-communal severance (Mar 5:2), bodily subjugation (Luk 9:42). Cluster observation: Characteristic 1 is the only one producing positive inner-being capacities through sustained engagement. Characteristics 2-4 all produce uniformly negative states — and the negative states escalate across the cluster: from internal faculty corruption (Char 2) to communal-spatial destruction (Char 3) to total constitutional domination (Char 4).

questions.question_text: How does the sustained effect differ from the immediate response (T1.5)?

findings.session_b_note:
The data does not address this distinction explicitly. However, the evidence permits an observation:

The **immediate response** appears to be affective or relational in character — love (Luk 7:47), fear/reverence (Psa 130:4), blessedness (Rom 4:7). These are responses *to* the encounter with forgiveness.

The **sustained effect** appears to be constitutional and dispositional — the permanent condition of release (afesis), the established capacity for horizontal forgiveness, the sustained hope-orientation, the love-orientation that becomes a settled relational disposition.

The pattern suggested (though not named in the data): the immediate response is the inner-being *movement* at the moment of encounter; the sustained effect is the inner-being *state* that the movement establishes over time. The immediate love response (Luk 7:47) may become, with time, the settled relational disposition of readiness-to-give.

*New finding:* This distinction between immediate movement and sustained state is not assembled in the existing observations. The data implies it but does not name it. This is a potential Session D contribution — the temporal dimension of forgiveness's inner-being operation.

The sustained effects are constitutive — they rebuild and orient the inner person over time. This is not merely temporal but qualitative: the immediate response acknowledges what grace is; the sustained effect is what grace does to the person over time.

findings.finding_value: T1's distinction between immediate response and sustained effect (Q&A-030) maps precisely onto T5's two transformation sequences (Q&A-126). The immediate response pattern (trust, praise, receptive desire) corresponds to the initial stages of T5's positive arc (encounter → trust → refuge). The sustained effect (stable orientation, community capacity, settled disposition) corresponds to T5's later stages (reorientation → overflow → formation-agent capacity). Furthermore, T1's "sustained effect" (Q&A-028) identified stable inner orientation as the primary sustained product — T5 confirms this through the transformation to orientation change (Q&A-123) and the formation-agent role (Q&A-136). The two tiers read together reveal a temporal architecture for goodness: immediate contact produces first responses; sustained formation produces constitutive character; and the character-formed person becomes a formative resource for others.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-001: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanch…
findings.finding_value: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved), condition of its object (eleeinos — the pitiable state that calls compassion forth), and externalised act (almsgiving, mercy-act). No other characteristic in the programme review set operates across all four kinds simultaneously. The four root families (RACHAM, CHASAD, SPLANCHN, OIKTIROM) identify four constituent dimensions of the single characteristic, each naming a distinct register — somatic-maternal, covenantal-relational, visceral-immediate, and deliberative-pitying respectively. The structural opposites are two distinct kinds: willed judicial hardness (the hardened heart that refuses compassion) and unwilled prosperity-blindness (Eze 16:49 — the one who does not see the need because they are satiated). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed by the consistent outward-facing structure: compassion cannot exist without a suffering other. The definitional tier's most critical gap — the receiver's inner-being experience — is entirely absent from the data, affecting T1.5, T1.6, and T1.7 throughout. This gap is the single most significant analytical absence in the registry.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-011: T1's sustained-effect analysis (largely P-rated because the receiver's inner-being experience is absent) and T5's formation arc together reveal a gap that is structurally significant: the formation pr…
findings.finding_value: T1's sustained-effect analysis (largely P-rated because the receiver's inner-being experience is absent) and T5's formation arc together reveal a gap that is structurally significant: the formation process from single compassion-event to compassion-character is the most important untraced developmental relationship in the registry. T5 provides the directional finding (the formative cycle feeds back from after-state to before-state) and names the three mechanisms (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological). T1 provides the definitional starting point (compassion as character quality is the endpoint of formation). Together they frame an arc that is identified but not filled: how does the moment of splanchnizō (T1 inner-event) accumulate into the settled character of ra.chum (T1 character quality)? T5's mechanisms suggest the answer but the data does not trace the path explicitly — a gap confirmed by both tiers.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-001: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition of being in favour — charis as inhabited state), enabling capacity (the specific power given for specific tasks — 2Cor 12:9), and character quality (gracious speech, gracious conduct — chen in 889-003). No single English equivalent captures all four. The four modes of operation (sovereign bestowal, covenantal-relational sustaining, capacity-conferring, character-forming) correspond to the four kinds without collapsing them. Two structural opposites are identified: pride (the self-elevation that refuses the favour of the greater, active and willed) and ingratitude/gracelessness (acharistos — the failure to register and respond to grace received, which T3 confirms as image-impairment). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed throughout: grace is constitutively directional — it flows from the greater to the lesser and requires the receptor's inner-being engagement to complete its operation.

The sustained effects are primarily constitutional and relational: character formation (love, goodness), deepened capacity (compassion, comfort), stable inner orientation (gentleness, hope), and transformed identity (koinōnos in divine nature). **[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — immediate response is guilt-acknowledgment or confident appeal; sustained effect is the development of proclamation capacity (A1-005) and the orientation of the community around testimony to divine righteousness. From immediate recognition to sustained witness.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — immediate response is gladness (3246-003); sustained effect is rootedness and recognisable path (A2-013; A2-017). Immediate joy develops into structural stability.
**[B — Moral Uprightness]** B is silent on immediate response, so the comparison cannot be made here.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — immediate response to justification is hope (Tit 3:7); sustained effect is the development of the heir-identity and increasing freedom from condemnation. The hope of the immediate becomes the identity of the sustained.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — immediate response to God answering the cry for justice is relief and worship (Rev 19:2). Sustained effect of entrusting vengeance to God is the development of the non-retaliatory posture (Rom 12:19).

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — immediate response to freedom from condemnation is release (Joh 8:10–11). Sustained effect is the conscience freed from its condemning voice and the capacity for obedience that freedom makes possible.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — immediate response to reckoning is action (Rom 6:11–12); sustained effect is the development of theological perception and the capacity for endurance under suffering (Rom 8:18). The act becomes capacity over time.
**[G — Structural Opposites]** Silent on immediate response; sustained effect is hardness (Rom 2:5).

**[CLUSTER]** Pattern: immediate response is specific and often affective (guilt, joy, hope, release, action); sustained effect is structural and developmental (rootedness, proclamation, heir-identity, non-retaliation, theological perception). Righteousness is not a momentary experience but a shaping force that develops the inner person over time.

findings.finding_value: The clearest borders: (1) Grace/mercy border: the cha.nan root generates both the grace vocabulary (chen, charis) and the supplication vocabulary (tachanum, techinah — seeking mercy). The border is functional: grace is the disposition of the giving side; mercy is the specific response to need/guilt on the receiving side. In many verses both are present simultaneously; the border is porous. (2) Grace/works border: Rom 11:6 draws the sharpest border in the NT — grace and works are mutually exclusive soteriological modes, even if they coexist in the same person experientially. (3) Favour/election border: chen/favour (889-001) and divine election sometimes overlap (Exo 33:12 — "I know you by name and you have found favour in my sight"). The favour is the form of the elect relationship, but not identical with the election itself.

findings.finding_value: The most significant sustained-vs-immediate divergence is in M46-A: the immediate experience of material abundance is pleasure (eating, being filled, delighting — Neh 9:25 with a.dan); the sustained effect is inner closure and apostasy (Neh 9:26 — they were disobedient and rebelled). The immediate is positive; the sustained effect is harmful. This divergence is the core dynamic of M46-A: what feels like abundance and satiation in the moment produces inner deterioration over time. The same divergence applies in M46-B: the immediate experience of wealth accumulation may feel like security (hon as strong city, Pro 18:11); the sustained effect is insatiability, grief, and hardness. For M46-D, the immediate-sustained relationship is a progression: immediate joy in voluntary release → sustained capacity for paradoxical richness in poverty.
