(1) *Personal inner commitment to the sinful course*: 1Ki 16:26 — "walked in all the way of Jeroboam" — the leader must be internally committed to the sinning direction; they cannot transmit what they do not themselves hold. (2) *Occupation of the authority position*: 1Ki 16:2 — "I exalted you out of the dust and made you leader over my people Israel" — the authority position is what makes the inner commitment's transmission effective. The same inner sinning commitment in a non-leader produces personal sinning (CHAR-1/5/6) rather than contagious sin. (3) *Active exercise of leadership toward the sinning direction*: 2Ki 17:21 — "Jeroboam drove Israel from following the Lord" — the active exercise of leadership energy in the sinning direction is the causative mechanism. Passive personal sinning without leadership-directed transmission does not produce CHAR-7.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Two evidenced enabling conditions. (1) *Perceived weakness of governing authority*: 2Ki 1:1 and 3:5 — both Moab revolts occur "after the death of Ahab" — the death of the strong authority figure creates the enabling condition for revolt; the perceived weakness of the successor authority makes revolt viable. (2) *Spiritual-authority vacuum in the governing authority*: 2Ch 21:10 — "because he had forsaken the Lord" — Jehoram's forsaking of God creates a spiritual-moral vacancy that enables the revolts of Edom and Libnah; when the governing authority has abandoned the spiritual foundation of legitimate rule, the subject peoples revolt.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Three enabling conditions. (1) *Corrupt heart*: Mat 15:19 — "out of the heart come evil thoughts... slander" — the corrupted heart is the primary enabling condition; (2) *Conceit and diseased craving*: 1Ti 6:4 — "puffed up with conceit... unhealthy craving for controversy" — pride and the appetite for controversy enable slander; (3) *Unbelief*: 1Ti 1:13 — Paul's former blasphemy arose from "ignorant unbelief" — the absence of saving knowledge of God removes the constraint against blasphemy. VCG-03's beast is the extreme form: total anti-God orientation as the constitutive enabling condition for constitutive blasphemy.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence is not framed around "receiving" wickedness as though it is something bestowed. The question is better addressed as: what inner conditions enable the settling of this characteristic in a person? The evidence suggests: (a) the pre-existing exclusion of God from the mind (Psa 10:4 — the wicked's practical atheism pre-exists and enables the settled orientation); (b) the abandonment of counsel from the righteous (Psa 1:1 — alignment with wicked counsel); (c) the decision to enter "the path of the wicked" (Pro 4:14 — VCG-07 — wickedness is entered as a path); (d) the silencing of the internal voice of God-fear (Psa 36:1 — the replacement of God-fear with transgression's voice is the enabling inner event). The characteristic settles where the God-orientation of the inner person has been abandoned.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The question "reception" is analytically unusual for this characteristic since it is framed as a constitutional baseline condition rather than something received from outside. The evidence addresses the conditions under which the characteristic deepens and consolidates rather than its initial reception. Deepening conditions: (1) the absence of faith — Heb 3:12 (vc=14423 — VCG-06): the evil, unbelieving heart leads to apostasy; (2) the absence of the received word — Jam 1:21 (vc=14368 — VCG-05): rampant wickedness must be stripped away before the word can take root — the presence of wickedness blocks reception of the word, and presumably the absence of the word enables the wickedness to consolidate; (3) vacated inner space — Mat 12:45 (vc=65879 — VCG-06): the swept but unoccupied inner space invites deeper evil; (4) self-seeking and obedience to unrighteousness — Rom 2:8 (vc=14338 — VCG-05): the self-seeking person who "does not obey the truth but obeys unrighteousness" is in a state enabling the characteristic's deepening.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic is not primarily a received condition but an inner moral condition that develops from within. The enabling conditions for its development are: (1) the prior erosion or silencing of the conscience — Jer 6:15 (vc=1680 — VCG-04) describes the state where conscience has already been silenced, which is both a symptom and an enabling condition for further abomination; (2) the crooked heart as a settled inner condition — Pro 11:20 (vc=1677 — VCG-01) and Pro 3:32 (vc=1686 — VCG-02): the devious inner orientation enables the specific inner qualities named as abominable; (3) the absence of hearing the law — Pro 28:9 (vc=65958 — VCG-03): "if one turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination" — the deliberate rejection of divine instruction opens the person to abominable inner conditions by removing the corrective that would otherwise check them; (4) the absence of discernment — Isa 44:19 (vc=65961 — VCG-05): no consideration, no knowledge or discernment allows abomination without recognition.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The enabling conditions for idolatrous abomination to take root are: (1) proximity to peoples who practice it — Deu 20:18 (vc=65932 — VCG-02): the nations "may not teach you to do according to all their abominable practices" — proximity and relational exposure enables reception; (2) the absence of active covenant separation — Ezr 9:1 (vc=65949 — VCG-03): failure to separate from peoples with abominations opens the inner person to their influence; (3) the coveting of what is attractive in the idol — Deu 7:25 (vc=1682 — VCG-02): "you shall not covet the silver or gold on them or take it for yourselves, lest you be ensnared by it" — inner coveting of what is on the idol is the mechanism of reception; (4) marital-relational entanglement — Ezr 9:14 (vc=65950 — VCG-03): intermarriage with abomination-practicing peoples as the relational channel through which inner attachment is received.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The enabling conditions are: (1) chosen association with evildoers — Job 34:8 (vc=38214 — VCG-04): "who travels in company with evildoers and walks with wicked men" — chosen relational proximity shapes inner character toward iniquity; Psa 141:4 (vc=38230 — VCG-04): the prayer against "busy myself with wicked deeds in company with men who work iniquity" shows that association is the primary entry vector; (2) the heart's susceptibility to incline — Psa 141:4 (vc=38230 — VCG-04): "do not let my heart incline to any evil" — the heart's inclination capacity is what is at risk; (3) the will's preference for iniquity over affliction — Job 36:21 (vc=38216 — VCG-04): "this you have chosen rather than affliction" — volitional choice of the easier/more attractive iniquitous path over the hard righteous one; (4) the absence of active volitional resistance — Psa 119:133 (vc=38227 — VCG-04): the prayer for steadiness implies its absence would enable reception.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The enabling inner conditions for generating evil expressed through speech: (1) the hardened will that refuses to yield to divine authority — Rev 16:9/11/21 (VCG-01): the will hardened against repentance enables defiant blasphemy; (2) the rejection of legitimate authority — Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): "relying on their dreams, they reject authority and blaspheme the glorious ones" — authority-rejection is the enabling inner condition for the blasphemous expression; (3) incomprehension — Jude 10 (vc=14355 — VCG-01): "blaspheme all that they do not understand" — the absence of cognitive understanding leaves contempt as the inner substitute; (4) moral failure in those representing God — Rom 2:24 (vc=14357 — VCG-02): moral failure enables the social defamation of God's name; (5) malicious hostile evaluation of another — Joh 18:30 (vc=14378 — VCG-03): the accusers' inner evaluation ("if this man were not doing evil") enables the false charge.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals enabling conditions at two levels: constitutional and relational-associational. At the constitutional level: the absence of conscience engagement (all six characteristics — the conscience as the primary internal block whose absence enables reception), and the heart's susceptibility to incline (Char 5: Psa 141:4 — "do not let my heart incline to any evil"). At the relational-associational level: chosen proximity to evildoers (Char 5: Job 34:8 — travels in company with evildoers; Char 1 implied by Psa 1:1 — "walks in the counsel of the wicked"). Char 4 adds the visual-desire mechanism (Eze 20:7-8 — eyes feasting on idol-objects as the entry mechanism). Char 6 adds the authority-rejection precondition (Jude 8 — "relying on their dreams, they… reject authority and blaspheme"). Char 2 adds the constitutional fallen condition as the background enabling condition (Mat 7:11 — "you who are evil" as the pre-existing state from which further evil reception flows). The cluster reveals that reception of inner evil requires: absent conscience + susceptible heart + wrong association + specific triggering conditions unique to each characteristic.

**[CHAR-1]** E — "Reception" is an unusual frame for a defilement-state; the characteristic is typically incurred rather than received. But if the question is read as: what inner conditions enable the person to recognise, respond to, and resolve the defilement appropriately — the evidence is clear. Three inner conditions enable the full reception of the characteristic's normative function: (1) conscience-alertness: the capacity to recognise when guilt surfaces (Lev 5:2-3, M10c-A-VCG-01 — the person who "comes to know it" and responds); (2) will-alignment with the sacral order: willingness to pursue remedy through appointed means (washing, waiting, examination, water of impurity); and (3) formed discernment: the cultivated ability to distinguish clean from unclean (Lev 10:10, 11:47, M10c-B-VCG-01), which enables one to recognise the defilement-state correctly when it is incurred.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Three enabling inner conditions are evidenced. (1) Unchecked desire: Rom 1:24 (VCG-02) — impurity arises from "lusts of their hearts" that have been given rein through the prior rejection of God. The enabling condition is desire without governance. (2) Silenced or weak conscience: Eph 4:19 (VCG-02) — callousness precedes the giving over to impurity; 1Cor 8:7 (VCG-03) — the conscience is weak and can be defiled when the person acts against it without genuine conviction. The enabling condition is a conscience that cannot hold the person to moral standards. (3) Former association with idols or morally corrupted environments: 1Cor 8:7 (VCG-03) — "through former association with idols, eat food as really offered to an idol" — the context of formation shapes susceptibility to defilement of conscience. Association with what defiles enables defilement.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Three enabling inner conditions are evidenced. (1) Sustained unfaithfulness of the corporate will: 2Ch 36:14 (VCG-03) — "exceedingly unfaithful, following all the abominations of the nations" — habitual corporate unfaithfulness is the primary enabling condition. (2) Desire-driven idolatrous lust: Eze 23:7 (VCG-02) — "she defiled herself with all the idols of everyone after whom she lusted" — unchecked corporate desire for what lies outside the covenant is the engine. (3) Deliberate will-act of desecration: Jer 7:30 (VCG-03) — the sons of Judah "set their detestable things in the house that is called by my name, to defile it" — the will's deliberate choice to install what defiles in the sacred space. The enabling condition is thus the corporate will turned away from God and toward idolatrous attachment, desire, and deliberate desecration.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 21-verse corpus does not evidence specific inner conditions in the affected person that enable reception. The characteristic is imposed externally by the spirit's own agency without requiring a cooperating inner condition. Possessed persons include a child (Mar 7:25, Luk 9:42), an unnamed man in a synagogue (Mar 1:23), and a man among tombs (Mar 5:2) — no common inner enabling conditions are identified. This is analytically significant: the absence of inner-enabling conditions distinguishes Characteristic 4 structurally from Characteristics 2 and 3.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four enabling-condition profiles reveal a fundamental structural division within the cluster. Characteristics 1, 2, and 3 each identify specific inner enabling conditions, while Characteristic 4 does not. Characteristic 1's enabling conditions: conscience-alertness (capacity to recognise the incurred defilement — Lev 5:2-3), will-alignment with the sacral order (willingness to pursue remedy), and formed discernment (cultivated ability to distinguish clean from unclean — Lev 10:10). Characteristic 2's enabling conditions: unchecked desire (lusts of the heart — Rom 1:24), silenced or weak conscience (Eph 4:19, 1Cor 8:7), and former association with defiling environments (1Cor 8:7). Characteristic 3's enabling conditions: sustained unfaithfulness of the corporate will (2Ch 36:14), desire-driven idolatrous lust (Eze 23:7), and deliberate will-act of desecration (Jer 7:30). Characteristic 4: no inner enabling conditions evidenced — the characteristic is imposed externally without cooperating inner conditions. The cluster's structural division: Characteristics 1, 2, and 3 all have inner-enabling conditions that make the person susceptible or responsive. Characteristic 4 has none. This confirms Characteristic 4 as uniquely external in mechanism: the other three characteristics are received or engaged through the person's own inner constitution; Characteristic 4 is imposed regardless of the person's inner state.

questions.question_text: Under what inner conditions is the characteristic blocked, distorted, resisted, or not taken up — including, where the evidence shows it, distortion or interference by another spirit (adversarial or angelic)?

findings.session_b_note:
Q030 answer addresses resistance sources directly:

1. **Religious authority misused:** Mar 2:7 — the scribes resist Jesus's act of forgiveness on theological grounds ("who can forgive sins but God alone?"). Misunderstanding of divine prerogative blocks recognition of forgiveness when it is present.

2. **Structural incoherence:** Mat 18:35 — the servant who received forgiveness but resists extending it. The failure to receive at the heart level what was received at the verbal/legal level.

3. **Volitional refusal:** Mat 6:15 — the person who chooses not to forgive others thereby closes themselves to receiving forgiveness. The connection is structural: withholding blocks reception.

4. **Obstruction of others' access:** Mat 23:13 — "you shut the kingdom of heaven in people's faces." The Pharisaic pattern of blocking access rather than opening it.

5. **The outer limit:** Mar 3:29 — blasphemy against the Spirit as the permanent blocking condition. The Spirit's work is permanently rejected; the inner openness through which forgiveness is received is permanently closed (OBS-064-024).

findings.session_b_note:
The data is relatively explicit here, yielding two distinct blocking conditions:

**Self-sufficiency and prosperity-blindness (Rev 3:17, SD-015):** The Laodicean condition — "I am rich, I have prospered, I need nothing" — is named as the precise inner state that prevents recognition of the pitiable condition. Self-enclosed prosperity is identified as an inner orientation that renders the person incapable of perceiving their own need. If need-recognition is the condition for receiving compassion, then its absence (self-sufficiency) is the primary blocking condition.

**Judicial hardness — the deliberately closed eye (H2347 chus):** The prohibition contexts ("your eye shall not pity") reveal that the impulse toward compassion can be deliberately overridden. While these are primarily divine-judicial or legal contexts, they reveal a structural reality: the inner movement toward compassion can be closed by an act of will oriented toward judgment rather than mercy. Applied to the receiving side, a person oriented primarily toward justice and merit — expecting to receive what one deserves — may block the reception of compassion by treating it as inappropriate or unearned.

findings.session_b_note:
- **Idolatrous joining:** Hos 4:17 — when the joining capacity is misdirected toward idols, divine fellowship is foreclosed. God's response is abandonment (*leave him alone*), suggesting that the block is not merely behavioural but relational at the deepest level.
- **Moral incompatibility:** 2Cor 6:14 — the person whose inner orientation is toward lawlessness or darkness cannot receive righteous fellowship. The incompatibility blocks reception structurally, not merely circumstantially.
- **Faithlessness:** Mal 2:14 — faithlessness toward the covenant companion violates and distorts the fellowship bond. The faithless disposition blocks sustained genuine fellowship.
- **Hardened character:** Jer 13:23 — the leopard-spots image (group 7573-001) suggests that character deeply conformed to evil resists the kind of change that would enable righteous fellowship reception. This operates at the level of character fixity rather than momentary choice.

findings.session_b_note: Four blocking conditions (SBF-067-Q028): (1) Self-direction — "following their own devices" (Isa 65:2). Inner sovereignty-of-self is incompatible with receiving goodness from outside the self. (2) Wilful refusal — "we will not walk in it" (Jer 6:16). The will's active rejection of the good way — not ignorance but resistance. (3) Moral self-justification / redefinition — Jer 44:17 / Mal 2:17: redefining goodness as what serves one's advantage inverts the assessment faculty and closes off recognition of genuine goodness. (4) Departure from faith/trust — Rom 11:22: "otherwise you too will be cut off" — departure from the faith-relationship with God closes off ongoing experience of divine chrēstotēs. The progression: self-direction → wilful refusal → moral redefinition → departure represents an escalating closure of the inner being to goodness. (OBS-067-OBS-028, OBS-067-OBS-043, OBS-067-OBS-044, SBF-067-Q028)

findings.session_b_note: The data names several inner blockers: (a) **love of darkness** — Joh 3:19 (OBS-103-147): the inner orientation toward darkness is the condition that prevents reception of love-as-light. The person who loves the darkness does not receive the light; the blocker is the prior love-commitment to a wrong object. (b) **love of money** — 1Ti 6:10 (OBS-103-132): love of money causes departure from faith — the love of a wrong object displaces the reception of divine love. (c) **pride/self-seeking** — 1Cor 13:4-7 (OBS-103-127): love of self expressed as arrogance and self-seeking is explicitly named as what love is not — the self-orientation blocks the other-orientation that genuine love requires. (d) **false-brotherhood orientation** — Gal 2:4 (OBS-103-068): the concealed inner agenda of the false brother prevents genuine love-reception within the community. The pattern: all inner blockers are disordered loves — prior commitments to wrong objects that displace the capacity for rightly directed love.

findings.session_b_note: The data addresses blocking of mercy's extension rather than its reception more directly. Mercilessness blocks the receipt of mercy (Jam 2:13 — "judgment without mercy to one who has shown no mercy," OBS-111-070). Taking a bribe (*kopher* as bribe, 1Sa 12:3) corrupts the mercy-mechanism by redirecting it toward injustice (OBS-111-044). What blocks reception of mercy in a willing God remains less clearly addressed — the data is richer on the posture of the seeking person than on what prevents them from receiving. The gap is whether pride, self-sufficiency, or unrepentance is named as blocking reception. OBS-111-044, OBS-111-070.

findings.finding_value: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved), condition of its object (eleeinos — the pitiable state that calls compassion forth), and externalised act (almsgiving, mercy-act). No other characteristic in the programme review set operates across all four kinds simultaneously. The four root families (RACHAM, CHASAD, SPLANCHN, OIKTIROM) identify four constituent dimensions of the single characteristic, each naming a distinct register — somatic-maternal, covenantal-relational, visceral-immediate, and deliberative-pitying respectively. The structural opposites are two distinct kinds: willed judicial hardness (the hardened heart that refuses compassion) and unwilled prosperity-blindness (Eze 16:49 — the one who does not see the need because they are satiated). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed by the consistent outward-facing structure: compassion cannot exist without a suffering other. The definitional tier's most critical gap — the receiver's inner-being experience — is entirely absent from the data, affecting T1.5, T1.6, and T1.7 throughout. This gap is the single most significant analytical absence in the registry.

findings.finding_value: T1's sustained-effect analysis (largely P-rated because the receiver's inner-being experience is absent) and T5's formation arc together reveal a gap that is structurally significant: the formation process from single compassion-event to compassion-character is the most important untraced developmental relationship in the registry. T5 provides the directional finding (the formative cycle feeds back from after-state to before-state) and names the three mechanisms (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological). T1 provides the definitional starting point (compassion as character quality is the endpoint of formation). Together they frame an arc that is identified but not filled: how does the moment of splanchnizō (T1 inner-event) accumulate into the settled character of ra.chum (T1 character quality)? T5's mechanisms suggest the answer but the data does not trace the path explicitly — a gap confirmed by both tiers.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-001: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition of being in favour — charis as inhabited state), enabling capacity (the specific power given for specific tasks — 2Cor 12:9), and character quality (gracious speech, gracious conduct — chen in 889-003). No single English equivalent captures all four. The four modes of operation (sovereign bestowal, covenantal-relational sustaining, capacity-conferring, character-forming) correspond to the four kinds without collapsing them. Two structural opposites are identified: pride (the self-elevation that refuses the favour of the greater, active and willed) and ingratitude/gracelessness (acharistos — the failure to register and respond to grace received, which T3 confirms as image-impairment). The immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response before positive states settle) is a T1.5 finding confirming that grace does not bypass creaturely recognition but requires and produces it as a transitional state. The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed throughout: grace is constitutively directional — it flows from the greater to the lesser and requires the receptor's inner-being engagement to complete its operation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-011: T1's sustained-effect finding (immediate/sustained contrast as qualitative, not merely temporal — what grace does immediately is creaturely recognition; what it does over time is constitution of ident…
findings.finding_value: T1's sustained-effect finding (immediate/sustained contrast as qualitative, not merely temporal — what grace does immediately is creaturely recognition; what it does over time is constitution of identity and character) maps onto T5's formation mechanisms. The encounter mechanism (T5) produces the immediate effects named in T1.5; the word, inference, and mediated-transformation mechanisms (T5) produce the sustained effects of T1.6. T5's five mechanisms collectively explain how the four kinds named in T1.2 are produced across different temporal and contextual registers: disposition-receipt is the encounter mechanism; standing is the spirit-outpouring mechanism; capacity is the mediated-transformation mechanism; character quality is the sustained word-and-inference mechanism. T1 names what is produced; T5 names how each kind is produced.

findings.session_b_note: The data reveals a causal structure governing the degree of shalom: (1) Orientation of the mind toward God (Isa 26:3 — "you keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you, because he trusts in you") — the directing of the mind toward God produces perfect peace; (2) Love of God's law (Psa 119:165 — "great peace have those who love your law") — orientation toward God's word produces great peace; (3) Righteous character (Isa 32:17 — "the effect of righteousness will be peace") — the degree of shalom follows from the degree of righteousness; (4) Trust (Psa 4:8, Isa 30:15) — trust is the inner act that enables peace's reception; (5) The absence of stubbornness/self-deception (Deu 29:19, Jer 23:17) — the factors that reduce shalom are the absence of trust and the presence of self-deception. The causal structure: covenant faithfulness → trust → orientation toward God → peace. Each factor contributes; disruption at any point reduces the degree of shalom available.

findings.session_b_note: Two blocking conditions are evidenced. (1) Faithlessness/covenant violation blocks covenantal giving and produces judicial giving-over instead — the movement from 872-001 (covenantal giving) to 872-004 (judicial giving-over) is precisely the consequence of Israel's faithlessness (OBS-060-021, OBS-060-043). The inner condition of persistent covenant violation does not merely delay the giving — it inverts it into giving-over. (2) Misattribution/idolatry blocks proper reception: Hos 2:8 (group 872-002 non-anchor verse) shows that Israel received God's grain, wine, and oil and attributed them to Baal — the reception occurred but was distorted by misattribution to wrong source. The inner condition of idolatrous misattribution prevents the giving from being received in its true character (as an expression of divine faithfulness and love) even when the material gift is received. For human giving: the absence of inner orientation (giving from compulsion or obligation rather than from inner commitment) is not explicitly addressed in the anchor verses, but the group descriptions consistently name inner orientation as constitutive of the giving — its absence would constitute a distortion.

Love as the primary blocking condition: Pro 10:12 — "love covers all offences" — what could become the seed of hatred is covered rather than nursed. Lev 19:17's command to frank confrontation prevents the inner settlement of hatred by keeping the relational channel open.

Fear of the Lord blocks contempt (Mal 1:6 — its absence is what makes contempt possible). The posture of openness to formation blocks contempt of reproof (Pro 15:5 — "whoever heeds reproof is prudent").

The enabling condition for righteous abhorrence (love of what is good) simultaneously blocks its inversion. Sustained immersion in what is true and good sharpens the moral recoil from its opposite rather than dulling it.

Fear of God (setting God before oneself) blocks ruthlessness (Psa 54:3's diagnostic by implication). Mercy and kindness as settled character qualities (Pro 11:17) block cruelty. The righteous person's regard for life (Pro 12:10) prevents the cruel pattern.

Relationship with God as the source of identity and worth: Isa 51:7 — "you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; fear not the reproach of man." The identity established in God cannot be overwritten by the social designation of reproach.
Having an advocate who can contend on one's behalf (Exo 23:22, Isa 49:25) makes the adversary relationship bearable and resistible.

Compassion for the other — the genuine capacity to be pained by another's suffering blocks the development of pleasure in it. The prior conditions (enmity and contempt) being blocked would prevent malice from developing its compound form.

The primary blocking condition for all agent-side M06 characteristics is the same: love of what is good + fear of the Lord + relational accountability. This complex provides the structural barrier to the entire cluster. The verse evidence is consistent: where these are present and active, the M06 characteristics cannot take permanent root.
Disordered love (love of darkness rather than light — Joh 3:19 — Group 1565); love of the world as rival to love of the Father (1Jo 2:15 — Group 1565).

Hardness that refuses to be moved (the judicial-withholding of compassion — Ezekiel's "eye shall not pity" — Groups 338, 630 — but this is appropriate judicial withholding, not a blocking of reception).
Having received mercy but withholding it — the unforgiving servant's condition (Mat 18:33 — Group 1630) blocks the mercy-economy from operating through him.
Hardness and impenitent heart in response to divine kindness (Rom 2:4-5 — Group 1111 context); the presumption that treats kindness as permission rather than invitation.
Pride/haughtiness (Pro 18:12 — Group 1272 — "before destruction a man's heart is haughty"); the contentious spirit (2Ti 2:24 — Group 867 contrast).
Refusal of comfort — Gen 37:35 (Group 1741) — Jacob "refused to be comforted"; Psa 77:2 (Group 1741) — "my soul refuses to be comforted." An active inner determination not to receive.
Walking in darkness while claiming fellowship (1Jo 1:6 — Group 1055); fundamental moral incompatibility (2Cor 6:14 — Group 1056).
[Sub-group not separately addressed in source — see cluster-level finding for this prompt]

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Pride and self-sufficiency — the attempt to establish one's own righteousness (Rom 10:3). Human anger — "the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God" (Jam 1:20) — the inner condition of wrath distorts the capacity to receive what is right.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Self-trust — trusting in accumulated righteousness (Eze 33:13). The distortion of M26-A2-003 (counterfeit and failure) — presenting the appearance of righteousness without the inner reality.
**[B — Moral Uprightness]** The demand for smooth things instead of what is right (Isa 30:10, VSG 1214-001). Crookedness — the habitual orientation toward devious paths (Pro 2:15).

**[C — Justification]** Self-justification by law — "severed from Christ, you who would be justified by the law" (Gal 5:4). The inner condition of trust in self-generated righteousness blocks reception of justification.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** The impulse toward personal autonomous vengeance (Rom 12:19: "never avenge yourselves") blocks the right orientation of D. Impatience with God's timing (the widow's persistence implies the temptation to give up rather than trust).

**[E — Condemnation]** Hypocrisy — "you condemn yourself, because you, the judge, practice the very same things" (Rom 2:1, VSG 4846-002). The hypocritical inner condition distorts the reception of condemnation-as-verdict.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Doubt — "whoever has doubts is condemned if he eats, because the eating is not from faith" (Rom 14:23). Partial or prejudiced reckoning (the opposite of adiakritos impartiality) distorts the reckoning outcome.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Wickedness itself blocks all reception: the hard and impenitent heart (Rom 2:5) is the inner condition that makes reception of righteousness impossible without repentance.

**[CLUSTER]** The blocking conditions: pride, self-trust, preference for comfort over truth, self-justification, autonomous vengeance-impulse, hypocrisy, doubt. The cluster reveals that the conditions blocking righteousness are not primarily external constraints but inner orientations.
Self-sufficiency (VCG06: Pro 26:12 — wise in own eyes); worldly orientation (VCG07: 1Cor 1:21).

findings.finding_value: In M01-A, reception is blocked by: (1) a hardened heart — Isa 63:17 ("God himself has hardened their heart so that they do not fear him"); (2) a divided heart — Psa 86:11; (3) false-object attachment — 2Ki 17 corpus (fear misplaced on other gods blocks genuine fear-of-God); (4) external compliance without inner reality — Isa 29:13 ("hollow fear — learned external formula with no inner reality"); (5) pride and self-reliance — Pro 3:7 (fear-of-God set against self-reliant pride); (6) accumulated sinful patterns — Jer 3:8 ("Judah did not fear despite witnessing Israel's divorce-judgment — a will hardened against the corrective lesson before her").

M01-B's disordering of acute fear is blocked or distorted by: prior experience producing distrust (Act 9:26: Jerusalem disciples' fear of Saul based on his history), misidentification (Mat 14:26: disciples misidentify Jesus as a ghost, generating fear), and the crowd's conspiratorial social fear that displaces genuine fear-of-God (Isa 8:12: "inner disposition of communal dread that distorts perception of true danger").

M01-G's ordered courage is blocked by: insufficient investment in the spirit of power, love, and self-control (2Ti 1:7 implies that the blocking condition is the failure to stir up the gift God has given — 2Ti 1:6 context).

Reception of ordered fear (M01-A) is blocked by hardened hearts, divided allegiance, pride, accumulated sin, and the substitution of external compliance for inner reality. These are consistent with the programme's finding across other M-clusters that the heart's integrity is the primary enabling/blocking factor for inner-being characteristics.

The restraint corpus shows that God's compassion blocks the full expression of his warranted rage: Psa 78:38 (M02-B-VCG-05) — God repeatedly holds back because compassion modifies the release of wrath. The blocking condition for divine rage is divine mercy.
Human wrath is blocked by inner governance: Jam 1:19 (M02-A-VCG-04) prescribes slowness to anger as a deliberate inner discipline — the blocking condition is the practice of restraint.
The Proverbs envy warnings (Pro 23:17; 24:1; M02-E-VCG-04) show that the will, properly directed toward fearing God, blocks covetous jealousy — the blocking condition is active will-redirection.

Three types of blocking conditions are evidenced. (1) Hardness of inner state: the Corinthians' arrogance blocked the mourning that was appropriate (1Cor 5:2 — M03-B-VCG-04); Jesus's grief at the Pharisees' hardness of heart (Mar 3:5 — M03-C-VCG-02) names hardness as the condition that produces grief in the one who sees it rather than the one who has it. (2) Pride and self-deception: Babylon's boast that she will never see mourning marks spiritual blindness (Rev 18:7 — M03-B-VCG-04). (3) Distraction by wealth or worldly investment: the rich young man's inability to follow through his grief (Mat 19:22; Mar 10:22 — M03-C-VCG-01) shows wealth's attachment blocking grief from producing action; merchants weep over Babylon from self-interest rather than genuine inner orientation (Rev 18:11 — M03-A-VCG-05). (4) Performative substitution: the weeping at the altar in Mal 2:13 (M03-A-VCG-02) is outward performance without genuine inner repentance — a distorted form of the characteristic.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Conditions that block or distort: (1) **unfaithfulness to God** — Hos 9:1 prohibits rejoicing precisely because Israel has "played the whore, forsaking your God"; their inner joy is illegitimate; (2) **idolatrous attachment** — Hos 10:5 shows exultation in an idol produces eventual mourning when the idol fails; (3) **directing exultation at evil** — Pro 2:14 shows those who "rejoice in doing evil" — the characteristic operating in a corrupted form; (4) **extremity of suffering** — Job 3:6–7 shows that overwhelming anguish can make even the capacity for joy seem impossible; though notably Hab 3:18 demonstrates the will can recover exultation even in extreme loss.

(2) *Fear of God*: 1Ti 5:20 — "so that the rest may stand in fear" — the fear of God (or fear of judgment) that public rebuke aims to produce in the community is the deterrent against persistent refusal. (3) *Receiving and acting on the knowledge of truth*: Heb 10:26 — the person who has received knowledge of truth and acts on it rather than continuing to sin.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The blocking conditions from the corpus: (1) *Abiding in Christ*: 1Jo 3:6 — "no one who abides in him keeps on sinning" — the abiding relationship with Christ is the primary structural preventive against habitual defection. (2) *Pleasing God*: Ecc 7:26 — "he who pleases God escapes her" — the inner disposition of God-pleasing (God-orientation) enables escape from the entrapment that habitual defection produces. (3) *Responsive listening*: 1Sa 2:25 — the blocking condition opposite to "they would not listen" is responsive hearing of the corrective voice; hearing and responding to God and his representatives.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Reception-enabling conditions: (1) *Dependence on the authority figure*: the community's reception of the transmitted sin is enabled by their structural position under the leader's authority — they receive what the leader transmits because the leader is their authority; (2) *Absence of independent God-orientation strong enough to resist*: Exo 23:33 — the warning implies that without the protective boundary (removing foreign nations), the community will be vulnerable to sin-transmission through influence. Reception-blocking conditions: 2Ki 23:15 — Josiah's response shows that a leader whose inner commitment is to God can reverse the transmission by dismantling the structures. The blocking requires either a leader whose own inner commitment to God overrides the transmitted sinning pattern, or the community's own independent resistance.

**[CHAR-8]** E — The blocking conditions appear by implication from the enabling conditions. (1) *Perceived strength and legitimacy of governing authority*: Moab's revolts occurring "after the death of Ahab" (2Ki 1:1; 3:5) imply that during Ahab's reign, Moab did not revolt — the strong authority blocked revolt. (2) *The ruler's faithfulness to God*: 2Ch 21:10's causal link implies the converse: a ruler who does not forsake the Lord maintains the spiritual ground of legitimate authority that prevents the subject peoples from revolting. Fidelity to God in the governing authority is the primary blocking condition.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The blocking conditions from the corpus: (1) *Creaturely humility and restraint*: Jude 9 — Michael "did not presume to pronounce a blasphemous judgment" — the inner condition of knowing one's creaturely limits restrains sinful speech; (2) *Renunciation and replacement*: Eph 4:31 — "let all... slander be put away from you" — the deliberate inner act of renunciation is the blocking condition; (3) *Knowledge of God (faith)*: 1Ti 1:13 — Paul's blasphemy was from "ignorant unbelief" — the converse is that knowing God in faith prevents blasphemous speech.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence from VCG-04 (moral contrast) and VCG-07 (directional orientation) shows that the conditions blocking wickedness-as-settled-person-identity are: (a) active fear of God (its absence is definitional for the wicked — Psa 36:1; its presence in Psa 1:1 is the blessed person's condition); (b) the counsel of the righteous (Psa 1:1 — the blessed person avoids the wicked's counsel); (c) responsiveness to the prophetic call to turn (Eze 3:18–19; 33:8–19 — the wicked who turns is specifically the one who has not settled into the characteristic). The primary blocking condition is the sustained orientation of the inner person toward God — sustained non-service (Mal 3:18 defines the wicked by their non-service, so service is the blocking condition).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The evidence names specific inner conditions that block the characteristic's deepening and expression: (1) genuine love — Rom 12:9 (vc=14417 — VCG-06): love actively abhors evil and holds fast to good — love's orientation structurally opposes the characteristic; (2) the implanted word — Jam 1:21 (vc=14368 — VCG-05): the received word blocks rampant wickedness from remaining; (3) faith and the word of God — 1Jo 2:14 (vc=14430 — VCG-01): "the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one" — the word's abiding in the person is the primary blocking condition; (4) the cleansed conscience through Christ — Heb 10:22 (vc=14426 — VCG-06): the conscience "sprinkled clean from an evil conscience" is the transformed state that blocks the characteristic's access to the relational dimension; (5) divine armor — Eph 6:16 (vc=14428 — VCG-01): faith as shield extinguishing the evil one's flaming darts.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The blocking conditions are: (1) a functional, shame-producing conscience — Eze 9:4 (vc=1698 — VCG-04): those who sigh and groan over abominations are marked for protection — their operative conscience is what prevents them from committing abomination themselves; (2) the hearing and keeping of law — Pro 28:9 (vc=65958 — VCG-03): the inverse of turning away the ear from the law; (3) the upright inner way — Pro 3:32 (vc=1686 — VCG-02): the upright person is in God's confidence precisely because their inner orientation is not crooked, meaning uprightness of inner way is the blocking condition; (4) discernment and reflection — Isa 44:19 (vc=65961 — VCG-05): the one who "considers" and has "knowledge or discernment" would perceive the abomination before committing it.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Blocking conditions: (1) active covenant separation — Deu 18:9 (vc=65931 — VCG-02): "you shall not learn to follow the abominable practices of those nations" — proactive non-learning is a blocking condition; (2) immediate destruction of idol-objects — Deu 7:25 (vc=1682 — VCG-02): "you shall burn with fire" — the removal of the physical object removes the attraction-mechanism; (3) hearing and responding to the prophetic word — Eze 20:8 (vc=65911 — VCG-05) shows the alternative: the command to "cast away the detestable things your eyes feast on" — compliance with this command would have blocked the characteristic; (4) the active removal of abominable objects from the inner community — 2Ch 15:8 (vc=65902 — VCG-03): Asa's reform — the act of purging protects the community's inner space from idolatrous influence.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Blocking conditions: (1) open ears to instruction — Job 36:10 (vc=38215 — VCG-04): "He opens their ears to instruction and commands that they return from iniquity" — receptivity to divine instruction is the primary inner block; (2) maintained steps according to divine promise — Psa 119:133 (vc=38227 — VCG-04): "keep steady my steps according to your promise" — volitional steadiness following the divine word blocks iniquity's dominion; (3) active releasing of iniquity held in the hand — Job 11:14 (vc=38207 — VCG-04): "if iniquity is in your hand, put it far away" — volitional distance from held iniquity as a blocking act; (4) forsaking iniquitous thoughts and returning to the Lord — Isa 55:7 (vc=38200 — VCG-02): the prescribed internal blocking movement; (5) cleansing the heart — Jer 4:14 (vc=38205 — VCG-02): "O Jerusalem, wash your heart from evil, that you may be saved" — the commanded inner cleansing as the blocking act.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Blocking conditions: (1) repentance — Rev 16:9 (VCG-01): "they did not repent" — its presence would have arrested the characteristic; the absence of repentance enables continued blasphemy; (2) good conscience — 1Pe 3:16 (vc=14380 — VCG-03): "having a good conscience" — the inner integrity of conscience protects against both generating false accusation and being undone by it; (3) honourable conduct — 1Pe 2:12 (vc=14377 — VCG-03): honourable conduct prevents the generation of justified accusations; (4) accurate understanding — Jude 10 (vc=14355 — VCG-01): the contrary of not-understanding; if they understood, they would not blaspheme; (5) submission to authority — Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): the contrary of authority-rejection; authority-submission blocks the blasphemy that flows from authority-rejection.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a composite blocking profile across the six characteristics. The most consistent blockers: (1) A functioning conscience (all six — the conscience as the primary internal block that registers and resists the characteristic); (2) Divine instruction received through open ears (Char 5: Job 36:10 — God opens their ears; Char 4: Deu 18:9 — not learning to follow abominable practices; Char 6: authority-submission as the opposite of authority-rejection — Jude 8); (3) Honourable conduct orientation (Char 6: 1Pe 2:12 — honourable conduct that eventually silences false accusation; Char 3: Pro 3:32 — the upright who are in divine confidence). The cluster reveals that blocking M10b characteristics requires inner-faculty alignment — functioning conscience, open instructed ears, and the will oriented toward the good — rather than merely behavioural management. Char 4 adds the unique physical-removal blocking mechanism (Deu 7:25 — burn the idols to remove the visual-desire feedback loop), confirming that for idolatrous abomination, environmental control of the outer-to-inner feedback is necessary alongside inner-faculty alignment.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Two blocking conditions are directly evidenced. First, ignorance: Lev 5:2-3 (M10c-A-VCG-01) shows defilement preceding awareness — the person is defiled before they know it. Ignorance does not prevent the condition but prevents the appropriate response. Second, willful refusal: Num 19:20 (M10c-A-VCG-07) — the man who is unclean and "does not cleanse himself" is cut off. The will's deliberate choice not to engage the appointed remedy is the primary blocking condition named in the evidence. A third distortion is evidenced in the NT: Peter's categorical conviction (M10c-B-VCG-05, Act 10:14) initially blocks the divine revision of the clean/unclean category — a formed conscience can become an inner resistance to new divine speech.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Two blocking conditions are directly evidenced. (1) A strong/formed conscience: 1Cor 8:7 (VCG-03) — those with "knowledge" (genuine moral conviction) eat without defiling their conscience, because the conviction is genuine and the conscience is not overridden. (2) Active consecration and separation: 2Cor 6:17 (VCG-03) — "go out from their midst, and be separate from them... touch no unclean thing; then I will welcome you" — active separation from defiling environments and influences is the primary blocking condition; the external act of separation protects the inner person from the condition's reception. Isa 52:11 (VCG-03): "purify yourselves, you who bear the vessels of the Lord" — active self-purification is a blocking condition against the characteristic's return.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Three blocking conditions are evidenced. (1) Consecrated separation — the Nazirite's commitment (Num 6:7, VCG-05): "not even for his father or for his mother... shall he make himself unclean, because his separation to God is on his head" — the inner dedication to God overrides even natural relational impulse, preventing the defilement. (2) Active covenantal fidelity: Eze 18:6 (VCG-01): "does not defile his neighbor's wife" — the righteous man's will consistently refusing sexual defilement across generations (18:6, 18:15) is the blocking orientation. (3) Priestly discernment and institutional guardianship: 2Ch 23:19 (the Characteristic 1 register but governing the same principle) and Eze 44:23 (VCG-05): "they shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and show them how to distinguish between the unclean and the clean" — instruction in the clean/unclean distinction is a blocking condition at the institutional level.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 21-verse corpus does not evidence specific inner conditions in the potential recipient that block the characteristic. The evidence focuses on the authoritative power that removes it (divine command — Mar 5:8, Mar 9:25) rather than on inner conditions that prevent its arrival. The VCG-03 authority-commissioning register names granted authority as the means of opposition (Mat 10:1, Mar 6:7), but this is external authoritative power against the agent, not inner enabling in the potential recipient.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The blocking-condition profiles confirm the same structural division. Characteristics 1, 2, and 3 each identify inner blocking conditions; Characteristic 4 does not. Characteristic 1's blockers: ignorance (which does not prevent the condition but prevents the appropriate response — Lev 5:2-3); willful refusal of remedy (Num 19:20 — the decisive moral fault); and a formed conscience that may initially resist even divine revision (Act 10:14 — Peter's categorical conviction). Characteristic 2's blockers: strong/formed conscience (1Cor 8:7 — genuine conviction eats without defilement) and active consecration/separation (2Cor 6:17 — "go out from their midst"). Characteristic 3's blockers: consecrated separation (Num 6:7 — the Nazirite's dedication overrides natural kinship impulse), active covenantal fidelity (Eze 18:6 — "does not defile his neighbor's wife"), and institutional priestly guardianship (Eze 44:23). Characteristic 4's blockers: not evidenced in the 21-verse corpus — the authoritative divine power that removes the characteristic (Mar 5:8, Mar 9:25) is the VCG-03 register, but this is external power against the agent, not inner-blocking in the potential recipient. Cluster pattern: blocking operates through the conscience and will (Chars 1, 2) and through communal-institutional formation (Chars 1, 3). Characteristic 4 resists the concept of inner blocking altogether — its only effective resistance is divine authority.

questions.question_text: What is the inner-being state of the person in whom the characteristic is present but does not take hold?

findings.session_b_note:
The data provides partial evidence. The inner state of the non-receiver is not named comprehensively but can be drawn from several observations:

- **The unforgiving servant (Mat 18:35):** The person who encounters forgiveness and receives it verbally but not at the heart level remains in a state of internal incoherence — the outer form is present, the inner release is not. The consequence is judgment.
- **The scribes (Mar 2:7):** The person who encounters forgiveness and misidentifies it (as blasphemy rather than divine act) remains in a state of spiritual misrecognition — they are in the presence of what they most need but cannot see it for what it is.
- **The person who refuses to forgive (Mat 6:15):** The closure of horizontal forgiveness appears to close vertical reception. The inner state is one of self-imposed closure.
- **The outer limit (Mar 3:29):** The person for whom forgiveness is permanently inaccessible is named as "guilty of an eternal sin" — a permanent guilt-state with no resolution path.

*Gap noted:* The data does not describe the phenomenological inner experience of the non-receiver — what it feels like from the inside to be in the presence of forgiveness and not receive it. This is not evidenced.

findings.session_b_note:
The data addresses one specific case directly and implies others:

**The explicitly pitiable but self-unaware (Rev 3:17):** The person who encounters compassion but cannot receive it — because they cannot perceive their own pitiable condition — remains in a state of spiritual destitution without being aware of it. The inner state is one of self-deceptive sufficiency masking actual need. The irony named in the data is pointed: those who most need compassion may be those least able to receive it.

**The one in extreme duress (Lam 4:10 context):** The compassionate women who violate their own compassion under siege conditions represent a different case — a person whose compassion-capacity has been overwhelmed by external catastrophe. The inner state is one of constitutional rupture: the characteristic that defines the person has been forced into violation. This is not a failure of reception but a failure of the character under unbearable pressure.

**What is missing (P):** The data does not directly address the inner-being state of a person who encounters human compassion but refuses or cannot receive it for reasons other than self-deception (e.g., shame, distrust, grief, pride). This is a gap not covered by existing SD pointers.

findings.session_b_note:
The verse evidence provides a direct answer in Jer 44:10 and in the refusal clause of group 7552-003 ("the condition of brokenness before God that occasions divine presence, *and its refusal*"). The person who encounters the conditions for contrition — who is confronted with their moral condition before a holy God — but refuses the contrite posture is characterised by:

**Hardness** — the inner being that does not yield to the crushing encounter remains closed and resistant. The people of Jer 44:10 have been confronted with the full weight of their condition but have not humbled themselves, feared, or turned. Their inner being is, in the vocabulary of the structural opposite, **proud and closed** — self-sufficient against divine assessment.

The consequence of this non-reception is notable: Jer 44:10 is within the group that also contains Isa 57:15 (the divine dwelling with the contrite). The God who dwells with the contrite does not dwell with the hardened. The inner-being state of the one who refuses contrition is: continued self-sufficiency, divine absence, and — as the trajectory of Jer 44 shows — eventual catastrophe without divine covering.

*New finding: the inner-being state of the one who refuses contrition is not merely neutral absence of the quality; it is a specific closed condition (hardness) with a specific consequence (divine absence). This was implicit in OBS-030-028 but not assembled as an answer to the reception-refusal question.*

findings.session_b_note:
The data addresses what blocks reception, but does not directly describe the inner-being state of the person who encounters fellowship and fails to enter it.

**What can be inferred:**
- **Isolation:** Ecc 4:10 — the person who falls without a companion is alone in their falling. The failure to be in fellowship leaves a structural vulnerability.
- **Spiritual blindness:** The person who is joined to idols (Hos 4:17) is not simply blocking divine fellowship — they may not recognise the fellowship they are forfeiting. The occult charming groups (7565-002, 7569-001) suggest misdirected inner seeking that substitutes occult power for genuine spiritual fellowship.
- **Moral culpability without awareness:** Mat 23:30 — the Pharisees' claim that they would not have participated suggests a failure to recognise their actual complicity (following fellowship). Unrecognised fellowship can produce unrecognised culpability.

**Gap:** The question of what the person who *encounters* divine nature fellowship and refuses it experiences is not addressed in the data. This is a genuine gap, likely deferrable to Session D.

findings.session_b_note: Two forms of non-reception are evidenced: (1) Haman (Est 5:9, 884-009): the person who experiences a surface form of well-being (tov-lev — glad of heart) without its genuine ground. The inner state is one of fragile gladness — pleasantness without rootedness. One adverse sight immediately destroys it. This is not a person who has rejected goodness but one who has mistaken a lesser good for the genuine good. The inner state is: temporarily satisfied, morally ungrounded, and constitutionally fragile. (2) Those who "will not walk in it" (Jer 6:16): the person who has heard and encountered the good way but refused it. The inner state is one of offered-but-rejected goodness — the will has been engaged by the good and actively turned away. The inner state is: resistant, self-willed, and under the verdict of their own refusal. (OBS-067-OBS-040, OBS-067-OBS-041, SBF-067-Q028)

findings.session_b_note: The data provides several instances: (a) Joh 3:19 (OBS-103-147) — the person who encounters light-as-love and does not receive it 'loved the darkness' — the inner state is commitment to the alternative; the non-reception is an inner-being act of love misdirected. (b) Luk 16:14 (OBS-103-136) — the Pharisees who were money-lovers ridiculed Jesus' teaching; their inner state is intellectual rejection grounded in love-of-money. (c) 2Ti 4:10 (OBS-103-148) — Demas, in love with the present world, deserts: the non-reception of love-community is an act of love toward the world instead. The pattern is consistent: the person who does not receive love is not loveless — they are loving the wrong thing. Lovelessness in the sense of having no love-capacity does not appear in the data; what appears is love misdirected.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-001: Love's definition resolves to a structured family of inner-being orientations sharing one mechanism — directed attachment toward an object — whose moral character is entirely determined by the object …
findings.finding_value: Love's definition resolves to a structured family of inner-being orientations sharing one mechanism — directed attachment toward an object — whose moral character is entirely determined by the object chosen. Within this shared mechanism, the vocabulary distinguishes three structural registers: love as disposition (the stable inner orientation — chesed, agapē as character), love as act (the commanded and exercised expression — agapaō, enemy-love), and love as condition (the identity-constituting state of being-loved — agapētos). These are not three separate loves but three aspects of love's single operation: the person has a deep stable orientation (disposition), exercises it in specific acts (act), and exists within the love-relationship as constituted by it (condition). The vocabulary arc runs from the ontologically highest (God is love — 1Jo 4:8) through the morally normative (chesed, commanded agapē) to the affective-natural (phileō, dod) to the morally inverted (love of darkness, love of self). No other characteristic in the programme commands a comparable vocabulary range. The definition's boundary with adjacent characteristics (compassion, mercy, kindness) is partially drawn: love is the broader orientation; compassion is love's suffering-triggered mode; mercy and kindness are love's formal relational expressions. The boundaries require Session D precision.

findings.session_b_note: The structural opposite — the one who encounters mercy-extension but does not receive it — is partially addressed. Mat 18:34 (the unforgiving servant who received mercy but does not extend it or remain in its reception) shows that mercy un-received in its transformative dimension results in judgment. The unforgiving servant's inner state is one in which received mercy has not penetrated to reshape inner disposition. But the data does not directly name the inner state of the person who encounters and resists God's mercy. This is a gap — the data addresses the one who fails to extend mercy, not clearly the one who refuses to receive it. OBS-111-055.

findings.session_b_note: Jer 44:10 provides the clearest evidence: the un-contrite person is characterised by hardness (not humbled), absence of fear (not trembling), and orientation away from God's word (not walking in the law). The inner-being state is one of self-enclosure — the inner being turned back on itself, impermeable to divine assessment. The refusal of contrition is not passive neutrality but active self-protection of the inner being from the weight of its own moral condition. *New finding: the person who refuses contrition is characterised by inner self-enclosure — an active impermeability rather than a neutral absence of feeling.* OBS-030-028, OBS-030-047.

findings.finding_value: T1 as a whole reveals that contrition is a definitionally complex inner-being condition whose structure is determined by its origin (passive, produced by encounter), its constitutional location (spirit and heart), and its directional logic (downward into brokenness, then threshold toward divine response). The three-mode structure (penitential, anguish, substitutionary) is unified by the crushing metaphor but differentiated by the agent and relational context of the crushing. The definition tier establishes contrition's primary asymmetry: the person is not the author of their own contrition — they receive it from encounter with reality they cannot deflect — and this passivity is precisely what positions them for divine nearness. The structural opposite (inner self-enclosure) and the blocking condition (merit-claiming) together define contrition negatively as the absence of self-sufficiency before God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-009: The definition tier (T1) establishes contrition as a passive inner condition produced by encounter; the faculty tier (T3) shows that this passivity simultaneously opens every inner faculty. The connec…
findings.finding_value: The definition tier (T1) establishes contrition as a passive inner condition produced by encounter; the faculty tier (T3) shows that this passivity simultaneously opens every inner faculty. The connection between T1 and T3 is that contrition's defining feature — the dissolution of self-protection — is precisely what enables the faculties. T1's structural negative (inner self-enclosure as the opposite of contrition, Q&A-033) is T3's impairment condition: the self-enclosed person has every faculty partially closed. Contrition's definition therefore predicts its faculty effects: a characteristic that is constitutively about removal of self-protective barriers will enable every faculty that self-protection would otherwise restrict.

Spiritual bondage results (Ephraim "joined to idols" — unable to break the joining). OBS-062-042.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-001: T1 establishes fellowship as a structurally complex characteristic whose definitional core (genuine participation-in, determined by its object) is expressed through five distinct modes and whose susta…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes fellowship as a structurally complex characteristic whose definitional core (genuine participation-in, determined by its object) is expressed through five distinct modes and whose sustained operation produces constitutional character formation. The definition tier's key insight: fellowship is formally unified by the object-determines-character logic but materially diverse across five modes (existential, companionship, moral complicity, transformative suffering, ontological). The structural negative (misdirected fellowship) is more dangerous than absence of fellowship — Hos 4:17 and Mat 23:30 present the active wrong-direction as the primary threat, not non-participation. The definitional complexity of fellowship explains why the single English word is analytically inadequate: it covers a range from minimal existential participation (Ecc 9:4) to maximal ontological transformation (2Pe 1:4) under the same label.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-001: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanch…
findings.finding_value: T1 reveals compassion as a definitionally complex characteristic that simultaneously operates as character quality (ra.chum — the settled disposition of the compassionate person), inner event (splanchnizō — the moment of being-moved), condition of its object (eleeinos — the pitiable state that calls compassion forth), and externalised act (almsgiving, mercy-act). No other characteristic in the programme review set operates across all four kinds simultaneously. The four root families (RACHAM, CHASAD, SPLANCHN, OIKTIROM) identify four constituent dimensions of the single characteristic, each naming a distinct register — somatic-maternal, covenantal-relational, visceral-immediate, and deliberative-pitying respectively. The structural opposites are two distinct kinds: willed judicial hardness (the hardened heart that refuses compassion) and unwilled prosperity-blindness (Eze 16:49 — the one who does not see the need because they are satiated). The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed by the consistent outward-facing structure: compassion cannot exist without a suffering other. The definitional tier's most critical gap — the receiver's inner-being experience — is entirely absent from the data, affecting T1.5, T1.6, and T1.7 throughout. This gap is the single most significant analytical absence in the registry.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-011: T1's sustained-effect analysis (largely P-rated because the receiver's inner-being experience is absent) and T5's formation arc together reveal a gap that is structurally significant: the formation pr…
findings.finding_value: T1's sustained-effect analysis (largely P-rated because the receiver's inner-being experience is absent) and T5's formation arc together reveal a gap that is structurally significant: the formation process from single compassion-event to compassion-character is the most important untraced developmental relationship in the registry. T5 provides the directional finding (the formative cycle feeds back from after-state to before-state) and names the three mechanisms (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological). T1 provides the definitional starting point (compassion as character quality is the endpoint of formation). Together they frame an arc that is identified but not filled: how does the moment of splanchnizō (T1 inner-event) accumulate into the settled character of ra.chum (T1 character quality)? T5's mechanisms suggest the answer but the data does not trace the path explicitly — a gap confirmed by both tiers.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-001: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes grace as a definitionally multi-kind characteristic: simultaneously divine disposition (the inclination of the greater toward the lesser — chen root), relational standing (the condition of being in favour — charis as inhabited state), enabling capacity (the specific power given for specific tasks — 2Cor 12:9), and character quality (gracious speech, gracious conduct — chen in 889-003). No single English equivalent captures all four. The four modes of operation (sovereign bestowal, covenantal-relational sustaining, capacity-conferring, character-forming) correspond to the four kinds without collapsing them. Two structural opposites are identified: pride (the self-elevation that refuses the favour of the greater, active and willed) and ingratitude/gracelessness (acharistos — the failure to register and respond to grace received, which T3 confirms as image-impairment). The immediate response pattern (fear → mourning → prostration as the creaturely recognition response before positive states settle) is a T1.5 finding confirming that grace does not bypass creaturely recognition but requires and produces it as a transitional state. The dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) is confirmed throughout: grace is constitutively directional — it flows from the greater to the lesser and requires the receptor's inner-being engagement to complete its operation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-011: T1's sustained-effect finding (immediate/sustained contrast as qualitative, not merely temporal — what grace does immediately is creaturely recognition; what it does over time is constitution of ident…
findings.finding_value: T1's sustained-effect finding (immediate/sustained contrast as qualitative, not merely temporal — what grace does immediately is creaturely recognition; what it does over time is constitution of identity and character) maps onto T5's formation mechanisms. The encounter mechanism (T5) produces the immediate effects named in T1.5; the word, inference, and mediated-transformation mechanisms (T5) produce the sustained effects of T1.6. T5's five mechanisms collectively explain how the four kinds named in T1.2 are produced across different temporal and contextual registers: disposition-receipt is the encounter mechanism; standing is the spirit-outpouring mechanism; capacity is the mediated-transformation mechanism; character quality is the sustained word-and-inference mechanism. T1 names what is produced; T5 names how each kind is produced.

findings.session_b_note: The data provides a clear picture: (1) Desolation — Eph 2:12: "having no hope and without God in the world" (OBS-034-060). The person who encounters the covenants of promise and remains a stranger to them lives in inner desolation — hopelessness, alienation, godlessness. (2) Bondage — Gal 4:24-25 (OBS-034-071): remaining under the Sinai covenant without entering the new covenant freedom is described as bearing children for slavery — the inner condition is one of bondage. (3) Moral collapse — Rom 1:31: the covenant-breaker (asunthetos) appears in the catalogue of moral and cognitive failure that characterises those who have suppressed the truth (OBS-034-057). Not receiving the covenantal bond produces inner moral dissolution. (4) Curse activation — Dan 9:11 (OBS-034-036): the person who encounters the covenant, receives its obligations, but breaks it experiences the activated curse — the inner consequence of breach. The common thread: not receiving covenant (or receiving it falsely/partially) produces inner conditions of desolation, bondage, moral dissolution, or judgment.

findings.session_b_note: The data provides one clear instance. Jer 13:16 (OBS-060-047): the person who fails to give glory to God — who encounters the command to give glory but does not receive and act on it — experiences inner-being darkness, stumbling, and gloom. The failure to receive the characteristic (glory-giving as relational correspondence) produces inner-being disorder. This is the most explicit statement in the corpus about the inner state of the non-receiver. The judicial giving-over texts (872-004) also imply a prior state of failed reception: those who are given over were first given covenantal faithfulness and did not receive/respond to it. But the inner-being state of that failure is not described in the anchor verses themselves — only the consequence (giving-over) is named. Gap: the data does not provide a direct description of the inner state of the person who hears the covenantal promise but does not receive it in faith; that question belongs to R059 (faith/unbelief vocabulary).

Job 31:29: "if I have rejoiced at the ruin of him who hated me" — the righteous person does not move into reciprocal hatred when hated. Exo 23:5: "if you see the donkey of one who hates you lying down under its burden, you shall rescue it with him" — the command assumes it is possible to act for the benefit of the person who hates you without reciprocating. The inner state is not described directly but implied: the person maintains a different inner-being orientation — grounded in something beyond the relational exchange — that enables acting for the enemy's good.

Isa 49:7: the Servant is "deeply despised, abhorred by the nation" yet the promise of divine vindication is the inner resource that enables the despised to bear contempt without being destroyed or reciprocating it.

The person who abhorres evil rightly (group 252-001) maintains righteous abhorrence without being consumed by it — the abhorrence is directed at the right object and produces moral stability rather than disorder.

Group 1775-002 documents this most fully: the recipient of ruthlessness who does not reciprocate it is characterised by appeal (Job 6:23), trust in God as deliverer (Isa 25:4), and confidence that God will contend (Isa 49:25, Jer 15:21). The inner state is not passivity but active sustained appeal grounded in a different understanding of where ultimate power lies.

1Th 2:2: Paul had "boldness in our God to declare the gospel" despite shameful treatment. Jer 15:15: "for your sake I bear reproach" — the prophet holds the reproach in the context of his relationship with God, which prevents identity destruction. The inner state involves the pain of reproach alongside a groundedness in God's regard that keeps the reproach from colonising the person's identity.
The person who faces an adversary through appeal and vigilance rather than through reciprocal hostility is characterised by sober-mindedness (1Pe 5:8) and persistent petition (Luk 18:3).

The verse evidence does not describe the inner state of those who are the objects of malice (Israel). The inner experience of being maliced is not documented in the three Ezekiel verses.

### T1.8 — Dimension Classification
[Sub-group not separately addressed in source — see cluster-level finding (cluster_subgroup_id IS NULL) for this prompt]
The person who claims love but does not receive it remains in darkness and self-deception (1Jo 2:15 — Group 1565 context — the world-lover).

The one whose compassion has been appropriately withheld (judicial register) is under judgment. The one who disobediently shows compassion where it should be withheld suffers moral culpability (1Sa 15:9 — Group 629-b).
The merciless person who forfeits mercy (Jam 2:13 — Group 1626 — anileōs). The person who does not receive God's sovereign mercy is in the condition of hardness (Pharaoh — Group 1628 context).

Hardness and continued unrepentance (Rom 2:4-5 — Group 1111 context). The person who encounters God's kindness without receiving it treats the kindness as ambient background rather than as the transformative address it is.
Haughtiness and contentiousness — the self-asserting, quarrelsome person (Pro 18:12 — Group 1272; 2Ti 2:24 — Group 867 contrast).
Sustained grief and desolation — Lam 1:16 (Group 1741): "a comforter is far from me, one to revive my spirit." The person who refuses comfort remains in the unreleved state.

Self-deception — the person who claims fellowship while walking in darkness (1Jo 1:6 — Group 1055) "lies and does not practice the truth." Estrangement — the pre-katallagē condition of enmity (Rom 5:11 — Group 2069 implies the prior state).
[Sub-group not separately addressed in source — see cluster-level finding for this prompt]

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Felix — alarmed, then dismissing (Act 24:25, VSG M26-A1-006). The inner-being state: conviction without conversion; alarm without repentance; recognition without submission.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Named in A2-003 (distortion and counterfeit) and A2-004 (far from righteousness). Inner-being state: either presenting a counterfeit, or so far from it that the encounter produces no movement toward it — "if favour is shown to the wicked, he does not learn righteousness" (Isa 26:10, VSG 1214-001).

**[B — Moral Uprightness]** Demands smooth things instead (Isa 30:10, VSG 1214-001). Inner-being state: preference for comfort and approval over truth has become the governing orientation. The person actively resists uprightness because it threatens the smooth narrative they prefer.

**[C — Justification]** Remains in the condition that justification is designed to resolve: under the weight of their own inability to stand before God. Inner-being state: uncleared conscience, unresolved guilt-standing, oriented toward self-generated solutions that cannot succeed.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Continues in the self-executing vengeance impulse (Rom 12:19). Inner-being state: the destructive weight of unresolved resentment and the burden of maintaining one's own retributive justice — a weight the person was not designed to carry.

**[E — Condemnation]** Remains under the condemning verdict — either externally (the judicial sentence stands) or internally (the condemning conscience is unresolved). Inner-being state: the weight of being under judgment without the resource that would lift it.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** In a state of condemnation (the eating is condemned because the reckoning was not from faith, Rom 14:23). Inner-being state: the faculty is present but misdirected, and the misdirection produces guilt rather than freedom.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Described in Isa 26:10 (VSG 1214-001): "in the land of uprightness he deals corruptly and does not see the majesty of the Lord." Inner-being state: the eyes are closed to the standard even while living within its territory.

**[CLUSTER]** The inner-being state of the person who encounters righteousness but does not receive it: alarm without repentance, counterfeit without reality, preference for smooth things, unresolved guilt-standing, self-executing resentment, weight of condemning verdict, misdirected faculty, and blindness to the standard. Non-reception of righteousness is not neutral — it produces a specific and coherent inner-being state of disorder.
VCG06 (Pro 26:12 anchor): "there is more hope for a fool than for a person wise in their own eyes" — self-wisdom as the inner state forecloses reception more completely than simple ignorance.

findings.finding_value: The person who encounters material prosperity but does not receive inner closure is the person of M46-C and M46-D: the diligent whose soul is richly supplied (Pro 13:4), the contented person who has learned to be settled regardless (Phil 4:11), the generous person who gives from abundance (2Cor 8:2). They receive the material goods without the inner closure they can produce — the countervailing inner conditions prevent the closure from forming.

findings.finding_value: The person who encounters the demand for voluntary release but does not receive it is the rich young ruler (Luk 18:23) — he became very sad but could not release. His inner state: grief (perilupos) without resolution. This is the most precise description in the cluster of what non-reception of M46-D looks like: sorrow without action, encounter without transformation.
