findings.finding_value: The person who encounters the stimulus for reverential fear but does not receive it is in a state of moral blindness (Psa 36:1: "no dread of God before their eyes — fundamental moral blindness that allows transgression to speak freely in the heart"); defiant self-sufficiency (Psa 55:19: "not fearing God marks an inner disposition of defiant self-sufficiency"); and ultimately apostasy or judgment-bound hardness (Jer 5:22-24: "the people do not say in their hearts 'let us fear the Lord'" — ingratitude and irreverence are one; the absence of fear in the heart is the root of covenant failure). The NT is direct: Rom 3:18 ("absence of fear of God in their inner orientation — indicates that godless humanity lacks the reverential awareness that should govern all thought and conduct").

The person who encounters acute fear's stimulus and is commanded "do not fear" but does not receive the release remains in the grip of paralysis, silence, or flight. The commanded-release corpus (B-VCG-06) assumes the person's ongoing struggle with the fear until the divine word penetrates.
The person who encounters the call to courage but remains in timidity is in the state described by Rev 21:8: cowardice as a defining inner orientation, heading toward apostasy.

Non-reception of reverential fear (M01-A) produces moral blindness and defiant self-sufficiency. Non-reception of commanded-fear-release (M01-B's "do not fear") produces paralysis. Non-reception of courage-over-timidity (M01-G) produces apostasy. The common feature: non-reception leaves the inner person structurally misaligned — either toward wrong objects of fear or toward no genuine alignment at all.

Isa 42:25 (M02-B-VCG-06) is the most explicit evidence: "God's rage is poured out as consuming fire on Israel in battle, yet the people failed to perceive or take it to heart — the inner faculty of understanding is closed off, blocking recognition of divine wrath." The state of non-reception is cognitive closure — the inner faculty of understanding is not functioning. The person under wrath who does not receive (recognise, respond to) it is in a state of inner darkening.

Jer 7:19 (M02-D-VCG-01) asks whether Israel's provocation wounds God or rebounds on them as shame — the person who provokes anger but does not receive the intended moral signal is in a state of self-destructive moral blindness.

The corpus names this state explicitly in several places. The Corinthians who should have mourned but did not are described as arrogant (1Cor 5:2 — M03-B-VCG-04) — their inner state is one of puffed-up complacency that crowds out grief. Babylon, who boasts she will never see mourning, is in a state of pride and spiritual self-deception (Rev 18:7). The self-indulgent condemned for not being grieved over Joseph's ruin (Amo 6:6 — M03-BOUNDARY) are in a state of moral numbing — the empathic inner faculty that should respond to national catastrophe has ceased to function. The person who encounters grief occasions but does not receive grief is characterised by a kind of inner insensibility — a dulling of the relational and moral responsiveness that grief requires.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The VCG-02 passages show the alternative inner state: mourning (Hos 10:5 — priests mourn when the calf departs); joylessness (Job 3:6–7); inverted exultation directed at death (Job 3:22); enemy exultation over the righteous's defeat (Psa 13:4). The person who cannot receive genuine Godward exultation is either in a state of mourning and grief, or has misdirected their exultation-capacity toward wrong objects. The evidence does not show a neutral middle ground — the person is either exulting rightly, exulting wrongly, or emptied of the capacity by extremity.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The VCG-06 corpus provides the evidence: (1) **Mourning and groaning** — Lam 5:15 ("the joy of our hearts has ceased; our dancing has been turned to mourning"); (2) **Sighing** — Isa 24:7 ("all the merry-hearted sigh" when joy is stripped away); (3) **Joylessness as desolation** — Isa 24:11 ("all joy has grown dark; the gladness of the earth is banished") — the inner state is one of inner darkness replacing the brightness of joy; (4) **Shallow inadequacy** — Ecc 2:1–2 (joy pursued and found vain — the Preacher who seeks joy as a project finds it hollow); (5) **Crushing** — Pro 15:13 ("by sorrow of heart the spirit is crushed") — the opposite inner state to the glad heart is a crushed spirit. The person who cannot receive genuine joy is in a state of mourning, sighing, inner darkness, or crushed spiritedness.

**[CHAR-7]** E — M04-F provides the answer: Job 9:27 (grief-saturated, attempting cheerfulness and failing); Psa 39:13 (requesting to smile briefly before death — joy almost entirely beyond reach); Jer 8:18 ("my joy is gone; grief is upon me; my heart is sick within me" — the prophet in the total absence of the characteristic's comfort). These show the person who cannot receive Suffering-Joy in a state of unrelieved grief, heartsickness, and barely-surviving distress. The characteristic's absence is not neutral but marks the full weight of suffering bearing upon the inner person without the Spirit-enabled transcendence.

**[CHAR-3]** E — (1) **Moral blindness** — the fool who finds joy in folly (Pro 15:21 — M04-B, but adjacent) and the one who does not-good are unable to perceive the genuinely good; (2) **Distress** — the Israelites who cannot receive the good land as good remain in fear and distress (Num 14:3); (3) **Hollow festivity** — Isa 22:13's "let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die" — receiving circumstantial pleasure but not genuine gladness, which requires more than pleasure; (4) **Nostalgia without restoration** — Hos 2:7's "it was better then" — the memory of former gladness without the conditions for its return; (5) **Self-loathing** — Eze 36:31's trajectory from not-good recognition to loathing — the person who encounters the evaluative-gladness faculty in its condemning mode without finding restoration ends in self-directed revulsion.

**[CHAR-4]** E — (1) **Alienation from God** — Jer 6:10 (the ear closed to God's word, the heart sealed against its proper object); (2) **Destructive desire** — Jer 42:22 (the people desire to go to Egypt, and their very desire leads to disaster — Delight directing the will toward what destroys); (3) **Moral deformation** — Pro 18:2 (the fool taking pleasure only in his own opinion — Delight contracted onto the self); (4) **Judgment** — Isa 65:12; 66:4 (the people who "chose what I did not delight in" meet judgment); (5) **Spiritual captivation** — Rev 13:3; 17:8 (the world marveling at the beast — the person whose name is not in the book of life, captivated by the wrong magnificent object). The person who encounters but does not receive genuine Delight is not neutral — the Delight faculty continues to operate and attaches itself to whatever object presents itself, however wrong.

**[CHAR-5]** E — (1) **Isolation and grief** — 2Sa 1:26 (David's distress at losing Jonathan's pleasant companionship — the absence of pleasantness producing grief); (2) **False pleasure** — Pro 9:17 (stolen bread appearing pleasant — the person receives a simulacrum of Pleasure that leads to death); (3) **Denied enjoyment** — Job 20:18 (the wicked man getting no enjoyment from his profits — blocked from receiving the natural Pleasure of his own labour's fruit); (4) **Hardness and closure** — Jer 6:10's "uncircumcised ear" (adjacent — the ear closed to God's word taking no pleasure) — the inner being sealed against receiving genuine Pleasure; (5) **Restlessness** — Ecc 2:8's self-accumulated pleasures leave the Preacher unsatisfied — when Pleasure is sought rather than received it produces restlessness rather than rest.

**[CHAR-6]** E — (1) **Hardened and rebellious** — Neh 9:17 (failed Wonder → stiffened neck → appointing a leader to return to Egypt) — Wonder-failure leading directly to rebellion; (2) **Unbelief** — Psa 78:32 ("despite his wonders, they did not believe") — the person who witnesses wonders but does not receive them as wonders remains in unbelief; (3) **Restless and sin-prone** — Psa 78 generally shows the pattern: Israel witnessed wonder after wonder and still rebelled, showing that Wonder not received is evidentially ineffective for transformation; (4) **Troubled astonishment** — Mar 10:32 (those who followed Jesus were afraid while those who accompanied him were amazed) — partial Wonder reception producing mixed fear rather than full receptive awe.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The non-reception states across the seven form a coherent picture of the person resistant to positive inner-being engagement: (1) **Mourning and grief** — the common condition when Joy (Char 2) and Exultation (Char 1) are not received (Lam 5:15; Isa 24:7); (2) **Moral blindness** — the condition when Gladness (Char 3) is not received in its evaluative form (idol-craftsman says "it is good"); (3) **Misdirected captivation** — the condition when Delight (Char 4) is not received in its rightward form: the Delight-faculty attaches to whatever presents itself (Rev 13:3; 17:8 — beast-captivation); (4) **Restlessness and self-accumulation** — the condition when Pleasure (Char 5) is sought rather than received (Ecc 2:8's self-accumulated concubines leave the Preacher unsatisfied); (5) **Hardened rebellion** — the most severe outcome when Wonder (Char 6) is not received: Neh 9:17 shows Wonder-failure leading directly to stiff-necked rebellion; (6) **Unredeemed grief** — the condition when Suffering-Joy (Char 7) cannot be accessed: M04-F's Jeremiah ("my joy is gone; grief is upon me; my heart is sick" — Jer 8:18). Together these non-reception states name the spectrum of inner-being dysfunction that the cluster's seven characteristics address.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Two distinct non-reception states emerge. (1) **Moral hardening** — the person who refuses shame's corrective signal (Jer 3:3; 6:15) is in a state of inner desensitisation: the conscience cannot register what should register. The immediate consequence is ongoing sin without corrective friction, and the long-term consequence is divine judgment (Jer 6:15 — "therefore they shall fall among those who fall"). (2) **Willed resilience** — the person in the voluntary-acceptance register (M07-A-VCG-03; Heb 12:2; Isa 50:7) does not receive shame's collapse-signal not through hardening but through the stronger orientation of will toward a greater object. Jesus "despising the shame" is not moral hardening — it is the engagement of a greater joy. Paul "will not be ashamed" because his authority is genuinely from God — not denial of the shame-pressure but its resolution through grounded confidence. These two non-reception states are analytically distinct: the first is pathological (inner death), the second is volitionally mature (inner strength).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Two possibilities: (1) Hardened defiance — the person undergoes humiliation and either doubles down on pride or cannot integrate the corrective signal. (2) Dissolved without transformation — the nations "shorn of strength" (Isa 37:27) are "reduced to withered plants" — CHAR-2 has collapsed them without producing the corrective reorientation.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The evidence does not extensively describe the inner state of the person who encounters worth-denial directed at them but does not receive it as a blow to their standing. Silent on this specific prompt.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The person who cannot receive CHAR-4's corrective is the one whose evaluative standard has been replaced by self-worship or earthly orientation. Phili 3:19's "their end is destruction" names this person's trajectory. The inverted conscience does not receive CHAR-4's corrective signal because the signal itself has been reinterpreted by the corrupted standard.

**[CHAR-5]** S — The corpus does not extensively describe the inner state of the person who encounters CHAR-5 directed at them but does not receive it as damaging to their standing. The Pauline evidence (2Cor 10:10 — critics dismissing Paul's presence as of no account) shows Paul bearing this without apparent inner displacement, but the inner mechanics of this resilience are not elaborated in the CHAR-5 corpus. Silent.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Psa 73:13's psalmist — who has maintained innocence but doubts its value — is the person who encounters CHAR-6's protective function but finds it apparently failing (enemies are prospering while he maintains moral integrity). The inner state is a crisis of moral confidence: the innocence is real but its protective benefit seems invisible. This is not a loss of innocence but a loss of confidence in innocence's protective value — a faith crisis about whether God vindicates moral integrity.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Two distinct non-reception states emerge across the cluster. (1) Pathological hardening (Chars 1, 4, 6): the seared conscience (Jer 6:15), the inverted conscience that glories in shame (Phili 3:19), the incapacity for innocence (Hos 8:5). These are states of progressive inner damage — the faculty that should receive the signal has been so repeatedly refused that it no longer functions. (2) Volitional resilience (Chars 1, 5): the servant who sets the face like flint (Isa 50:7), Bartimaeus who throws off the shame-identity in response to Jesus's call (Mar 10:50). These are states of moral strength grounded in a higher worth-assignment — the person does not receive the shame-signal as damaging because God's assignment overrides the shame-system's verdict. Cluster-level distinction: refusing shame's damage through grounded confidence in God is resilience; refusing shame's corrective through pride or idolatry is pathological. The difference lies entirely in the orientation of the will.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Psa 131:1 (vc=34059, M08-A1-VCG-03; vc=34224, M08-A2-VCG-01) evidences the alternative inner-being state directly: "my heart is not lifted up; my eyes are not raised too high; I do not occupy myself with things too great and too marvelous for me" — a state of active, deliberate, calm self-lowering; the heart and eyes held below the level that CHAR-1 would occupy. Pro 29:23 (vc=33960, M08-A4-VCG-04) names the alternative state: "he who is lowly in spirit will obtain honour" — the inner posture of lowliness of spirit. Dan 4:37 (vc=34094, M08-A4-VCG-04) evidences the post-humbling alternative from the experiential inside: Nebuchadnezzar now "praises and extols and honours the King of heaven" — the God-directed inner orientation that follows CHAR-1's reversal. These are not passive states; the evidence shows them as actively held and deliberately maintained against CHAR-1's pull.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Psa 19:13 (vc=34095, M08-B-VCG-02) most directly evidences this: "keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me, then I shall be blameless" — the person who successfully resists CHAR-2 is the humble servant who actively seeks divine restraining grace, lives under God's authority, and thereby attains blamelessness. Psa 119:51 (vc=34099, M08-B-VCG-02): "the insolent utterly deride me, but I do not turn away from your law" — the person who encounters CHAR-2 from others but does not receive it holds steadfastly to the divine law that CHAR-2 despises, finding in that adherence the inner stability that CHAR-2 cannot overcome.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Gal 6:14 (vc=33869, M08-C-VCG-02) most directly evidences the alternative: "may I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world" — the person who does not receive VCG-01 boasting is the one for whom the cross has evacuated all worldly boasting-grounds. Phili 3:3 (vc=33879, M08-C-VCG-03): "worship by the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh" — the alternative inner state is wholly Christ-directed glorying with no self-directed alternative.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Rom 12:3 (vc=60866, M08-D-VCG-02) provides the positive alternative directly: "think of yourself with sober judgment, each according to the measure of faith that God has assigned" — the person who does not receive CHAR-4 is in a state of accurate, God-referenced self-assessment. 1Cor 8:1 (vc=33935, M08-D-VCG-01): "love builds up" — the alternative is the cognitive-social posture of love-directed, other-building engagement with knowledge.

**[CHAR-5]** E — 1Ti 6:17–18 (context of vc=60878, M08-E-VCG-02) evidences the alternative inner posture most directly: the wealthy person who does not develop hupsēlofroneō (CHAR-5) is one who places hope in God, is ready to give generously and share, and stores up treasure for the future. The alternative inner state is generous, God-directed stewardship — using received structural goods in service of others rather than as the ground for self-exaltation.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The alternative inner states described across the five are remarkably consistent: each names a posture of received-goods-acknowledged and God-directed orientation. CHAR-1's alternative is Psa 131:1 (M08-A1-VCG-03): heart not lifted, eyes not raised — deliberate creaturely lowering. CHAR-2's alternative is the servant who prays against presumptuous sins (Psa 19:13, M08-B-VCG-02): the humble servant who seeks divine restraint. CHAR-3's alternative is Gal 6:14 (M08-C-VCG-02): the world crucified to the self, all worldly boasting-grounds evacuated. CHAR-4's alternative is sober judgment within God-given measure (Rom 12:3, M08-D-VCG-02) and love-directed engagement with knowledge. CHAR-5's alternative is generous stewardship with hope in God (1Ti 6:17–18, M08-E-VCG-02). The cluster-synthesis: the alternative inner state is the posture of the humble receiver — one who accepts their creaturely station, acknowledges God as the source of all goods, and directs the capacities they possess outward toward God and others rather than inward toward self-elevation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The corpus describes this across several negative instances. 2Th1:8 — those who "do not obey the gospel" are in a state of "not knowing God" — relational rupture at the deepest level, with catastrophic eschatological consequence. 2Th3:14 — the one who refuses to obey apostolic instruction reveals "an inner refusal" that the communal response is designed to awaken to repentance — the blocking state is refusal, not merely ignorance. Pro30:17 — the eye that scorns to obey a mother is in a state of contemptuous dismissal of legitimate authority — a moral condition the text marks with severe consequence. The inner state of the non-receiver is consistent: some form of self-assertion or inner refusal that places the person's own judgment or desire above the legitimate authority's claim.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The two-verse corpus does not directly name the inner state of the person who encounters the occasion for contrition but does not enter it. The evidence describes those who are contrite (the recipients of God's nearness and reviving) without describing those who refuse contrition. The structural implication is hardness, self-sufficiency, or unrepentance — but this is inferred from the contrast structure rather than directly evidenced in §3.B.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The two-verse corpus does not directly describe the inner state of the person who fails to receive or embody this characteristic. The structural opposites (severity, hesitation) are implied but not described as inner states of specific persons.

**[CHAR-5]** S — The three-verse corpus does not directly describe the inner state of the person who encounters semnotēs but does not receive or embody it. The evidence describes the characteristic in those who have it rather than those who lack it.

**[CHAR-6]** S — The corpus does not directly name the inner state of the person who encounters the occasion for willing-heartedness but whose heart is not willing. Exo35:5 implies that some in the community are not of a willing heart (only "whoever is of a willing heart" is called to bring) but does not describe those whose hearts are not willing. Psa51:12 indirectly names the unwilling-spirit state as the condition requiring divine restoration — but this is specifically post-failure, not a general description of the non-willing person.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The corpus describes this state across the negative instances. The non-humbling person is in a condition of *increasing guilt* (2Ch33:23 — Amon), *inner rootedness in evil* (2Ch36:12 — Zedekiah's refusal as the root of his evil), and *self-enclosure against God's word* (2Ch36:12 — refusing to humble before the prophet who spoke from God's mouth). The Phili2:3 contrast frames the non-humbling person as ruled by "selfish ambition and conceit" — cognitive self-assertion rather than other-regard. The Colossian material (Col2:18) identifies the distorted inner state as being "puffed up without reason by his sensuous mind" — an inflated inner condition that mistakes performance for transformation. The inner-being state of the non-receiver is thus pride-in-operation: self-enclosed, self-elevating, resistant to both divine address and genuine other-regard.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The non-receiving person is most directly described for CHAR-1 (pride-in-operation: self-enclosed, self-elevating, resistant to divine address) and CHAR-2 (inner refusal: some form of self-assertion placing personal judgment over legitimate authority's claim). The other four characteristics are largely silent on this at the verse level — they describe givers and receivers who are present and responsive rather than those who encounter the characteristic and remain closed. The cluster-level inference: the silence on non-receiving states in CHAR-3 through CHAR-6 is consistent with the cluster's orientation toward those who are genuinely present and open. M09's evidence is weighted toward the person who has or is forming the characteristic; the anatomy of the hardened, resistant person who encounters M09 and refuses it is described most fully only in M09's structural opposite (M08 Pride and its distortions). The cluster effectively defers the detailed anatomy of non-reception to M08's evidence register.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The person who encounters the temptation to sin but does not — the character of the sinning-resisted state — is evidenced in several portraits. Joseph in Gen 39:9: the temptation is present; the inner state is one of named moral clarity ("How then can I do this great wickedness?") and upward reference (God's claim). Job in Job 1:22 and 2:10: under devastating suffering, Job's inner state is one of sustained moral restraint — conscience-active control even under pressure. Nehemiah in Neh 6:13: the trap is set; his inner state involves recognising the mechanism ("for this purpose he was hired") and refusing to yield. The common feature is that the non-sinning person retains full moral agency, with the will actively engaged in the decision not to sin rather than simply being unaware of the choice. The inner-being state is one of conscious, conscience-engaged refusal.

**[CHAR-10]** S — The corpus does not directly evidence the inner-being state of the person who resists enticement, hypocrisy, or apostasy. Gal 2:11's Paul (confronting Peter rather than joining the hypocrisy) is the implicit positive exemplar, but his inner state during the confrontation is not described in the 5-verse corpus.

**[CHAR-11]** E — Rom 6:22 — "you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life" — the freed person is: no longer under sin's dominion, now under God's authority (slave of God), producing the fruit of sanctification, and oriented toward eternal life. Rom 6:18 — "having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness" — the freed person's inner allegiance has been relocated from sin to righteousness. The inner state is not the absence of sin's presence but the absence of sin's dominion: Rom 6:11 — "dead to sin and alive to God" — the condition persists as a reality to reckon oneself dead to, not as a master with living authority over the person.

**[CHAR-12]** E — 1Jo 3:9 and 1Jo 5:18 together describe the liberated inner-being state. (1) *Born of God*: a constitutional state of divine birth that has transformed the inner person's relationship to sin; (2) *God's seed abiding*: an indwelling divine principle that constitutionally prevents habitual sinning from taking hold; (3) *Protected by Christ*: an external protective guardianship that bars the evil one's touch. The liberated state is thus: constitutionally new (born of God), internally reinforced (God's seed abiding), and externally protected (Christ's guardianship). This is not a self-generated freedom but a God-given, Christ-protected liberation.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Jer 16:10 — the people under judgment ask "What is our iniquity? What is the sin that we have committed against the Lord our God?" — the non-receiving state is incomprehension: the record is there (God sees it; judgment has come) but the person cannot identify it in themselves. Isa 3:9 — "they proclaim their sin like Sodom; they do not hide it" — the alternative non-receiving state: the record has produced such conscience-deadness that the person exhibits their sin publicly without awareness of its gravity. Both states involve a failure of the inner conscience to correctly interpret the moral reality of the record before God.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Mar 3:29 — "guilty of an eternal sin" — the person guilty of the eternal sin is in a state of permanent unresolved guilt before God; the seeking cannot break through the condition. For the broader case (seeking without receiving), the corpus is largely silent: the pattern evidenced is that genuine seeking (repentance + faith — Act 2:38/10:43) produces reception. The case of seeking without receiving is not directly evidenced beyond the eternal-sin exception of Mar 3:29.

**[CHAR-15]** S — The corpus does not describe the inner-being state of the individual within the community who recognises the generational sin-pattern but stands apart from it. Isa 43:27 names the first father's sin; Eze 37:23 names the promise to cleanse; neither describes the inner experience of the individual who breaks the pattern within their generation.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Amo 9:10 names the resistant state: "who say, 'Disaster shall not overtake or meet us'" — the inner state is confident self-deception about the consequences of the sinner-identity. Joh 9:24/25 — the Pharisees who declare Jesus "a sinner" with certainty while the healed man refuses the label — the resisters are in a state of inverted moral judgement: applying the sinner-label to the holy and denying it to themselves. The inner state of resistance is thus characterised by moral inversion: others are sinners; the self is not.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Eze 21:23/24 — "they have sworn solemn oaths, but he brings their guilt to remembrance" — the person who suppresses guilt-acknowledgment exists in a state of false oath-confidence that is overridden by God's recall of the guilt-record; Amo 9:10 (CHAR-16 context) — "disaster shall not overtake or meet us" — the guilt-denier's inner state is presumptuous self-assurance. Jer 2:22 names the guilt-denier's activity: attempting self-cleansing while the stain remains before God. The inner state of guilt-refusal is thus false confidence sustained against an objective guilt-reality that God sees and will eventually expose.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Hos 12:8 names it: "I am rich... they cannot find in me iniquity" — the inner state is wealthy self-sufficiency generating false moral confidence. Psa 36:2 — "flatters himself in his own eyes" — the inner state is proud self-deception. Job 31:33 — "if I have concealed my transgressions... by hiding my iniquity in my heart" — the alternative to honest disclosure is conscious inner concealment; the person knows the iniquity but buries it deliberately. The denier's inner state thus has two forms: unconscious self-deception (Psa 36:2 — cannot see or hate the iniquity) and conscious concealment (Job 31:33 — hiding it in the heart).

**[CHAR-19]** E — Isa 1:5 names it comprehensively: "why will you still be struck down? Why will you continue to rebel? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint" — the persistent transgressor's inner state is one of comprehensive moral-spiritual illness in both cognitive (head) and volitional (heart) faculties. Jer 2:29 — "why do you contend with me? You have all transgressed against me" — the inner state is self-righteous contention against God despite guilt. The persistent transgressor's inner state is thus a combination of structural inner deterioration (Isa 1:5 — head and heart incapacitated) and self-justifying posture (Jer 2:29) that produces inability to stand in God's right ways (Hos 14:9 — stumbling).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The question requires reframing for CHAR-2: unintentional sinning is not "received" from outside but committed. The more relevant question for this characteristic is: what is the inner-being state of the person who *fails to respond* when unintentional sinning surfaces to awareness — who does not confess or seek remedy? The corpus does not directly evidence this failure mode within CHAR-2's 18 verses. By implication, the person who suppresses awareness after the sin surfaces moves from CHAR-2 into CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression) territory. The CHAR-2 corpus presupposes a response; the absence of response is not evidenced here but is implicitly the boundary marker beyond which CHAR-2 ends.

**[CHAR-20]** E — 2Ch 28:22 names it most precisely: "in the time of his distress he became yet more faithless to the Lord — this same King Ahaz" — the inner state is a will that has become constitutively oriented away from God such that the very pressure that would normally drive a person toward God drives this person further from him. Pro 11:6 — "the treacherous are taken captive by their lust" — the inner state under sustained faithlessness is captivity to the will's own craving; the person is not free to turn toward God because the lust has assumed agentive control. The hardened-under-distress state of 2Ch 28:22 is CHAR-20's most extreme dispositional portrait.

**[CHAR-21]** E — 2Pe 2:12 names it most vividly: "like irrational animals, creatures of instinct, born to be caught and destroyed... will also be destroyed in their destruction" — the inner state is animal-instinctual operating without reason, heading toward destruction that matches their nature. 1Ti 6:5 — "depraved in mind and deprived of the truth" — the inner state lacks the basic cognitive capacity to access truth. Jude 10 — destroyed by what they understand instinctively — the instinct has replaced moral reasoning as the inner governing faculty. The characterised inner state is: reason and moral faculty replaced by unreflective instinct, enslaved to the corruption that will ultimately destroy the self.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Zep 3:5 names it with the greatest diagnostic precision: "the unjust knows no shame" — the inner-being state is one of complete insensibility to the moral wrongness of their own conduct. Job 15:16 fills out the appetite-dimension: "a man who drinks injustice like water" — the person's deepest craving is for what wrongs others; the inner orientation is appetitive toward harm. Psa 53:1 names the cognitive-theological foundation: "There is no God" in the heart — the inner denial of divine accountability is the cognitive substructure of the shameless, water-drinking injustice.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The corpus does not directly evidence the non-confessing person's inner state within CHAR-3's 34 verses (this belongs primarily to CHAR-4 — Conscience suppression). However, VCG-03 (Deu 1:41) and the Pharaoh pattern (Exo 9:27/10:16 — confesses under pressure, hardens when pressure lifts) evidence the *partial* version: the person who produces the verbal form but whose inner state remains unchanged. This partial state is characterised by: the conscience may have registered (enough to produce the words) but the will has not been reoriented. The full non-confessing person (who would not even produce the words) is outside this corpus's scope — their state belongs to CHAR-4.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The 8-verse corpus does not directly evidence this scenario — the persons exhibiting conscience suppression in the corpus are not described as encountering and then refusing to resolve it (that would be closer to CHAR-5 — Refusal to repent). The corpus describes conscience suppression as an *already-settled* inner condition: Jer 2:35 (already claiming innocence), Jer 16:10 (already failing to recognise), Ecc 8:12 (already sinning a hundred times), Tit 3:11 (already warped). The inner-being state of the person within conscience suppression is: moral self-perception that does not accurately register one's own sinfulness — a state characterised by false peace (Jer 2:35 — "his anger has turned from me") or genuine puzzlement (Jer 16:10 — "what sin?").

**[CHAR-5]** E — The corpus evidences the turning person most directly through Eze 33:12 — "the wickedness of the wicked, he shall not fall by it when he turns from his wickedness" — the turning person is the one whose prior wickedness does not condemn them because the will has moved. The turning person's inner state is the opposite of "did not depart" — it is active departure, movement, change of direction. The corpus (18 verses all describing refusal) does not portrait the inner state of the turning person extensively, but Eze 33:12's "turns from his wickedness" is the positive counter-portrait: the will that moves in the direction of departure.

**[CHAR-6]** E — 1Jo 3:6 provides the clearest evidence: the person who "abides in him" is the one who does not keep on sinning — the inner-being state is one of *sustained relational union with Christ* that structurally prevents the habitual pattern. Ecc 7:26 — "he who pleases God escapes her" — the inner-being state is one of active God-pleasing orientation, which provides the dispositional resource for escaping the snare that traps the sinner. The positive inner-being state is thus: abiding in Christ (1Jo 3:6), pleasing God (Ecc 7:26), and responsive hearing (the opposite of 1Sa 2:25) — all of which represent an active God-oriented inner constitution that prevents the sinning pattern from becoming habitual.

**[CHAR-7]** S — The corpus does not evidence the inner-being state of a community member who resists the leader's transmitted sinning direction. The corpus shows compliance (dominant Kings pattern) and structural reversal (Josiah). The individual community member who privately maintains their God-orientation while the leader transmits the sinning direction is not addressed in the 19-verse corpus. This is a gap in the evidence.

**[CHAR-8]** S — The corpus does not describe the inner-being state of communities that maintain submission to governing authority. The corpus is entirely focused on the revolting parties; the non-revolting community's inner state is not addressed.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Jude 9 and 2Pe 2:11 provide the clearest evidence: Michael and the angels do not pronounce blasphemous judgments even in contexts where they might seem warranted. The inner-being state of the non-blasphemer is: creaturely deference — "The Lord rebuke you" (Jude 9) — acknowledging that some pronouncements exceed creaturely authority and belong to God alone. The non-blasphemer's inner state is defined by the recognition of their own creaturely limits in speech.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The person who encounters the wicked but does not adopt the characteristic maintains deliberate moral separation and inner integrity. Psa 26:5 (VCG-03) is the clearest evidence: "I hate the assembly of evildoers, and I will not sit with the wicked" — the maintenance of moral separation requires an active internal stance of refusal. Psa 1:1 (VCG-04) describes the blessed person as defined by what they refuse to enter. The wicked's social-corrosive power (Num 16:26 — VCG-04 — "proximity risks being swept away") indicates that the person who does not receive the characteristic must actively distance; the inner state is one of maintained integrity against a contagious force. 2Ch 19:2 (VCG-03) warns that helping the wicked even without adopting their wickedness draws divine displeasure — the inner state of the non-receiver must include practical separation, not merely internal distinction.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The person who encounters evil as constitutional inner nature in another but does not absorb it maintains a posture of active moral abhorrence and protective separation. Rom 12:9 (vc=14417 — VCG-06): the commanded inner state is "abhorrence" of evil combined with holding fast to the good — the non-receiver's inner state is one of active moral revulsion maintained as a deliberate orientation. 1Cor 5:13 (vc=14465 — VCG-04): the community that expels the evil person is the community whose own constitutional condition is healthy enough to recognise and reject the invasive one. 1Cor 14:20 (vc=14364 — VCG-05): "be infants in evil" — the non-receiver is characterised by moral inexperience in the domain of evil — an inner state of preserved moral simplicity in this domain.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The person who encounters abominable conditions (in others or as an inner temptation) and does not receive them maintains a state of active moral revulsion and grief. Eze 9:4 (vc=1698 — VCG-04): those who "sigh and groan over all the abominations committed in it" — the inner state is one of conscience-driven grief that mirrors the divine revulsion. Pro 29:27 (vc=65959 — VCG-01): "an unjust man is an abomination to the righteous" — the righteous person's inner response to the abominable is moral revulsion. This is the functionally conscience-alive person: their inner moral faculty identifies the abominable, recoils from it in grief or revulsion, and marks them as distinct from those who commit it without response. The non-receiving state is one of inner moral perceptiveness and affective-moral recoil.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The non-receiving person maintains a state of active moral revulsion and decisive removal. 2Ch 15:8 (vc=65902 — VCG-03): Asa "took courage and put away the detestable idols" — courage and decisive action characterise the non-receiver. 2Ki 23:24 (vc=65901 — VCG-03): Josiah's comprehensive purge — the non-receiving community leader actively removes every form of the characteristic. The inner state is one of covenant loyalty that finds idolatrous abomination repugnant (mirroring the divine revulsion) and is moved to decisive corrective action. This mirrors Eze 9:4 (from CHAR-3's corpus) — the grieving conscience that marks the person for protection by refusing to participate.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The non-receiving person maintains a state of active rejection and volitional distance from iniquity. Psa 101:8 (vc=38226 — VCG-03): the royal psalmist "morning by morning will destroy all the wicked in the land, cutting off all the evildoers" — the non-receiver is actively engaged in removing the characteristic from the communal space. Psa 141:9 (vc=38231 — VCG-03): prayer for protection from evildoers' snares — the non-receiver maintains a state of watchful protection. Job 11:14 (vc=38207 — VCG-04): "if iniquity is in your hand, put it far away" — the non-receiver is one who has actively distanced themselves from held iniquity. The inner state of non-reception is characterised by active rejection, volitional distancing, and the willingness to call on the Lord (contrasted with evildoers who "do not call upon the Lord" — Psa 14:4 — VCG-03).

**[CHAR-6]** E — The non-receiving person (the one who does not generate evil speech when provoked) maintains: (1) non-retaliatory inner orientation — 1Cor 4:13 (vc=14351 — VCG-02): "when slandered, we entreat" — the inner state is one of constrained, non-retaliatory appeal rather than counter-blast; (2) good conscience — 1Pe 3:16 (vc=14380 — VCG-03): "having a good conscience, so that when you are slandered, those who revile your good behavior in Christ may be put to shame" — the inner integrity of good conscience is the foundation of the non-receiving state; (3) honourable-conduct orientation — 1Pe 2:12 (vc=14377 — VCG-03): the non-receiver lives honorably, producing good deeds that eventually silence the false accusation. The inner state of non-reception is: good conscience + non-retaliatory entreaty + honourable conduct orientation.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals a consistent positive inner-state for the non-receiver: the person who encounters M10b evil but does not receive it is consistently characterised by (a) active grief and moral revulsion (Char 3: Eze 9:4 — sighing and groaning over abominations; the conscience alive to the evil's weight), (b) non-retaliatory inner resilience (Char 6: 1Cor 4:13 — when slandered, we entreat; 1Pe 3:16 — good conscience maintained amid slander), and (c) maintained covenant fidelity (Char 4: 2Ch 34:33 — Josiah's sustained devotion to the Lord after purging abominations). The cluster's non-receiver profile is: conscience alive and responding with grief (not passive indifference), will non-retaliatory and sustained toward good (not reactive escalation), and active volitional distance from the characteristic (all six — the person who recognises and rejects what they encounter). The non-receiver is not merely passive — they are characterised by active moral engagement with what they decline to receive.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The person who is in the defilement-state but does not respond appropriately is characterised by two inner conditions. If the failure is ignorance, the person remains in an unresolved defilement — the guilt is real but inactive; the state persists (Num 19:13 — "his uncleanness is still on him"). If the failure is willful non-cleansing, the person is in a condition of deliberate sacral defection: Num 19:20 names this as "defiling the sanctuary of the Lord" — the will's refusal of remedy becomes an act of corporate sacral harm. The inner state of the willful refuser is one of hardened will operating against the sacral order, which the evidence treats as the most serious form of the characteristic's failure mode.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The person who does not receive the moral-inner defilement-state is characterised in VCG-05 (Rev 3:4, Rev 14:4, Isa 35:8). Rev 3:4 (VCG-05): "people who have not soiled their garments... they are worthy" — their inner state is one of maintained integrity; the moral condition is uncompromised. Rev 14:4 (VCG-05): "they have not defiled themselves... they follow the Lamb wherever he goes" — their inner state is one of total consecration to Christ, actively oriented toward the Lamb rather than toward corrupted desire. The non-reception state is not passive neutrality but an active positive orientation: consecrated following, maintained integrity, worthiness for divine fellowship.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The person who does not receive the corporate/covenantal defilement-state is characterised in the positive-inverse at multiple points. Eze 4:14 (VCG-05): the prophet's declaration — "I have never defiled myself. From my youth up till now I have never eaten what died of itself" — shows the inner state as lifelong personal maintenance of covenantal integrity; the conscience actively defending the inner person's maintained purity. Eze 18:6/15 (VCG-01): the righteous man "does not defile his neighbor's wife" across generations — the inner state is will's consistent covenantal fidelity. The positive-inverse state is thus: a will committed to covenantal faithfulness, a conscience that actively defends maintained purity, and an institutional vocation of teaching the clean/unclean distinction.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 21-verse corpus does not describe a person whom the spirits attempt to possess but fail to. The structural resistance is authoritative divine power (VCG-03), not inner-being conditioning in the potential recipient. The evidence suggests that the characteristic's reception is entirely determined by the spirit's agency rather than by the recipient's inner resistance.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The positive-inverse state profiles collectively reveal the cluster's positive vision of the undefiled person. Characteristic 1: active sacral vigilance — the person who does not incur the defilement is one whose will actively avoids defiling contacts; the undefiled state is maintained through watchful discipline (Lev 11:43-44). Characteristic 2: active positive orientation (VCG-05) — Rev 3:4 ("people who have not soiled their garments... worthy"); Rev 14:4 ("they have not defiled themselves... they follow the Lamb") — the non-defilement state is not passive neutrality but consecrated following. Characteristic 3: lifelong maintained covenantal integrity (Eze 4:14 — "I have never defiled myself... from my youth up"), will's consistent covenantal fidelity (Eze 18:6/15 — "does not defile his neighbor's wife"), and institutional vocation of teaching the clean/unclean distinction (Eze 44:23). Characteristic 4: not evidenced — the 21-verse corpus does not describe a person whom the spirits attempt to possess but fail to (the resistance is in divine authority, not in the person's inner state). Cluster pattern: the undefiled state in Characteristics 1, 2, and 3 is characterised by active positive orientation (sacral vigilance, consecrated following of the Lamb, covenantal fidelity) — not passive neutrality. Characteristic 4 cannot describe the undefiled state in this way, confirming that its characteristic is the only one where the person's own inner condition does not determine reception.
